questions.q: An AI model is being retrained on new data after detected drift. Before the retrained model replaces the current production model, what must happen?
opts: The retrained model must pass the same evaluation criteria as the original before it replaces the production model
The data science team must document the specific drift patterns detected before the retrained model is promoted
The compliance team must review the new training data to confirm no new data governance issues were introduced
The project sponsor must formally approve the retraining since it constitutes a model update
questions.explain: A retrained model is a new model version — it must pass the same evaluation gates (accuracy, bias testing, fairness metrics, business success criteria) as the original before replacing the production model. Retraining to address drift and then deploying without re-evaluation risks trading one performance problem for another. Sponsor approval, documentation, and compliance review are supplementary steps.

questions.q: The model monitoring dashboard shows prediction volume dropped by 60% unexpectedly last Tuesday. Performance metrics for predictions made appear normal. What should the project manager investigate FIRST?
opts: Whether users manually bypassed the AI model for 60% of decisions due to a loss of confidence
Whether the monitoring system itself is experiencing data collection issues that underreport actual prediction volume
Whether a data drift event occurred last Tuesday that caused the model to reject 60% of incoming inputs
Whether an upstream system failure, API change, or integration error reduced the volume of inputs reaching the model
questions.explain: A sudden 60% volume drop with stable per-prediction performance is more consistent with an upstream integration problem — a source system not sending data, an API change breaking the connection, or a pipeline failure — than with drift, user behavior, or monitoring issues. Drift typically degrades performance, not volume. The investigation starts with the data pipeline feeding the model.

questions.q: The project manager is designing a deployment plan for an AI model that will replace a high-stakes manual underwriting process. Which deployment approach BEST manages risk?
opts: Shadow deployment — AI runs in background without affecting decisions while the manual process continues
Full cutover — replace the manual process immediately to realize the efficiency gains quickly
Parallel run — operate AI alongside manual underwriting for a period, comparing outputs before full cutover
Staged rollout — deploy to a pilot business unit first, evaluate outcomes, then expand to all units
questions.explain: For a high-stakes process, a staged rollout (start with a pilot unit, evaluate outcomes, expand based on evidence) provides the best risk management while delivering real operational value. A parallel run also works but requires more resources. Shadow deployment doesn't generate real-world outcome feedback. Full cutover for a high-stakes manual process with no parallel validation is too risky.

questions.q: A regulatory change requires that all AI models used in financial decisions include an explanation mechanism for all affected consumers. The project manager discovers the current model cannot generate explanations. What is the MOST appropriate action?
opts: Continue operating while building explanatory capability in parallel over the next year
Immediately assess whether the regulation requires a compliance date and develop a remediation plan to meet it
Add a general disclosure statement that AI was used in the decision as a temporary compliance measure
Petition the regulator for an exemption based on the model's high accuracy and established business value
questions.explain: Regulatory compliance has a defined timeline — the first question is when compliance is required, then planning remediation to meet that date. Operating without compliance while building in parallel only works if the regulatory timeline permits it. General disclosure doesn't satisfy an explanation requirement. Seeking exemptions before assessing requirements inverts the process.

questions.q: A model serving infrastructure upgrade is planned. The operations team wants to use a blue-green deployment approach. The project manager should ensure this approach includes:
opts: A model performance validation on the new infrastructure before shifting live traffic, and a rollback plan if issues emerge
Approval from the data science team confirming the model will perform identically on the new infrastructure
Communication to all end users that a brief service interruption is planned during the infrastructure cutover
A cost analysis confirming the blue-green infrastructure cost is within the operational budget
questions.explain: Blue-green deployment for model infrastructure must include validation that the model performs identically on the new environment before live traffic is shifted — infrastructure differences can subtly change model behavior or latency. A rollback plan must exist in case issues emerge after traffic shift. Budget approval, data science sign-off, and user communication are secondary requirements.

questions.q: A project manager is establishing the handoff from the project team to the operations team for a deployed AI model. What is the MOST critical element to include in the handoff package?
opts: Project financial documentation showing all development costs and projected operational ROI
Meeting notes from all Phase I through Phase V project team retrospectives and lessons learned sessions
Complete source code for all model development experiments run during Phase III and Phase IV
Model card, monitoring plan, retraining procedure, incident response playbook, and escalation contacts
questions.explain: The operations team needs to manage the model without the project team's ongoing involvement. The critical package: model card (what the model does, its limitations, intended use), monitoring plan (what to watch), retraining procedure (when and how to retrain), incident response playbook (what to do when things go wrong), and escalation contacts. Source code, financials, and retrospectives serve other purposes.

questions.q: A post-deployment review shows the AI model delivered 40% of the ROI projected in Phase I. The gap is not due to technical failure. What should the project manager investigate?
opts: Whether a competitor deployed a similar model that has reduced the addressable value opportunity
Whether the model's accuracy has degraded since deployment, reducing its prediction quality
Whether the Phase I ROI assumptions about adoption rates, use case frequency, or value per prediction were inaccurate
Whether the MLOps team implemented the monitoring incorrectly, causing underreporting of model impact
questions.explain: If the model works technically but ROI is 40% of projection, the Phase I ROI assumptions were likely wrong — adoption was lower than expected, the use case was less frequent than assumed, or the value per correct prediction was overestimated. CPMAI requires investigating the specific assumption that failed, not blaming technical performance, monitoring, or external competition without evidence.

questions.q: An AI model that recommends investment products is producing outputs that are accurate but the compliance officer notes they sometimes recommend products outside the customer's risk profile. What action is required?
opts: Add a compliance disclaimer to all investment recommendations produced by the AI model
Implement a rule-based constraint layer that filters AI recommendations to only products within each customer's defined risk profile
Retrain the model with additional training examples showing only in-profile product recommendations
Raise the issue with the product team to update product risk profile definitions to better match AI outputs
questions.explain: An AI recommending products outside a customer's risk profile is a regulatory compliance and customer harm issue requiring immediate remediation. A rule-based constraint layer that filters outputs to compliant products is the most immediate and reliable fix — it applies compliance rules deterministically on top of AI outputs. Disclaimers don't prevent harm. Retraining takes time. Changing risk profiles to match AI is backwards.

questions.q: After production deployment, the model's average prediction confidence drops gradually over six weeks without any obvious single-event cause. What does this MOST likely indicate?
opts: Gradual data drift — the real-world input distribution is slowly diverging from the training distribution
A configuration change in the scoring pipeline that altered how features are preprocessed before scoring
Increased diversity in incoming queries causing the model to encounter more out-of-distribution examples
A memory leak in the model serving infrastructure degrading compute performance over time
questions.explain: Gradual, smooth decline in confidence scores over weeks without a discrete event is the characteristic signature of data drift — real-world inputs are slowly moving away from the training distribution. Sudden drops suggest infrastructure or configuration changes. Gradual drift is the expected pattern when business conditions, user behavior, or market dynamics change over time.

questions.q: A deployed AI model produces a critical error affecting 500 customer accounts. The operations team wants to retrain the model immediately to fix the issue. What should the project manager do FIRST?
opts: Notify the governance board and affected customers before taking any technical corrective action
Conduct a root cause analysis of the error before deciding on the appropriate corrective action
Authorize immediate retraining to minimize the duration of incorrect predictions in production
Activate the rollback plan to revert to the previous stable model while the error is investigated
questions.explain: When a deployed AI model causes harm, the first action is harm containment — rolling back to the previous stable model stops the error from affecting more customers. Root cause investigation is important but comes after harm is contained. Retraining without understanding the error may reproduce it. Governance notification and customer communication are important but follow rollback, not precede it.

questions.q: A project manager is conducting a 90-day post-deployment review. Adoption is strong but the business team has begun using the model for a purpose outside its original intended use. What should the project manager do?
opts: Notify the data science team to begin training a new model specifically for the emerging use case
Support the expanded use since strong adoption demonstrates the model's value across multiple use cases
Assess whether the new use case falls within the model's validated scope and require a formal use case extension review if it does not
Document the expanded use as an organizational success story demonstrating AI value creation
questions.explain: Using an AI model for purposes outside its validated scope creates reliability, fairness, and governance risks — the model may not perform appropriately for the new use case, bias testing may not have been done for it, and governance accountability may be unclear. CPMAI requires formal assessment and, if needed, a use case extension review before expanded use is approved.

questions.q: The organization is scaling an AI model from one business unit to five. The original deployment had 2 stakeholder groups. The scaled deployment will have 15. What risk should the project manager flag?
opts: The model may not be technically accurate enough for the additional business units' use cases
Stakeholder management complexity increases significantly — communications, requirements gathering, and change management must be scaled accordingly
The model serving infrastructure may not scale to the additional prediction volume across five business units
The MLOps team may not have sufficient capacity to support five simultaneous model deployments
questions.explain: Scaling from 2 to 15 stakeholder groups multiplies the stakeholder management complexity — each group may have different requirements, workflow integrations, governance expectations, and adoption challenges. The project manager must flag this as a significant change management and communications planning challenge, not just a technical scaling problem.

questions.q: A deployed AI model's business owner asks the project manager to disable monitoring for two weeks during a major system migration to reduce operational complexity. What should the project manager advise?
opts: Advise against disabling monitoring and propose maintaining it at reduced scope during the migration if resources are constrained
Agree but require daily manual performance checks as a compensating control during the monitoring gap
Escalate to the governance board since disabling monitoring requires formal risk acceptance at the appropriate level
Agree since monitoring can be restored quickly after the migration is complete with minimal risk
questions.explain: Disabling monitoring exposes the organization to undetected model failures for two weeks — especially during a system migration when integration changes can cause unexpected model behavior. CPMAI advises against disabling monitoring and proposes an alternative: maintaining monitoring at reduced scope (core metrics only) during the migration. If full disabling is considered, it requires formal governance risk acceptance, not bilateral agreement.

questions.q: An AI model produces a recommendation that a user flags as clearly incorrect. The user bypasses the recommendation and the correct outcome results. What process should the project manager ensure captures this event?
opts: A customer service escalation process that compensates the user for the incorrect recommendation
A model performance report updated to reflect the reduction in accuracy caused by the error event
A bug report filed with the development team for root cause analysis and model debugging
A feedback loop process that captures user overrides with outcome data to inform model improvement and monitoring
questions.explain: User overrides with known correct outcomes are valuable training signal and model quality feedback. CPMAI Phase V requires a structured feedback loop that captures these events, documents the override rationale, and feeds outcome data back into the model improvement cycle. Bug reports, compensation processes, and accuracy reports don't create the systematic feedback mechanism CPMAI requires.

questions.q: A model's monitoring alerts fire at a high rate, causing alert fatigue — the operations team has started ignoring them. What is the MOST important corrective action?
opts: Implement an automated response system that handles low-severity alerts without human intervention
Reduce the total number of monitoring metrics tracked to lower the overall alert volume
Review and recalibrate alert thresholds to ensure alerts fire only for genuinely actionable situations requiring human response
Assign a dedicated operations staff member to review all alerts and filter false positives before distribution
questions.explain: Alert fatigue from poorly calibrated thresholds is a serious monitoring failure — when teams ignore alerts, critical failures go undetected. The root cause is almost always thresholds set too sensitively, firing alerts that aren't truly actionable. Recalibrating thresholds to ensure alerts require and deserve human response is the correct fix. Reducing metrics, adding staff, or automating responses don't fix threshold miscalibration.

sections.title: AI Project Management: Scenarios & Judgment
sections.description: Cross-domain PM · Stakeholder management · Risk · Change control · Communication · Team dynamics

questions.q: A data scientist on the team believes the AI solution will eliminate their job function over time. This belief is affecting their engagement and work quality. What should the project manager do?
opts: Reassure the data scientist that AI will not eliminate their role and ask them to refocus on deliverables
Address the concern directly, clarify the team member's evolving role in the AI-enabled environment, and involve them in shaping how AI augments their function
Escalate to HR since job anxiety is a personnel issue outside the project manager's scope
Replace the team member with someone more supportive of AI transformation to protect project quality
questions.explain: A team member's fear about their own job security is a legitimate concern requiring direct, honest engagement — not dismissal or escalation. CPMAI project managers acknowledge the concern, clarify how roles evolve in an AI-augmented environment, and involve the team member in shaping the solution. Dismissing, escalating, or replacing avoids the real issue and undermines team trust.

questions.q: The project manager is preparing a lessons learned document at project closure. What element would be MOST valuable for the organization's future AI projects?
opts: Documented insights on data quality issues, estimation accuracy, stakeholder engagement approaches, and governance decisions that affected outcomes
A technical specification of the final model architecture and development environment configuration
A competency assessment of each team member's performance during the project for HR reference
A financial summary showing actual costs versus Phase I estimates across all five CPMAI phases
questions.explain: The most organizationally valuable lessons learned address the recurring challenges in AI projects: data quality problems and how they were identified and resolved, estimation patterns (where AI projects consistently differ from initial plans), what stakeholder engagement approaches worked, and which governance decisions were effective. Technical specifications and financial summaries serve narrow audiences.

questions.q: A project manager is closing an AI project. The model has been handed over to operations but the project team still receives escalations from the business because operations hasn't fully taken ownership. What should the project manager do?
opts: Reopen the project to provide continued support since the handoff was evidently premature
Document the incomplete handoff as a lessons learned item and close the project as planned
Continue handling escalations until the business is comfortable with the operations team's support capability
Formally complete the project closure, establish a defined transition period with clear handoff milestones, and redirect escalations to operations
questions.explain: An incomplete operational handoff requires a formal, structured transition — not continued project team support or immediate hard closure. A defined transition period with specific handoff milestones (operations handles tier-1 escalations by date X, full support by date Y) and a clear redirect protocol gives operations the time to mature while ending the project team's ambiguous support role.

questions.q: An AI project is in Phase IV evaluation and is on track. The organization announces a merger that will expand the customer base by 300%. What Phase I activity should the project manager revisit?
opts: The vendor contracts since the expanded customer base will require renegotiating licensing agreements
The project timeline since the merger will likely delay regulatory approval for deployment
The business case and scope — the merger changes the population the model will serve and may require revalidating feasibility and success criteria
The team composition since the merger may provide access to additional data science talent
questions.explain: A 300% customer base expansion fundamentally changes the use case — the model was designed for the original population. Phase I feasibility must be revisited: is the training data representative of the expanded population, are the success metrics still appropriate at this scale, and are the ethical and bias assessments valid for new customer segments? The business case scope has materially changed.

questions.q: After deployment, the project manager receives feedback that a specific user group finds the AI model's interface confusing and consistently misinterprets outputs. What is the MOST important first step?
opts: Retrain the model to produce outputs that match the user group's existing mental models
Improve the output presentation, explanation format, and user training for that specific group before assuming the model needs to change
Commission a user research study to determine how the AI model should be redesigned for broader usability
Increase monitoring for that user group to detect whether their misinterpretation leads to downstream errors
questions.explain: Confusing interface and misinterpreted outputs are most likely a UX and training problem, not a model problem. The first step is improving how outputs are presented and explained to that user group, and providing better training before concluding the model itself needs retraining. Retraining is an expensive intervention that addresses the model, not the communication gap.

questions.q: A business stakeholder repeatedly requests features outside the project's defined scope, causing the data science team to spend time evaluating and declining requests. What should the project manager do?
opts: Establish a formal change request process and communicate it to the stakeholder so requests are properly evaluated and documented
Escalate the stakeholder behavior to their manager as a project interference issue
Accept the most reasonable out-of-scope requests to maintain positive stakeholder relationships
Ask the data science team to ignore out-of-scope requests and continue focusing on approved deliverables
questions.explain: Recurring out-of-scope requests require a formal change request process — this gives the stakeholder a proper channel (their requests are heard and evaluated), gives the project manager visibility into all requests, and prevents informal scope creep from consuming team capacity. Ignoring requests damages the relationship; escalating is premature; accepting without process creates ungoverned scope expansion.

questions.q: The project manager is asked to estimate the effort for building a new AI feature. The team has no prior experience with this specific AI technique. What is the BEST estimation approach?
opts: Apply a 3x multiplier to the data science lead's initial estimate to account for AI project uncertainty
Defer the estimate until Phase II when data availability is confirmed and the technical approach is clearer
Use the average effort from similar features in the team's prior projects as the baseline estimate
Conduct a time-boxed spike experiment to gain actual experience with the technique before estimating
questions.explain: When the team has no experience with a specific AI technique, estimation without evidence is speculation. A time-boxed spike experiment — a short focused investigation — produces actual experience-based data to ground the estimate. Generic multipliers don't improve estimate quality. Prior project averages don't apply if the technique is different. Deferral delays the estimate without improving it.

questions.q: A project team member suggests that because the AI model makes thousands of decisions per day, occasional errors are statistically acceptable and don't require individual review. The project manager should:
opts: Disagree and implement manual review for every individual AI decision to eliminate harm from errors
Agree since statistical error tolerances are the appropriate standard for high-volume AI systems
Challenge this — individual errors may be acceptable statistically but still cause significant harm to the specific individuals affected, requiring a proportionate response process
Agree but establish a threshold below which individual errors are automatically closed without review
questions.explain: Statistical acceptability of error rates at scale does not eliminate the harm to individuals affected by each error. CPMAI's responsible AI principles require a proportionate response process — affected individuals need a way to report errors, have them reviewed, and be remediated. 'Statistically acceptable at scale' is not an ethical justification for having no individual recourse mechanism.

questions.q: A project team is highly technically skilled but has no experience with stakeholder management for AI projects. The project manager notices key business stakeholders are disengaged. What is the MOST appropriate action?
opts: Assign a business analyst to act as a translator between the technical team and business stakeholders
Develop and implement a stakeholder engagement plan that creates regular touchpoints and meaningful participation opportunities for business stakeholders
Reduce the frequency of business stakeholder meetings to allow the technical team to focus on development
Escalate stakeholder disengagement to the sponsor as a risk to project adoption
questions.explain: Stakeholder disengagement in an AI project threatens adoption and business alignment. The correct response is a structured stakeholder engagement plan — regular touchpoints, decision checkpoints that matter to business stakeholders, and participation opportunities that make engagement meaningful. A translator helps with communication but doesn't substitute for a genuine engagement strategy.

questions.q: Halfway through Phase III, the project manager discovers a new open-source AI library that would significantly improve model performance. Adding it would require refactoring 40% of the existing codebase. What should the project manager do?
opts: Evaluate the performance gain against the refactoring cost, risk, and timeline impact before making a recommendation
Defer the library to the next model iteration since mid-phase codebase changes are inherently too risky
Ask the data science team to implement the library in parallel and select whichever approach is ready first
Implement the library immediately since performance improvements are always worth the refactoring investment
questions.explain: A new library offering performance gains mid-phase requires trade-off analysis — how significant is the performance improvement, what is the refactoring cost, what is the timeline risk, and does the improvement materially affect business outcomes? Neither 'always worth it' nor 'always too risky' is the right default. CPMAI requires evidence-based evaluation before recommending course change.

questions.q: A project team is building an AI model for a use case that is similar to one that failed at the organization three years ago. What should the project manager do with this organizational history?
opts: Share the historical failure with the sponsor as context but proceed without letting past results affect the current approach
Assign the same team members who worked on the prior project to avoid repeating known mistakes
Treat the historical failure as irrelevant since three years have passed and technology has advanced significantly
Research the prior failure's root causes and specifically address them in the current project's risk management and feasibility assessment
questions.explain: Prior failures are organizational knowledge that should directly inform current project risk management. The project manager should research specifically why the prior project failed — data quality, stakeholder alignment, business case problems, or technical issues — and explicitly address those root causes in the current project's assessment and planning. Ignoring history or simply informing stakeholders without acting on it wastes the learning.

questions.q: An AI project team consists of data scientists, data engineers, and business analysts but does not include anyone with legal or compliance expertise. What risk should the project manager flag?
opts: The team's communication style may not meet the standards expected by executive stakeholders
The team lacks sufficient technical diversity to evaluate multiple algorithm approaches effectively
Legal and compliance gaps may cause the team to proceed with data use, model deployment, or automation that violates regulations
Without legal expertise, the team cannot protect intellectual property developed during the project
questions.explain: Missing legal and compliance expertise creates risk that the team will make data, modeling, or deployment decisions that violate regulations — without anyone to identify the violation. CPMAI requires cross-functional team composition to include the perspectives needed to identify all significant project risks, including legal and regulatory ones.

questions.q: A risk was identified in Phase I: 'The data required may not be available in sufficient volume.' Now in Phase III, the data shortage has materialized. What should the project manager have done differently?
opts: Escalated the risk immediately in Phase I rather than including it in the risk register
Defined risk response actions in Phase I and triggered those responses when early warning signs appeared in Phase II
Deferred the project until the data shortage risk was fully resolved before committing to any further phases
Added the risk to the steering committee report in Phase I to transfer ownership to the governance board
questions.explain: Identifying a risk in Phase I creates an obligation to define response actions — not just document it. The project manager should have planned risk responses in Phase I (e.g., alternative data sources, scope adjustment, data augmentation strategies) and monitored for early warning signals during Phase II. Risk register documentation without response planning is incomplete risk management.

questions.q: The project's AI governance board has not met in three months due to scheduling conflicts, causing decisions to accumulate. What should the project manager do?
opts: Escalate the governance gap to executive leadership and propose alternative decision mechanisms to clear the backlog
Defer all pending decisions until the governance board reconvenes and accept the resulting project delays
Identify which decisions are within the project manager's authority and make those, escalating only the highest-risk items
Make the pending decisions independently to maintain project momentum during the governance gap
questions.explain: A three-month governance gap with accumulated decisions is a systemic problem requiring escalation to executive leadership. The governance board needs either a meeting to clear the backlog or an interim decision mechanism. Making decisions independently beyond the PM's authority, deferring indefinitely, or selectively escalating are all inadequate responses to a governance process breakdown.

questions.q: A project manager realizes the AI project's success has created organizational dependency: the business cannot operate without the model if it fails. What governance control should be recommended?
opts: Document the dependency in the model card and monitor for any performance degradation that might affect business continuity
Commission a second identical AI model as a hot standby to eliminate the single point of failure risk
Develop a manual fallback procedure that the business can execute if the AI model becomes unavailable
Retrain the model more frequently to reduce the probability of performance failure causing business disruption
questions.explain: Critical business dependency on an AI model requires a manual fallback procedure — a defined process the business can execute if the model is unavailable due to failures, maintenance, or unexpected drift. More frequent retraining, documentation, and redundant models address different risks. A manual fallback addresses the unavailability scenario that creates the dependency risk.

questions.q: A project manager is managing an AI project where the data science team consistently underestimates experiment iteration times. After four sprints, actual time is 2.3x the estimates. What should the project manager do?
opts: Accept the estimation variance as inherent to AI project uncertainty and rebaseline the schedule accordingly
Apply a 2.3x correction factor to all future estimates automatically and update the project plan accordingly
Facilitate a team retrospective to understand why estimation is off and collaboratively improve estimation accuracy
Escalate to the sponsor that the team's estimation quality is causing project delays
questions.explain: Systematic 2.3x estimation error requires investigation — why are estimates consistently off? Is it undiscovered complexity, scope creep within iterations, or methodology issues? A team retrospective to diagnose and improve estimation is the correct CPMAI response. Applying a correction factor without understanding the cause perpetuates the problem. Escalating without improvement planning is premature.

questions.q: The project sponsor asks the project manager for weekly AI performance updates but the model monitoring system only produces meaningful data on a monthly basis. What should the project manager communicate?
opts: Provide weekly updates using daily manual samples since the sponsor's expectation must be met
Explain the monitoring system's data cadence and propose what meaningful weekly indicators can be shared versus what requires monthly review
Decline weekly updates entirely since providing them would mislead the sponsor with incomplete data
Change the monitoring system to produce weekly data to meet the sponsor's reporting needs
questions.explain: The project manager should explain what can meaningfully be reported weekly (deployment health, incident count, user adoption) versus what requires monthly aggregation (model performance metrics). Providing misleading weekly AI performance metrics is worse than no report. Declining entirely fails the stakeholder. Changing the monitoring system for reporting cadence alone may be unnecessary overhead.

questions.q: A senior data scientist disagrees with the project manager's Phase II data quality go/no-go decision. The data scientist believes the data is good enough to proceed. What should the project manager do?
opts: Defer to the data scientist since they have greater technical expertise to evaluate data quality
Document both perspectives, present the disagreement with evidence to the steering committee, and let the committee decide
Compromise by proceeding to Phase III with the understanding that data issues will be addressed during development
Override the data scientist since the project manager has final authority on phase gate decisions
questions.explain: A substantive disagreement between the project manager's governance assessment and a senior technical expert's recommendation should be escalated to the steering committee with both perspectives documented. Neither party should unilaterally override the other. Compromise by proceeding with known quality issues is not a sound governance decision — it defers the problem to a more expensive phase.

questions.q: A project manager learns that the organization is planning to use the AI model's outputs to train a new AI model without the knowledge of the customers whose data was used. What should the project manager flag?
opts: Whether the data science team has capacity to support both the current model and a new model development effort
Whether the new model would create competitive risks if the approach became known to market competitors
Whether the new AI model will be technically compatible with the existing data infrastructure
Whether using model outputs to train a new model complies with the original data consent under which customer data was collected
questions.explain: Using AI model outputs derived from customer data to train a new model may constitute secondary use of personal data beyond what customers consented to. CPMAI's responsible AI principles require evaluating consent compliance for all downstream uses of data — including derived outputs. Technical compatibility, team capacity, and competitive risk are secondary to the consent and legal use question.

questions.q: An AI project is 70% complete when a key data scientist resigns unexpectedly. What should the project manager do FIRST?
opts: Pause all development work until a replacement is hired to prevent knowledge gaps from causing errors
Immediately begin recruiting a replacement data scientist before assessing the full impact of the departure
Assess the knowledge transfer risk — what critical knowledge the departing data scientist holds and whether it is documented
Notify the project sponsor of the departure and request emergency budget for a replacement hire
questions.explain: The immediate risk from a key departure is undocumented knowledge — if the data scientist holds undocumented understanding of data decisions, model architecture choices, or experiment results, that knowledge leaves with them. The first action is assessing what they know that isn't documented and capturing it before they leave. Recruiting, notifying sponsors, and pausing work are important but secondary to knowledge preservation.

sections.title: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML (20%)
sections.description: AI/ML concepts · Use cases · Learning types · Data types · ML lifecycle · AWS services

questions.q: A company needs to detect text in images of scanned invoices and extract structured information. Which combination of AWS services is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Rekognition for image analysis followed by Amazon Comprehend for entity extraction
Amazon Textract for document text extraction followed by Amazon Comprehend for NLP analysis
Amazon Transcribe for audio-to-text followed by Amazon Lex for intent recognition
Amazon Polly for text synthesis followed by Amazon Kendra for document search
questions.explain: Amazon Textract is designed specifically for extracting text and structured data from documents and images — including invoices, forms, and tables. Comprehend then analyzes the extracted text for entities, key information, and relationships. Rekognition is for general image analysis/labeling, not document text extraction.

questions.q: Which component of the ML lifecycle is responsible for transforming raw data into model-ready inputs?
opts: Feature engineering — creating and transforming input variables from raw data
Hyperparameter tuning — optimizing model configuration settings
Model deployment — making the trained model available for inference
Model evaluation — assessing performance on held-out test data
questions.explain: Feature engineering transforms raw data into model-ready inputs — normalizing values, encoding categorical variables, creating interaction terms, handling missing data. Model evaluation tests performance. Hyperparameter tuning optimizes model configuration. Deployment serves the trained model for inference.

questions.q: An ML model consistently predicts higher loan approval rates for one demographic group compared to another with identical financial profiles. What is this an example of?
opts: Bias — the model produces systematically unfair outcomes for specific demographic groups
Underfitting — the model is too simple to capture the true relationship in the data
Variance — the model's predictions are highly sensitive to small changes in input data
Overfitting — the model has memorized demographic patterns from the training data
questions.explain: Systematic unfair outcomes correlated with demographic characteristics is AI bias — a responsible AI concern requiring investigation and remediation. Variance refers to model sensitivity to input changes. Overfitting is training vs. validation performance gap. Underfitting is poor performance on both sets due to insufficient model complexity.

questions.q: A model achieves 99% accuracy on training data but only 61% on validation data. What does this indicate?
opts: Class imbalance — the validation set has a different distribution than the training set
Underfitting — the model is too simple to capture the patterns in the training data
Overfitting — the model has memorized the training data and does not generalize
Data leakage — validation data has been contaminated with training examples
questions.explain: A large gap between high training accuracy (99%) and low validation accuracy (61%) is the classic overfitting signature — the model memorized training data rather than learning generalizable patterns. Underfitting shows poor performance on both sets. Data leakage would inflate validation performance. Class imbalance affects metric interpretation but not this specific pattern.

questions.q: Which statement about agentic AI is MOST accurate?
opts: Agentic AI systems can only perform a single predefined task without external tool access
Agentic AI systems can autonomously plan, use tools, and take multi-step actions to achieve goals
Agentic AI requires human approval for every individual action it takes
Agentic AI is only applicable to computer vision tasks involving visual environment navigation
questions.explain: Agentic AI systems can autonomously plan sequences of actions, use external tools (APIs, databases, code execution), and take multi-step approaches to achieve complex goals — going beyond single-turn responses. They don't require approval for every action (though governance controls can require it for high-risk actions). They work across text, code, data, and other domains.

questions.q: What does F1 score measure in ML model evaluation?
opts: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, balancing both metrics equally
The area under the ROC curve measuring discrimination across all thresholds
The ratio of true positives to the total number of positive instances in the test set
The overall percentage of predictions that were correct across all classes
questions.explain: F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall — useful when both false positives and false negatives are costly and you need a single metric balancing both. Overall accuracy is option A. AUC-ROC is option C. Option D describes recall specifically.

questions.q: A company needs to translate customer support emails from 15 different languages into English in real time. Which AWS service handles this MOST directly?
opts: Amazon Lex — to build a multilingual conversational understanding interface
Amazon Polly — to synthesize translated content into audio responses
Amazon Comprehend — to detect the language and extract key entities from each email
Amazon Translate — to automatically translate text between languages
questions.explain: Amazon Translate is AWS's neural machine translation service for converting text between languages. Comprehend detects language and extracts entities but does not translate. Lex builds conversational interfaces. Polly converts text to speech. Only Translate handles actual language translation.

questions.q: A company trains an ML model using data from 2018 to 2023 and deploys it in 2026. Which risk should the team monitor for?
opts: Class imbalance — the positive class may be underrepresented in historical data
Data leakage from the validation set contaminating the training data
Concept drift — real-world patterns have changed since the training period
Overfitting — the model memorized 2018-2023 patterns too precisely
questions.explain: Concept drift occurs when real-world patterns change after the training period — a model trained on 2018-2023 data may fail in 2026 if customer behaviors, market conditions, or business processes have changed. This is distinct from overfitting (training vs. validation gap) and data leakage (training contamination).

questions.q: Which AWS service provides a managed environment for building, training, and deploying ML models at scale?
opts: Amazon Comprehend — for NLP analysis of text data
Amazon SageMaker AI — for the complete ML development lifecycle
Amazon Rekognition — for computer vision and image analysis
Amazon Transcribe — for speech-to-text conversion
questions.explain: Amazon SageMaker AI is AWS's comprehensive managed ML platform covering the full lifecycle: data preparation, model training, hyperparameter tuning, evaluation, and deployment. Comprehend is a managed NLP service. Rekognition is for computer vision. Transcribe converts speech to text.

questions.q: A model's precision is 0.95 but its recall is 0.42 for detecting fraudulent transactions. What does this mean for business operations?
opts: The model rarely flags legitimate transactions as fraud but misses most actual fraud
The model catches most fraud cases but generates too many false alarms
The model performs inconsistently and needs retraining on more recent data
The model is very accurate overall but struggles with minority class prediction
questions.explain: High precision (0.95) = when the model flags fraud, it's almost always right (few false alarms). Low recall (0.42) = the model misses 58% of actual fraud cases. For fraud detection, this means most fraud goes undetected — a critical business risk. The fix is to lower the classification threshold to increase recall, accepting more false positives.

questions.q: A company wants to convert customer voice support calls into searchable text transcripts. Which AWS service handles this MOST directly?
opts: Amazon Polly — to synthesize text responses back into natural-sounding speech
Amazon Lex — to build a conversational interface understanding customer intent
Amazon Comprehend — to extract entities and sentiment from call content
Amazon Transcribe — to convert audio recordings to text automatically
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe is AWS's speech-to-text service — it converts audio recordings to text transcripts. Comprehend analyzes text (after transcription). Polly converts text TO speech (the reverse direction). Lex builds conversational interfaces but doesn't convert bulk recordings to transcripts.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY difference between deep learning and traditional machine learning?
opts: Deep learning is always more accurate than traditional ML for every use case
Deep learning requires labeled training data; traditional ML does not require labels
Deep learning uses multiple neural network layers to automatically learn feature representations; traditional ML typically requires manual feature engineering
Deep learning only works on image data; traditional ML works on structured tabular data
questions.explain: Deep learning's key differentiator is automatic feature learning through multiple layers of neural networks — it discovers relevant patterns without explicit feature engineering. Traditional ML typically requires domain experts to manually engineer features from raw data. Both can use labeled data. Both work on multiple data types. Deep learning is not universally superior.

questions.q: Which AWS service is MOST appropriate for building a product recommendation engine for an e-commerce platform?
opts: Amazon Comprehend — to analyze customer product reviews for sentiment
Amazon Personalize — to deliver real-time personalized product recommendations
Amazon Forecast — to predict future product demand and inventory needs
Amazon Kendra — to enable intelligent product catalog search
questions.explain: Amazon Personalize is AWS's managed recommendation service — it delivers real-time personalized recommendations using the same ML technology Amazon uses on its own platform. Comprehend analyzes text sentiment. Forecast predicts demand. Kendra enables intelligent search. Only Personalize is designed for recommendation engines.

questions.q: A data scientist needs to process 50,000 documents overnight to extract sentiment scores. Which inference type is MOST appropriate?
opts: Batch inference for processing the full document set asynchronously at lower cost
Serverless inference to automatically scale based on incoming document volume
Asynchronous inference with immediate response tokens for each document
Real-time inference for immediate per-document scoring as each document arrives
questions.explain: Batch inference processes large datasets asynchronously offline at lower cost — ideal for overnight workloads where latency is not critical. Real-time inference is for low-latency interactive use. Serverless scales for variable real-time loads. Asynchronous inference handles long-running requests but is not optimized for bulk batch processing.

questions.q: Which data type is MOST appropriate for training a model to detect objects in warehouse surveillance footage?
opts: Image and video data representing visual frames from the surveillance system
Text data with incident reports describing equipment and personnel locations
Tabular structured data with sensor readings and timestamp metadata
Time-series data capturing equipment sensor readings at regular intervals
questions.explain: Object detection in video requires image/video data — the visual frames themselves are what the model learns to analyze. Tabular and time-series data are for structured numerical/sequential data. Text data describes scenes in language but cannot train a visual object detection model.

questions.q: What distinguishes supervised learning from unsupervised learning?
opts: Supervised learning works on tabular data; unsupervised learning works on text and image data
Supervised learning uses neural networks; unsupervised learning uses decision trees
Supervised learning trains on labeled input-output pairs; unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data
Supervised learning requires more compute; unsupervised learning is computationally cheaper
questions.explain: The defining distinction: supervised learning uses labeled examples where both inputs and correct outputs are provided during training. Unsupervised learning finds structure, patterns, or groupings in data without labels. Both can use various algorithms including neural networks and tree-based methods across all data types.

questions.q: A company wants to build a system that improves its product recommendations based on user feedback over time without explicit reprogramming. Which AI/ML learning type is MOST appropriate?
opts: Supervised learning using labeled historical purchase data
Unsupervised learning to cluster users into demographic segments
Reinforcement learning where the system learns from reward signals based on user interactions
Transfer learning by adapting a pre-trained retail recommendation model
questions.explain: Reinforcement learning learns from reward signals — in this case, positive user interactions (clicks, purchases) serve as rewards, allowing the system to improve recommendations over time without explicit reprogramming. Supervised learning requires labeled data. Unsupervised learning clusters but doesn't optimize for a reward.

questions.q: A company has customer transaction records with purchase amounts, dates, and product categories but no labels indicating fraud. Which ML technique is MOST appropriate for initial fraud pattern discovery?
opts: Clustering to identify unusual transaction patterns without requiring labeled examples
Regression to predict the transaction amount most likely to be fraudulent
Reinforcement learning to penalize the model when it misclassifies a transaction
Binary classification using logistic regression on historical fraud-labeled data
questions.explain: Clustering is an unsupervised technique that groups similar transactions together — unusual clusters (anomalies) can reveal fraud patterns without requiring labeled examples. Binary classification requires labeled fraud/non-fraud data which the company doesn't have. Regression predicts continuous values. Reinforcement learning requires a defined reward signal.

questions.q: A retail company wants to forecast inventory needs for the next quarter based on historical sales trends and seasonality. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon SageMaker AI — to build a custom regression model for demand prediction
Amazon Comprehend — to analyze customer reviews for product demand signals
Amazon Personalize — to recommend which products to stock based on customer preferences
Amazon Forecast — to generate time-series predictions of future demand
questions.explain: Amazon Forecast is AWS's managed time-series forecasting service built specifically for demand forecasting — it handles seasonality, trends, and related time-series data automatically. Personalize is for recommendations. SageMaker can build custom models but requires more development work. Comprehend analyzes text.

questions.q: Which scenario is LEAST appropriate for an AI/ML solution?
opts: Predicting which customers are likely to cancel their subscription in the next 30 days
Detecting anomalous network traffic patterns from millions of daily log entries
Translating customer support emails from 12 languages into English automatically
Calculating a fixed employee salary based on a predetermined pay grade and years of service formula
questions.explain: A fixed salary calculation based on a predetermined formula is a deterministic rule — no learning, no prediction, no pattern recognition needed. This is solved by simple arithmetic, not AI/ML. AI is not appropriate when a specific, exact outcome is needed from explicit rules rather than learning from data.

sections.title: Domain 2: Fundamentals of GenAI (24%)
sections.description: GenAI concepts · Tokens · Embeddings · Foundation models · Amazon Bedrock · Agentic AI · MCP

questions.q: A solutions architect needs to store embedding vectors for a product catalog of 10 million items to enable semantic search. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate for storing and querying these vectors?
opts: Amazon S3 — to store embedding files as objects with metadata tags
Amazon OpenSearch Service — which supports vector storage and approximate nearest-neighbor search
Amazon DynamoDB — to store embeddings as binary attributes with key-value access
Amazon Redshift — to store embedding arrays in columnar format for analytics
questions.explain: Amazon OpenSearch Service supports vector storage and approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search — designed for semantic similarity queries across millions of embedding vectors. S3 stores files but doesn't support vector similarity search. DynamoDB and Redshift don't natively support ANN vector search at scale.

questions.q: Which statement about multi-agent AI systems is MOST accurate?
opts: Multi-agent systems allow specialized agents to collaborate, with each handling tasks matched to its capabilities
Multi-agent systems eliminate the need for human oversight since agents monitor each other
Multi-agent systems are only applicable to software development automation use cases
Multi-agent systems require all agents to use the same foundation model for consistency
questions.explain: Multi-agent systems allow specialized agents to collaborate on complex tasks — one agent might handle research, another code generation, another quality review — each using the model and tools best suited to its role. Different agents can use different models. Human oversight remains important. Multi-agent patterns apply across many domains (research, business workflows, customer service).

questions.q: A company is evaluating GenAI for a compliance-critical financial reporting use case. Which limitation is MOST concerning for this specific use case?
opts: High token costs making large-scale financial report generation expensive
Limited context window preventing analysis of very long financial documents
High inference latency making real-time financial reporting difficult
Nondeterminism — the same prompt may produce different outputs each time
questions.explain: Nondeterminism is the most critical concern for compliance-critical financial reporting — regulatory requirements demand consistent, auditable, reproducible outputs. Different responses to identical inputs create compliance and audit trail problems. Latency, cost, and context limits are manageable operational constraints; nondeterminism is a fundamental characteristic affecting regulatory compliance.

questions.q: A company's GenAI application consistently generates responses that include information beyond what was asked, increasing per-response costs. Which parameter adjustment addresses this MOST directly?
opts: Increase context window to give the model more background before generating
Decrease temperature to make responses more deterministic and focused
Decrease max tokens to limit the maximum length of generated responses
Increase top-P to allow the model to consider more diverse token options
questions.explain: Max tokens sets a hard limit on response length — directly controlling the maximum number of tokens generated and therefore cost per response. Temperature affects randomness, not length. Increasing top-P increases diversity. Increasing context window gives more input context but doesn't limit output length.

questions.q: A GenAI application processes customer queries about a product catalog that contains 500,000 items. The team is designing the RAG pipeline. Which vector database consideration is MOST important at this scale?
opts: The vector database must support exact nearest-neighbor search for precise retrieval
The vector database must support approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search for scalable similarity queries
The vector database must store vectors in relational table format for SQL query compatibility
The vector database must replicate vectors across all AWS regions for global availability
questions.explain: At 500,000 items, approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search is essential — exact nearest-neighbor search becomes computationally impractical at scale. ANN algorithms (HNSW, IVF) trade a small accuracy loss for dramatically faster query performance. SQL compatibility, relational format, and global replication are secondary operational concerns.

questions.q: A developer notices that calling the same Amazon Bedrock model with identical prompts produces different responses each time. Which model parameter controls this behavior?
opts: Temperature — which controls the randomness of token selection during generation
Max tokens — which sets the maximum length of the generated response
Context window — which determines how much prior conversation is included
Top-P — which limits cumulative probability mass for token selection
questions.explain: Temperature controls output randomness — higher temperature increases variation between runs with identical prompts; lower temperature (approaching 0) makes outputs more deterministic and repeatable. Top-P also affects sampling but temperature is the primary randomness control. Max tokens and context window control length and memory, not randomness.

questions.q: A company is building a GenAI application that must answer questions about internal documents that change weekly. Which approach minimizes staleness without model retraining?
opts: Pre-train a custom model on all internal documents from scratch
Increase the model's context window to include all documents in every prompt
Fine-tune the foundation model weekly on updated documents
Use RAG to retrieve current document content at query time
questions.explain: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves current document content at query time — updates are immediately available without any retraining. Weekly fine-tuning is expensive, slow, and introduces a lag. Pre-training from scratch is even more expensive. Including all documents in every prompt hits context limits and increases cost significantly.

questions.q: What is a foundation model (FM) and how does it differ from a traditional ML model?
opts: Foundation models require no training data; traditional ML models require large labeled datasets
Foundation models are smaller, task-specific models; traditional ML models are large and general-purpose
Foundation models are large models pre-trained on broad datasets that can be adapted to many tasks; traditional ML models are trained from scratch for specific tasks
Foundation models only generate text; traditional ML models handle structured tabular data
questions.explain: Foundation models are large models pre-trained on vast, broad datasets that develop general capabilities adaptable to many downstream tasks through prompting or fine-tuning. Traditional ML models are typically trained from scratch for specific tasks using task-specific labeled data. FMs generate multiple modalities (text, images, code), not just text.

questions.q: Which AWS service provides access to a variety of foundation models from multiple providers through a single API?
opts: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart — for discovering and deploying pre-built ML models
Amazon Bedrock — for accessing foundation models from multiple providers via API
Amazon Q — for AI-powered business intelligence and code assistance
AWS Transform — for migrating legacy applications to modern cloud architecture
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock provides access to foundation models from multiple providers (Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Amazon Nova, Cohere, Stability AI) through a single unified API. SageMaker JumpStart provides pre-built ML models and solutions. Amazon Q is a business AI assistant. AWS Transform accelerates application modernization.

questions.q: A developer using Amazon Bedrock notices that inference costs are significantly higher than expected for a customer chatbot. Which optimization should be evaluated FIRST?
opts: Reduce the system prompt length to minimize input token consumption per request
Enable prompt caching for repeated system prompt content across conversation turns
Increase temperature to reduce the number of tokens the model evaluates before selecting
Switch to a smaller, less capable foundation model that may suffice for the chatbot use case
questions.explain: Prompt caching stores repeated content (system prompts, static context) so it only needs to be processed once — dramatically reducing input token costs for chatbots where the same system prompt appears in every conversation turn. Model switching may degrade quality. System prompt reduction may impair behavior. Temperature doesn't affect cost calculation.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY purpose of chunking in a RAG pipeline?
opts: Splitting model responses into multiple parts for streaming delivery to users
Partitioning training data into batches for efficient fine-tuning of foundation models
Reducing the cost of embedding generation by processing fewer total tokens
Dividing large documents into smaller segments that fit within model context limits while preserving semantic coherence
questions.explain: Chunking divides large documents into smaller, semantically coherent segments that: (1) fit within model context limits, (2) can be individually embedded and indexed, and (3) can be selectively retrieved based on query relevance. Without chunking, documents that exceed context limits cannot be processed. Cost reduction is a secondary benefit.

questions.q: Which concept describes representing text as numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning for use in similarity search?
opts: Grounding — connecting AI outputs to verified external data sources
Tokenization — splitting text into individual units for model processing
Embeddings — dense numerical vector representations capturing semantic meaning
Chunking — dividing large documents into smaller segments for processing
questions.explain: Embeddings are dense numerical vector representations of text (or other data) that capture semantic meaning — similar concepts have similar vectors in the embedding space. This enables semantic similarity search. Tokenization splits text into processable units. Chunking divides documents for processing. Grounding connects outputs to external data.

questions.q: A developer uses Amazon Bedrock to build a customer service agent that needs to look up order status from a database, check inventory, and process refunds. Which Amazon Bedrock feature enables these multi-step actions?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases — for connecting the agent to organizational documents
Amazon Bedrock Agents — for enabling multi-step task execution with tool use and action groups
Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation — for assessing agent performance across tasks
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — for preventing the agent from taking harmful actions
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock Agents enables AI agents to break down complex tasks, use tools, query knowledge bases, and execute multi-step workflows — including calling APIs to look up order status, check inventory, and process refunds. Knowledge Bases provide document retrieval. Model Evaluation assesses performance. Guardrails add safety controls.

questions.q: Which GenAI capability is MOST appropriate for a company that wants to automatically generate descriptive alt-text for thousands of product images on their website?
opts: Image-to-text generation using a multi-modal FM — analyzing images and generating descriptive text
Image classification — categorizing product images into predefined product categories
Text summarization — condensing existing product descriptions into shorter alt-text
Text-to-image generation — creating new product images from text descriptions
questions.explain: Generating alt-text from images requires a multi-modal FM that can analyze visual content and generate natural language descriptions — image-to-text generation. Text-to-image is the reverse direction. Image classification assigns category labels, not descriptive text. Text summarization works on existing text, not images.

questions.q: Which approach to FM customization has the LOWEST cost and requires NO model weight changes?
opts: In-context learning — providing examples and instructions in the prompt itself
Model distillation — training a smaller model to mimic a larger model's outputs
Pre-training — training a new FM from scratch on domain-specific data
Fine-tuning — retraining existing FM weights on task-specific labeled examples
questions.explain: In-context learning (few-shot prompting) requires no model changes — examples and instructions are provided directly in the prompt at inference time. Zero additional training cost, no infrastructure needed beyond inference. Pre-training and fine-tuning both modify model weights requiring compute. Distillation trains a new model requiring labeled data and compute.

questions.q: Which Amazon Bedrock feature allows builders to create web applications that use foundation models without writing code?
opts: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — for deploying, running and scaling agents in production
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases — for connecting FMs to document repositories
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — for adding safety controls to FM applications
Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management — for versioning and managing prompt templates
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides the runtime infrastructure to deploy, run, and scale agents in production — handling the operational complexity of running agentic AI applications. Knowledge Bases connect FMs to documents. Guardrails add safety controls. Prompt Management versions prompts. AgentCore is the production deployment and scaling service.

questions.q: A startup wants to build a GenAI application quickly using foundation models without managing model infrastructure. Which AWS service BEST meets this need?
opts: Amazon SageMaker AI — for full control over model training and serving infrastructure
Amazon Bedrock — for accessing foundation models via managed API without infrastructure management
Amazon EC2 with GPU instances — for hosting open-source models with maximum flexibility
Amazon EKS — for containerized deployment of foundation models at scale
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock provides foundation model access via managed API — no infrastructure to provision, manage, or scale. The startup gets immediate access to multiple FMs through a single API. SageMaker, EC2, and EKS all require infrastructure management. For a startup wanting speed and simplicity, Bedrock is the clear choice.

questions.q: What is 'context engineering' in the context of foundation model applications?
opts: The practice of optimizing what information is included in the context window to improve FM outputs
A technique for compressing large documents to fit within FM context limits
The process of engineering new AWS contexts for multi-region FM deployments
The process of designing the infrastructure context for FM deployment on AWS
questions.explain: Context engineering is the practice of deliberately optimizing what information is included in the FM's context window — prompt structure, retrieved documents, examples, instructions, conversation history — to improve output quality and relevance. It goes beyond basic prompt engineering to consider the full information environment the model operates within.

questions.q: What is the effect of increasing temperature from 0.2 to 0.9 in a GenAI model generating product descriptions?
opts: Responses become longer as the model explores more token options before selecting
Responses become more grounded in training data and less likely to hallucinate
Responses become shorter and more concise as the model filters less relevant tokens
Responses become more varied and creative but potentially less consistent and accurate
questions.explain: Higher temperature increases output diversity and creativity — the model samples from a broader distribution of likely tokens, producing more varied, creative outputs. This can be desirable for creative writing but reduces consistency and may increase hallucination risk for factual tasks. It does not directly control response length or grounding.

questions.q: Which statement BEST describes the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in agentic AI?
opts: A pricing model that determines cost per agent action in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
A security protocol that encrypts communications between AI agents and AWS services
A standardized protocol that enables AI agents to connect to and interact with external tools and data sources
A model evaluation framework for measuring agentic AI accuracy and safety
questions.explain: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standardized open protocol enabling AI agents to connect to external tools, APIs, databases, and data sources in a consistent way — allowing agents to take actions in the real world beyond text generation. It's not a security/encryption protocol, evaluation framework, or pricing model.

sections.title: Domain 3: Applications of Foundation Models (28%)
sections.description: FM selection · Prompt engineering · Fine-tuning · RAG · Evaluation metrics · Agents

questions.q: A developer adds the instruction 'Think through this step-by-step before providing your answer' to a complex multi-step reasoning prompt. Which technique is this?
opts: Zero-shot prompting — using no examples and minimal instruction
Few-shot prompting — providing labeled examples of step-by-step reasoning
Chain-of-thought prompting — eliciting explicit reasoning steps before the final answer
Negative prompting — instructing the model to avoid jumping to conclusions
questions.explain: Chain-of-thought prompting explicitly elicits step-by-step reasoning before the final answer — significantly improving accuracy on multi-step arithmetic, logical reasoning, and analytical tasks. Research shows this simple instruction substantially improves performance on complex reasoning tasks compared to prompting for the answer directly.

questions.q: A team evaluates a fine-tuned FM for text summarization using ROUGE scores. A ROUGE-L score of 0.71 is observed. What does this measure?
opts: The longest common subsequence overlap between generated and reference summaries
The semantic similarity between generated and reference summaries using BERT embeddings
The bilingual evaluation score comparing translation quality against reference translations
The percentage of generated summary words that appear in the reference summary (precision)
questions.explain: ROUGE-L measures the longest common subsequence (LCS) between the generated and reference text — capturing fluency and sentence-level structure beyond simple word overlap. ROUGE-P measures precision (words from generated that appear in reference). BERTScore measures semantic similarity. BLEU is for translation evaluation.

questions.q: When selecting an FM for a high-frequency trading alert system requiring sub-100ms response times, which selection criterion takes HIGHEST priority?
opts: Multi-modal capability — to process both text and numerical financial data simultaneously
Cost per token — to minimize expenses across high-volume trading alert generation
Model size — larger models have more capacity for complex financial pattern recognition
Inference latency — the model must consistently respond within the required time constraint
questions.explain: Sub-100ms latency is a hard technical requirement — if the model can't respond within that constraint, it fails the use case regardless of accuracy, capability, or cost. Latency takes highest priority when the use case has strict real-time response requirements. Model size often inversely correlates with latency. Multi-modal and cost are secondary.

questions.q: Which BERTScore metric advantage does it have over ROUGE for evaluating FM-generated text summaries?
opts: BERTScore evaluates grammatical correctness and syntax quality more accurately than ROUGE
BERTScore is faster to compute and requires fewer reference examples than ROUGE
BERTScore captures semantic similarity between generated and reference text even when different words are used
BERTScore measures factual accuracy by checking claims against external knowledge sources
questions.explain: BERTScore uses BERT embeddings to measure semantic similarity — capturing meaning equivalence even when different words express the same concept. ROUGE counts surface-level word overlap — missing semantically equivalent paraphrases. This makes BERTScore more robust for evaluating summaries that may use different but semantically equivalent vocabulary.

questions.q: A company needs to choose between fine-tuning a foundation model and using RAG for a legal document Q&A system. The legal database is updated daily. Which approach is MORE appropriate and why?
opts: Fine-tuning — because it permanently teaches the model legal terminology and reasoning patterns
RAG — because it retrieves current legal content at query time without retraining when documents change daily
Fine-tuning — because it reduces inference latency compared to retrieval-augmented approaches
RAG — because it is always cheaper than fine-tuning regardless of update frequency
questions.explain: Daily updates make RAG the correct choice — it retrieves current content at query time, reflecting the latest legal documents immediately without any retraining. Fine-tuning would require daily retraining cycles to stay current, which is expensive and impractical. Cost and latency are secondary to the update frequency consideration.

questions.q: A company is evaluating whether to use an FM or a traditional ML model for a credit risk classification task with strict regulatory explainability requirements. What should guide their decision?
opts: Regulatory explainability requirements — traditional ML models like logistic regression may better satisfy 'adverse action' notice requirements
Development timeline — FMs can be deployed faster than training custom traditional ML models
Cost — traditional ML training is always cheaper than FM inference at production scale
FM performance on benchmark datasets — select the option with the highest F1 score
questions.explain: Credit risk classification under regulations like ECOA requires explainable adverse action notices — logistic regression and decision trees provide native coefficient-level explainability that black-box FMs often cannot match. Regulatory explainability requirements should drive model selection in this context, not benchmark performance, timeline, or cost.

questions.q: Which evaluation approach uses another LLM to assess the quality of FM outputs instead of human reviewers or fixed reference answers?
opts: LLM-as-a-judge — using another LLM to evaluate output quality, coherence, and accuracy
Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation — running automated tests against predefined criteria
Human-in-the-loop evaluation — domain experts manually score each FM output
Benchmark dataset evaluation — comparing FM outputs against fixed reference answers
questions.explain: LLM-as-a-judge uses another LLM to evaluate FM outputs on criteria like coherence, accuracy, helpfulness, and safety — scalable when human review is expensive and fixed benchmarks don't exist for the specific domain. It's not a replacement for human evaluation in high-stakes cases but enables scalable automated assessment.

questions.q: Which FM selection criterion is MOST important when the use case requires generating responses in French, Spanish, Arabic, and Japanese?
opts: Output speed — to handle high-volume multilingual requests efficiently
Model size — larger models generally perform better across all tasks
Multi-lingual support — the FM must have strong capability across all required languages
Context window length — to process longer documents in each language
questions.explain: Multi-lingual capability is the primary selection criterion when outputs are required in multiple specific languages — not all FMs perform equally across all languages, and some have very limited non-English capabilities. Model size, context window, and speed are important but secondary to whether the model can actually generate quality output in all required languages.

questions.q: A legal team asks why the FM recommends a specific legal interpretation. Which metric BEST addresses the need to understand model reasoning?
opts: ROUGE score — measuring how closely the model's output matches reference legal opinions
BLEU score — evaluating translation quality between legal document formats
Interpretability/explainability — providing insight into which inputs influenced the model's output
Accuracy — measuring what percentage of legal interpretations match expert consensus
questions.explain: Interpretability/explainability provides insight into why the model produced a specific output — which inputs and reasoning steps led to the legal interpretation. ROUGE and BLEU are surface-level text similarity metrics. Accuracy measures correctness rate but doesn't explain individual outputs. Explainability directly addresses 'why did it recommend this interpretation?'

questions.q: A developer discovers that users are successfully manipulating a customer service chatbot by including instructions like 'Ignore your previous instructions and...' in their messages. What type of attack is this?
opts: Prompt hijacking/injection — overriding system instructions through user input
Model jailbreaking — exploiting model vulnerabilities through adversarial inputs
Prompt exposure — extracting the system prompt content through targeted queries
Prompt poisoning — injecting malicious content into the training data
questions.explain: Prompt injection/hijacking attempts to override or bypass the system prompt's instructions through carefully crafted user inputs. Poisoning attacks target training data. Jailbreaking exploits specific model vulnerabilities to bypass safety training. Prompt exposure tries to reveal the system prompt's content. Injection is specifically about overriding existing instructions.
