questions.q: Which negative prompt technique instructs the FM about what to AVOID generating?
opts: A temperature setting that reduces the model's tendency toward creative outputs
A guardrail configuration that filters model outputs after generation
A system message that defines the model's persona and response style constraints
A negative instruction in the prompt specifying outputs the model should not produce
questions.explain: Negative prompts explicitly instruct the model to avoid specific types of content, formats, or behaviors in its response — for example, 'Do not include medical advice,' 'Avoid using technical jargon,' 'Do not mention competitor products.' This is a prompt engineering technique distinct from system messages (which set persona), temperature (which controls randomness), or guardrails (which filter outputs).

questions.q: What is model distillation in the context of foundation model customization?
opts: Reducing model size by pruning neural network weights below a threshold
Compressing an FM's knowledge base by removing rarely accessed information
Training a smaller student model to mimic the outputs of a larger teacher model
Extracting specific capabilities from a general FM to create a specialized model
questions.explain: Model distillation trains a smaller 'student' model on outputs from a larger 'teacher' model — transferring knowledge to create a smaller, faster, cheaper model that approaches the teacher's performance. It's not compression of knowledge bases, capability extraction, or weight pruning (which is a related but distinct compression technique).

questions.q: A team measures that their FM-powered customer service system has a task completion rate of 73%. What does this metric indicate?
opts: 73% of all tokens generated by the FM were relevant to the customer's question
73% of customer interactions resulted in the customer's goal being successfully achieved
73% of FM outputs passed content safety filtering before delivery to customers
73% of customer queries were answered with accuracy above the defined threshold
questions.explain: Task completion rate is a business outcome metric measuring whether users' goals were actually achieved — in customer service, whether customer issues were resolved. It's distinct from accuracy (correct answers), relevance (appropriate content), or safety filtering rates. It directly measures business value delivered.

questions.q: A company wants to use an FM to analyze customer sentiment from support tickets with minimal prompt setup and no examples. Which prompting technique applies?
opts: Zero-shot prompting relying on the model's pre-trained understanding of sentiment
Chain-of-thought prompting for step-by-step reasoning through each ticket
Retrieval-augmented generation to ground sentiment analysis in historical ticket data
Few-shot prompting with labeled sentiment examples embedded in the prompt
questions.explain: Zero-shot prompting uses no examples — the model applies its pre-trained understanding of the task directly from the instruction. Modern large FMs handle sentiment analysis well zero-shot. Few-shot includes examples. Chain-of-thought adds reasoning steps. RAG retrieves external content. Zero-shot is the technique matching 'minimal setup, no examples.'

questions.q: A team is building an AI travel assistant using Amazon Bedrock that needs to check flight availability, book hotels, and send confirmation emails. Which component manages orchestrating these multi-step actions?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — for ensuring travel recommendations comply with company policies
Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management — for managing the travel assistant's system prompt versions
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases — for providing the agent with travel policy information
Amazon Bedrock Agents with action groups — for orchestrating tool calls to external APIs
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock Agents with action groups orchestrate multi-step tasks by calling external APIs — flight availability APIs, hotel booking systems, email services — as defined action groups. Knowledge Bases provide document-based context. Guardrails add safety controls. Prompt Management handles prompt versioning. Only Agents orchestrate multi-step tool use.

questions.q: A prompt engineer is improving a customer service FM's responses. Which technique involves showing the model several examples of ideal input-output pairs within the prompt itself?
opts: System prompting — setting the model's persona and behavioral constraints
Zero-shot prompting — providing a clear task description with no examples
Few-shot prompting — including two to five example input-output pairs in the prompt
Chain-of-thought prompting — instructing the model to reason step-by-step before answering
questions.explain: Few-shot prompting includes 2-5 example input-output pairs directly in the prompt — showing the model the exact format and quality of response desired. Zero-shot provides no examples. Chain-of-thought prompts explicit reasoning steps. System prompting sets behavioral context but doesn't include task examples.

questions.q: A company's FM-powered document search returns irrelevant results for complex technical queries. Which RAG improvement MOST directly addresses retrieval quality?
opts: Increasing the number of retrieved chunks to include more potential relevant content
Improving the embedding model or chunking strategy to better capture technical domain semantics
Increasing the FM's temperature to generate more diverse responses from retrieved content
Expanding the knowledge base to include more documents across broader topic areas
questions.explain: Retrieval quality depends on how well embeddings capture the semantic meaning of technical content — a domain-appropriate embedding model or better chunking strategy (preserving technical context) directly improves retrieval relevance. Returning more chunks increases noise. Temperature affects generation, not retrieval. More documents adds volume but doesn't improve matching quality.

questions.q: A developer wants to improve an FM's responses on a proprietary enterprise knowledge domain by showing it examples directly in the prompt without any retraining. Which technique does this describe?
opts: Instruction fine-tuning — training the model to follow enterprise-specific task formats
In-context learning — providing domain examples within the prompt at inference time
Continuous pre-training — extending base model training on enterprise documents
Transfer learning — adapting pre-trained weights to the enterprise domain
questions.explain: In-context learning provides domain-specific examples directly in the prompt at inference time — no model weight changes, no training infrastructure, no retraining. The model learns the pattern from the examples in its context window. Transfer learning, instruction fine-tuning, and continuous pre-training all involve modifying model weights.

questions.q: A developer is using Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management. Which benefit does prompt versioning provide?
opts: Automatically optimizing prompt wording to improve model performance
Encrypting prompt content to prevent exposure through API responses
Reducing inference costs by caching frequently used prompts across sessions
Enabling rollback to previous prompt versions if a new version degrades output quality
questions.explain: Prompt versioning in Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management enables tracking prompt changes and rolling back to previous versions if quality degrades — essential for production systems where prompt changes can significantly affect output quality. Prompt caching addresses cost. Prompt optimization is a separate activity. Encryption protects data at rest.

questions.q: Which fine-tuning approach trains only a small set of additional parameters while keeping the original FM weights frozen?
opts: Continuous pre-training — extending the base model's training on new domain corpora
Full fine-tuning — updating all model weights on the domain-specific training dataset
Instruction tuning — training the model to follow natural language task instructions
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT/LoRA) — adapting the model through small trainable layers
questions.explain: PEFT techniques like LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) add small trainable matrices while keeping original weights frozen — dramatically reducing compute and storage requirements for fine-tuning. Full fine-tuning updates all weights (most expensive). Instruction tuning is a training objective approach. Continuous pre-training extends base training.

sections.title: Domain 4: Guidelines for Responsible AI (14%)
sections.description: Bias · Fairness · Explainability · Transparency · Legal risks · AWS tools · Human-centered design

questions.q: A company's FM generates product recommendations that consistently suggest premium products to one demographic and budget products to another with identical purchase histories. Which responsible AI concern does this represent?
opts: Hallucination — the model is generating recommendations not grounded in actual purchase history
Algorithmic bias — the model produces inequitable outcomes correlated with demographic characteristics
Model variance — the model's recommendations are overly sensitive to minor input differences
Overfitting — the model has memorized specific demographic-product associations from training data
questions.explain: Systematically different recommendations for identical purchase histories across demographic groups is algorithmic bias — the model learned to associate demographics with product tiers in a discriminatory way. Hallucination is fabricated content. Variance is sensitivity to input changes. Overfitting is training vs. validation gap. The key signal is demographic disparity in outcomes for equivalent inputs.

questions.q: Which Amazon Bedrock feature allows organizations to apply content filtering, topic restrictions, and personally identifiable information (PII) detection to FM inputs and outputs?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — applying configurable safeguards to FM inputs and outputs
Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation — testing FM outputs for quality and safety
Amazon Bedrock Agents — orchestrating multi-step tasks with tool use
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases — connecting FMs to organizational document repositories
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails applies configurable content filtering, topic blocking, PII detection/redaction, grounding checks, and word filters to both FM inputs and outputs — implementing responsible AI safeguards at the application layer regardless of which underlying model is used. Knowledge Bases, Agents, and Model Evaluation serve different functions.

questions.q: What is 'label quality' in the context of training data for responsible AI?
opts: The proportion of positive to negative labels ensuring balanced class representation
The speed at which human annotators can apply labels to new training examples
The formatting consistency of how labels are applied across the entire training dataset
The accuracy and correctness of annotations assigned to training examples by human annotators
questions.explain: Label quality refers to the accuracy and correctness of annotations assigned by human annotators — whether the label assigned to each training example actually reflects the true ground truth. Poor label quality introduces noise, propagates annotator biases, and degrades model reliability. Formatting consistency, class balance, and annotation speed are related but distinct concerns.

questions.q: Which AWS service helps detect bias in ML model predictions by analyzing outcomes across different demographic subgroups?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — for filtering harmful content from FM outputs
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor — for detecting data and model quality drift in production
Amazon SageMaker Clarify — for bias detection and explainability analysis in ML models
Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) — for adding human review workflows to ML predictions
questions.explain: Amazon SageMaker Clarify detects bias in training data and model predictions by analyzing outcomes across demographic subgroups — identifying disparate impact before and after deployment. Model Monitor tracks drift in production. A2I adds human review. Bedrock Guardrails filters FM outputs. Only Clarify specifically targets bias detection and explainability.

questions.q: A company discovers their image recognition FM performs with 94% accuracy on light-skinned faces but 71% on dark-skinned faces. Using the principle of responsible AI, what is the FIRST action?
opts: Deploy the model with a disclaimer noting the accuracy difference for dark-skinned users
Investigate training data representation for dark-skinned faces and remediate before deployment
Accept the disparity as statistically within tolerance since 94% average accuracy is strong
Deploy to light-skinned users only and maintain manual processes for dark-skinned users
questions.explain: A 23-point accuracy gap correlated with skin tone is a bias and fairness failure requiring investigation and remediation before deployment — not acceptance, disclosure-only, or partial deployment that excludes a demographic group. The root cause is almost certainly underrepresentation in training data. Responsible AI requires fixing the root cause, not managing the symptom.

questions.q: A company wants human reviewers to validate high-confidence medical diagnosis AI outputs before they affect patient treatment decisions. Which AWS service enables this workflow?
opts: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) — to route AI outputs to human reviewers based on confidence thresholds
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor — to detect performance degradation in the production model
Amazon Rekognition — to add confidence scores to medical image analysis outputs
Amazon SageMaker Clarify — to detect bias in the diagnosis model's predictions
questions.explain: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) is specifically designed for human-in-the-loop ML workflows — routing outputs to human reviewers based on configurable conditions like low confidence scores, specific prediction types, or random sampling. Clarify detects bias. Model Monitor tracks drift. Rekognition is for image analysis.

questions.q: What is the MAIN difference between an interpretable model and an explainable model?
opts: Interpretable models are used for computer vision; explainable models are used for NLP tasks
Interpretable models require labeled training data; explainable models can work with unlabeled data
Interpretable models are accurate; explainable models trade accuracy for human understandability
Interpretable models are natively understandable by design (e.g., decision trees); explainable models use post-hoc tools to explain black-box outputs
questions.explain: Interpretable models are natively transparent by design — you can directly read their logic (decision trees, linear regression coefficients). Explainable models are typically complex black-boxes that use post-hoc explanation tools (SHAP, LIME, attention visualization) to provide after-the-fact explanations. The distinction is native transparency vs. applied explanation tools.

questions.q: Which dataset characteristic BEST reduces demographic bias in an FM trained on customer sentiment data?
opts: Dataset balance — having exactly equal numbers of positive and negative sentiment examples
Maximum dataset size — larger datasets inherently reduce demographic bias effects
Dataset inclusivity and diversity — ensuring representation across all demographic groups being served
Dataset recency — using only the most recent customer feedback to reflect current sentiment
questions.explain: Inclusive, diverse datasets representing all demographic groups the model will serve is the primary bias reduction strategy. Maximum size doesn't help if the data is already biased — it amplifies bias. Recency matters for relevance but not specifically for demographic representation. Sentiment balance (positive/negative) addresses class imbalance, not demographic bias.

questions.q: A company is selecting an FM and wants to assess the environmental impact of training and running the model. Which responsible AI principle does this reflect?
opts: Fairness — ensuring the model treats all users equitably regardless of their location
Safety — preventing the model from producing harmful environmental content
Sustainability — considering the environmental cost of training and operating AI systems
Transparency — disclosing the model's carbon footprint to affected stakeholders
questions.explain: Evaluating the environmental cost of training and running an FM reflects the sustainability principle in responsible AI model selection — considering energy consumption, carbon footprint, and environmental impact alongside performance and cost. This is explicitly called out in the AIF-C01 exam guide under responsible model selection.

questions.q: A data scientist uses Amazon SageMaker Model Cards to document a customer churn model. Which information is MOST critical to include for responsible AI governance?
opts: Model performance metrics, known limitations, intended use cases, and bias evaluation results
The cost of training the model and estimated monthly inference cost in production
The names and credentials of the data scientists who built and validated the model
The specific hyperparameter configuration and architecture used during model training
questions.explain: Model Cards for responsible AI governance should include: performance metrics (how well does it work), known limitations (where does it fail), intended use cases (what it should and shouldn't be used for), and bias evaluation results (is it fair). Technical configuration, cost, and team credentials serve operational and HR purposes but are secondary to responsible AI governance.

questions.q: Which approach BEST demonstrates responsible practices when deploying a GenAI system that affects hiring decisions?
opts: Limiting the model to screening tasks only and never using AI recommendations in final decisions
Training the model exclusively on successful employee data to optimize for company cultural fit
Maximizing model accuracy on the overall candidate pool to minimize total errors
Implementing regular bias audits, explainability for adverse decisions, and human review for all final hiring choices
questions.explain: Comprehensive responsible AI practice for hiring includes: regular bias audits (detecting disparate impact), explainability for adverse decisions (regulatory compliance), and human accountability for final decisions (accountability principle). Maximizing accuracy hides subgroup disparities. Excluding AI entirely is unnecessarily restrictive. Training only on successful employees encodes existing cultural bias.

questions.q: Which human-centered design principle for explainable AI ensures that users who receive AI-generated decisions understand why those decisions were made?
opts: Privacy by design — minimizing data collection in AI decision-making processes
User feedback mechanisms — allowing users to rate AI decision quality for model improvement
AI decision transparency — providing users with understandable explanations of AI decisions affecting them
Accessibility design — ensuring AI interfaces work for users with disabilities
questions.explain: AI decision transparency ensures affected users understand why an AI system made a decision affecting them — a core human-centered design principle for explainable AI. This enables users to contest decisions, understand their situation, and maintain informed consent. User feedback improves models. Accessibility enables use. Privacy protects data. Transparency enables understanding.

questions.q: A company deploys a hiring screening AI. Which legal risk is MOST relevant if the model produces disparate outcomes across protected classes?
opts: Intellectual property infringement — if the training data included copyrighted resumes
Discriminatory bias liability — violations of equal employment opportunity laws due to disparate impact
Hallucination liability — if the model fabricates qualifications that don't appear on resumes
Privacy violations — if the model retains and exposes candidate PII across sessions
questions.explain: AI hiring tools producing disparate outcomes across protected classes (race, gender, age, disability) create discriminatory bias liability under employment laws like EEOC guidelines and Title VII — this is the most direct legal risk. IP infringement, hallucination, and privacy are also real risks but the question asks about disparate outcome liability specifically.

questions.q: A developer notices their FM occasionally generates factually incorrect information presented with high confidence. Which characteristic of responsible AI does this most directly violate?
opts: Veracity — the model should produce accurate, truthful outputs rather than confident hallucinations
Robustness — the model should maintain consistent performance under adversarial inputs
Safety — the model should not produce outputs that could cause direct physical harm
Inclusivity — the model should benefit all user groups equally without exclusion
questions.explain: Veracity (truthfulness/accuracy) is the responsible AI characteristic directly violated by confident hallucinations — generating incorrect information presented as fact. Inclusivity covers equitable access and benefit. Robustness covers performance under adversarial conditions. Safety covers physical harm prevention. Confident false information is a veracity failure.

questions.q: A company trains an FM on customer service transcripts. Legal counsel raises a concern that the training data may include copyrighted content from third-party knowledge bases. Which legal risk is this?
opts: Data privacy violations — customer transcripts may contain PII without consent
Hallucination liability — copyrighted content may cause the model to generate false information
Biased model outputs — the third-party content may introduce demographic bias
Intellectual property infringement — using copyrighted content for training may violate IP rights
questions.explain: Using copyrighted content for FM training without permission or proper licensing may constitute intellectual property infringement — a significant legal risk explicitly identified in the AIF-C01 exam guide. IP owners may have claims against organizations training on their content without authorization. This is distinct from bias, privacy, or hallucination risks.

sections.title: Domain 5: Security, Compliance & Governance for AI (14%)
sections.description: IAM · Encryption · Data governance · Compliance · AWS audit services · Prompt security

questions.q: A company must demonstrate to regulators that their AI systems comply with data residency requirements ensuring customer data never leaves a specific country. Which combination of controls BEST addresses this?
opts: AWS CloudTrail logging combined with Amazon Macie data classification
AWS Config rules combined with Amazon VPC to enforce regional data processing boundaries
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails combined with IAM policies for content and access control
AWS Audit Manager combined with Amazon Inspector for compliance assessment
questions.explain: Data residency requires: AWS Config rules to monitor that resources stay within approved regions (detecting violations), and Amazon VPC with regional endpoints to ensure data processing traffic stays within the required geographic boundary. CloudTrail+Macie addresses audit/discovery. Guardrails+IAM addresses content and access. Audit Manager+Inspector assesses compliance posture.

questions.q: Which governance process ensures that AI systems used in production are periodically reviewed for continued compliance with organizational policies and regulatory requirements?
opts: Ongoing review cadence with defined intervals for assessing AI system compliance post-deployment
Ad-hoc review triggered only when an AI-related incident or complaint is received
Annual review required only for AI systems classified as high-risk by the organization
One-time pre-deployment responsible AI review before the system goes live
questions.explain: Effective AI governance requires ongoing review cadence with defined intervals — not one-time pre-deployment review, not incident-only review, and not only for high-risk systems. Regulations, organizational policies, and data distributions all change over time, requiring periodic systematic reassessment of deployed AI systems regardless of whether incidents have occurred.

questions.q: A developer notices that users are attempting to extract the system prompt of a customer service FM by asking 'What are your instructions?' Which type of attack is this?
opts: Model jailbreaking — bypassing safety constraints through carefully crafted inputs
Prompt poisoning — contaminating the model's knowledge through malicious inputs
Prompt injection — attempting to override system instructions with user input
Prompt exposure — attempting to extract the system prompt's confidential content
questions.explain: Prompt exposure attacks attempt to extract the confidential system prompt content — revealing proprietary instructions, personas, or business logic embedded in the system message. Prompt injection overrides instructions. Jailbreaking bypasses safety training. Poisoning targets training data. Exposure specifically targets revealing what's already in the system prompt.

questions.q: A data scientist wants to prevent a GenAI application from returning personally identifiable information (PII) included in knowledge base documents to end users. Which Amazon Bedrock feature addresses this MOST directly?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation — to test whether the model leaks PII in its responses
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases — to control which documents are included in the knowledge base
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — to detect and redact PII from model inputs and outputs
Amazon Bedrock Agents — to intercept and filter responses before delivery to users
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails includes PII detection and redaction — automatically identifying and masking sensitive information like names, SSNs, credit card numbers, and email addresses in both FM inputs and outputs before delivery. Knowledge Bases controls what's indexed. Agents orchestrate tasks. Model Evaluation tests performance. Only Guardrails provides active PII redaction.

questions.q: A company wants to ensure that only specific IAM roles can invoke Amazon Bedrock foundation models in their account. Which control enforces this MOST directly?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — to filter which model outputs can be returned to calling applications
IAM policies — to grant or deny specific roles permission to invoke Bedrock model APIs
AWS CloudTrail — to log all Bedrock API calls for post-hoc access review
Amazon VPC endpoint — to restrict Bedrock API traffic to the private network
questions.explain: IAM policies grant or deny specific IAM roles the permission to call Bedrock InvokeModel APIs — the primary access control mechanism. Guardrails filter content, not access. CloudTrail logs calls after they happen (detective, not preventive). VPC endpoints restrict network routing but not IAM-level access control. IAM is the correct answer for role-based access control.

questions.q: A company's FM application is experiencing 'output filtering and validation' failures where the model occasionally generates responses that bypass content safety rules. Which AWS approach addresses this at the application layer?
opts: Implementing Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to add an additional filtering layer on model outputs
Increasing the model's temperature to reduce the likelihood of boundary-case outputs
Adding IAM policies that restrict which users can invoke the model for sensitive tasks
Retraining the foundation model with additional safety examples to improve baseline safety
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails adds an application-layer content filtering safety net that operates independently of the model's built-in safety training — providing an additional, configurable layer that can catch outputs that bypass the model's baseline safety. Retraining changes the model but takes time. Temperature affects randomness. IAM controls access, not content.

questions.q: A company wants to maintain a complete audit trail of all Amazon Bedrock API calls made in their account, including which models were invoked and by whom. Which AWS service provides this?
opts: AWS Config — to track configuration changes to Bedrock resources over time
AWS Audit Manager — to continuously audit Bedrock usage against compliance frameworks
Amazon CloudWatch — to monitor real-time Bedrock API performance metrics
AWS CloudTrail — to log all Bedrock API calls with user identity and request details
questions.explain: AWS CloudTrail logs all API calls made in an AWS account — including Bedrock InvokeModel calls with user identity, timestamp, request parameters, and source IP. This creates the audit trail required for security investigations and compliance. CloudWatch monitors metrics. Config tracks configuration changes. Audit Manager assesses against compliance frameworks.

questions.q: A company must comply with a regulation requiring them to explain any AI-driven adverse decision to the affected customer within 30 days. Which model type is MOST compliant with this requirement by design?
opts: A transformer-based model with attention visualization for output interpretation
A large deep learning ensemble model that achieves the highest accuracy on the task
A logistic regression or decision tree model that provides native coefficient-level explainability
A fine-tuned foundation model with SHAP values added for post-hoc explanation
questions.explain: Logistic regression and decision tree models provide native coefficient-level or rule-based explainability — you can directly state which factors influenced the decision and by how much, without additional tools. For regulatory adverse action explanations, native interpretability is more defensible than post-hoc explanation tools (SHAP, attention) applied to black-box models.

questions.q: Which AWS service helps identify potential security vulnerabilities in Amazon EC2 instances hosting AI model serving infrastructure?
opts: Amazon Macie — to discover and classify sensitive data in S3 buckets used by the AI system
Amazon Inspector — to automatically assess EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and network exposures
AWS CloudTrail — to audit API calls made by the model serving infrastructure
AWS Trusted Advisor — to identify cost optimization opportunities in the AI infrastructure
questions.explain: Amazon Inspector automatically scans EC2 instances (and container images) for software vulnerabilities (CVEs), unintended network exposures, and security findings — directly assessing the security posture of model serving infrastructure. Macie discovers sensitive data. CloudTrail audits API calls. Trusted Advisor gives cost and best practice recommendations.

questions.q: Which AWS service continuously evaluates AWS resource configurations against predefined compliance rules and alerts when configurations drift from the desired state?
opts: AWS Config — continuously monitoring resource configurations against compliance rules
AWS Trusted Advisor — providing real-time guidance on AWS best practices and cost optimization
Amazon Inspector — scanning EC2 instances and container images for security vulnerabilities
AWS CloudTrail — logging all API calls and user activity across AWS services
questions.explain: AWS Config continuously monitors and records resource configurations, evaluates them against defined rules, and alerts on non-compliant configurations — ideal for governance of AI infrastructure. CloudTrail logs API activity. Trusted Advisor gives best practice recommendations. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities. Config specifically provides continuous compliance monitoring.

questions.q: An AI application processes sensitive financial records through Amazon Bedrock. The security team requires that data never traverses the public internet. Which configuration achieves this?
opts: Using AWS KMS customer-managed keys to encrypt all data sent to Bedrock
Enabling Amazon Macie to classify sensitive financial data before sending to Bedrock
Enabling AWS CloudTrail to log all API calls to Bedrock for security monitoring
Configuring a VPC endpoint for Amazon Bedrock to keep traffic on the AWS private network
questions.explain: A VPC endpoint for Amazon Bedrock routes all API traffic through the AWS private network — data never traverses the public internet. CloudTrail logs traffic but doesn't route it. KMS encrypts data but doesn't control network routing. Macie classifies data but doesn't affect network path. VPC endpoints are the correct solution for private network routing requirements.

questions.q: Which AWS service helps a company systematically assess their Amazon Bedrock usage against compliance frameworks like GDPR or HIPAA?
opts: Amazon Inspector — to assess vulnerabilities that could affect compliance posture
AWS CloudTrail — to provide activity logs as evidence for compliance auditors
AWS Audit Manager — to continuously collect evidence and assess controls against compliance frameworks
AWS Config — to monitor resource configurations for compliance rule violations
questions.explain: AWS Audit Manager continuously collects evidence, maps controls to compliance frameworks (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI DSS), and generates audit-ready reports — systematically assessing compliance posture rather than providing raw logs or monitoring configurations. CloudTrail provides logs. Config monitors configurations. Inspector assesses vulnerabilities.

questions.q: A company uses Amazon S3 to store training datasets for their AI models. Which AWS service automatically discovers and alerts on buckets containing sensitive data like PII or financial information?
opts: AWS Config — to monitor S3 bucket configuration changes and policy violations
Amazon Macie — to automatically discover, classify, and alert on sensitive data in S3
Amazon Inspector — to scan S3 bucket objects for security vulnerabilities
AWS CloudTrail — to log all S3 data access events for security monitoring
questions.explain: Amazon Macie uses ML to automatically discover, classify, and alert on sensitive data (PII, financial data, credentials) stored in Amazon S3 — providing visibility into what sensitive training data exists and where. Config monitors bucket configurations. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities (primarily in compute). CloudTrail logs access events.

questions.q: A healthcare company processes patient data through Amazon Bedrock. Which AWS service helps ensure the data remains encrypted during transit and at rest?
opts: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) — to manage encryption keys for data at rest and in transit
AWS CloudTrail — to audit access patterns to patient data across AWS services
Amazon Inspector — to assess security vulnerabilities in the AI application infrastructure
Amazon Macie — to discover and classify sensitive patient data stored in S3
questions.explain: AWS KMS manages encryption keys used to encrypt data at rest (S3 objects, EBS volumes, database storage) and can be used with services that support customer-managed keys. Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data. CloudTrail audits API activity. Inspector assesses infrastructure vulnerabilities. KMS is the direct encryption key management service.

questions.q: A company is implementing a data governance strategy for their AI systems. Which component ensures that training data can be traced back to its original source throughout the ML pipeline?
opts: Data residency — ensuring data remains within approved geographic boundaries
Data minimization — collecting only the minimum data necessary for the AI use case
Data lifecycle management — policies for retaining and deleting data at defined intervals
Data lineage — tracking data origin, transformations, and flow through the AI pipeline
questions.explain: Data lineage tracks where data came from, how it was transformed, and how it flows through the pipeline — enabling audit trails showing exactly what training data was used, from which sources, with what transformations. This is critical for compliance, debugging, and responsible AI. Lifecycle governs retention. Residency governs geography. Minimization limits collection.

sections.title: Mixed AWS AI Scenarios & Service Selection
sections.description: Cross-domain judgment · AWS service selection · Architecture decisions · Cost optimization

questions.q: A media company processes 100,000 news articles daily to extract named entities, sentiment, and key topics. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate for this at scale?
opts: Amazon Bedrock — to use a foundation model for article analysis with prompt engineering
Amazon Comprehend — a managed NLP service for entity extraction, sentiment, and topic modeling at scale
Amazon Kendra — to build an intelligent search index across all processed news articles
Amazon Transcribe — to convert audio news broadcasts to text before NLP processing
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend is a managed NLP service purpose-built for exactly these tasks at scale — entity extraction, sentiment analysis, key phrase detection, and topic modeling. It's more cost-efficient than using Bedrock (FM inference) for structured NLP extraction tasks. Kendra is for search. Transcribe converts audio. Comprehend is the right tool for high-volume structured NLP.

questions.q: A company's compliance team requires that all AI model training data used in their organization be documented with its source, collection method, and applicable usage rights. Which data governance component addresses this requirement?
opts: Data cataloging and lineage — documenting data sources, provenance, and usage rights
Data residency policies — ensuring training data stays within approved geographic regions
Data retention policies — defining how long training data is kept before deletion
Data minimization — ensuring only the minimum data necessary for training is collected
questions.explain: Data cataloging and lineage documentation records where training data came from (source), how it was collected (method), and what rights exist to use it (usage rights/licensing) — directly addressing the compliance requirement for data provenance documentation. Minimization limits quantity. Residency limits geography. Retention governs duration. Only cataloging/lineage documents provenance.

questions.q: A startup wants to build a GenAI customer service chatbot using the most cost-effective AWS approach with minimal infrastructure management. Which architecture is MOST appropriate?
opts: Deploy an open-source LLM on Amazon SageMaker AI endpoints with custom inference containers
Use Amazon Lex for natural language understanding combined with a custom ML model on Lambda
Train a custom LLM from scratch on Amazon EC2 GPU instances and host on Amazon EKS
Use Amazon Bedrock to access a foundation model API and build the chatbot with Bedrock Agents
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock + Bedrock Agents provides FM access via managed API with no infrastructure to provision, scale, or manage — the most cost-effective, lowest-overhead path for a startup. Training from scratch is extremely expensive. SageMaker custom containers require ML expertise and infrastructure management. Lex+custom model requires significant development without the generative capabilities FMs provide.

questions.q: A company needs to process 1 million customer feedback forms to classify them into 8 product feedback categories. The forms are already stored in Amazon S3. Which approach is MOST cost-effective?
opts: Use Amazon Kendra to index all forms and search for category keywords in each document
Use Amazon Bedrock with a large FM to classify each form individually in real time
Use Amazon Comprehend custom classification with batch processing of S3 documents
Use Amazon SageMaker AI to train a custom classification model from scratch on labeled feedback
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend custom classification with batch processing is purpose-built for exactly this — training a custom multi-class classifier on labeled examples, then running batch inference on millions of S3 documents at lower cost than FM inference. Bedrock FM inference per document at scale is expensive. SageMaker from scratch requires more development. Kendra is for search, not classification.

questions.q: A company's AI team wants to experiment with multiple foundation models quickly to identify which performs best for their use case before committing to a production deployment. Which AWS approach enables this MOST efficiently?
opts: Deploy each candidate model on separate Amazon SageMaker endpoints and test in parallel
Use Amazon Bedrock's model catalog to test multiple FMs through a unified API without infrastructure setup
Use Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to deploy pre-built models from the model hub for comparison
Build separate Amazon EC2-based inference servers for each candidate model to enable fair comparison
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock's model catalog provides access to multiple FMs from different providers through a single unified API — switch between models by changing a single parameter with no additional infrastructure. SageMaker endpoints require separate provisioning per model. JumpStart deploys models but requires more setup. EC2-based servers maximize complexity for this exploratory task.

questions.q: A company processes customer service calls and needs to: (1) convert speech to text, (2) detect customer sentiment, (3) extract key issues, and (4) translate non-English calls. Which AWS service combination is correct?
opts: Amazon Transcribe → Amazon Comprehend → Amazon Comprehend → Amazon Translate
Amazon Lex → Amazon Transcribe → Amazon Comprehend → Amazon Polly
Amazon Translate → Amazon Transcribe → Amazon Rekognition → Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Polly → Amazon Comprehend → Amazon Translate → Amazon Lex
questions.explain: The correct pipeline: Amazon Transcribe (speech-to-text) → Amazon Comprehend (sentiment detection) → Amazon Comprehend (entity/key issue extraction) → Amazon Translate (translate non-English). Polly converts text to speech (wrong direction). Lex builds conversational interfaces. Rekognition handles images/video. Comprehend handles both sentiment and entity tasks.

questions.q: A company wants to build an AI coding assistant for their developers. Which Amazon service is specifically designed for AI-powered developer tooling including code generation and explanation?
opts: Amazon SageMaker AI — for building and deploying custom code generation ML models
Kiro — an agentic IDE for spec-driven software development with AI assistance
Amazon Bedrock — for accessing general-purpose foundation models for code generation
Amazon Q Developer — an AI-powered developer assistant for code generation, explanation, and review
questions.explain: Amazon Q Developer is AWS's purpose-built AI developer assistant — providing code generation, explanation, security scanning, and code review within developer IDEs and workflows. Amazon Bedrock provides general FM access. SageMaker is for custom ML model development. Kiro is an agentic IDE for specification-driven development. Q Developer is specifically designed for the developer assistant use case.

questions.q: A company needs to implement responsible AI practices for their Amazon Bedrock application serving financial advice. Which combination BEST addresses hallucination risk?
opts: Add human review for all outputs using Amazon A2I with financial expert reviewers
Increase model temperature to explore more diverse financial advice options
Use RAG with verified financial data sources combined with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails grounding checks
Fine-tune the model exclusively on historical financial data to improve accuracy
questions.explain: The most comprehensive hallucination mitigation: RAG grounds responses in verified financial data sources (reducing fabrication), and Bedrock Guardrails grounding checks verify that responses are supported by the retrieved sources (detecting unsupported claims). Increasing temperature increases hallucination risk. Fine-tuning alone doesn't prevent hallucination. A2I human review is valuable but the question asks about addressing the root cause.

questions.q: A machine learning team wants to deploy a new version of their customer churn model while monitoring for performance degradation compared to the current production model on live traffic. Which AWS approach enables this?
opts: Amazon SageMaker AI with shadow deployment — running new model alongside production to compare outputs
Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation — testing both model versions against benchmark datasets
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor — detecting data drift in the production model's input distribution
AWS Config — tracking configuration changes between the two model deployment versions
questions.explain: SageMaker shadow deployment runs the new model version alongside the production model on live traffic, capturing both outputs for comparison — enabling evidence-based deployment decisions using real production data. Bedrock Model Evaluation uses benchmark datasets, not live traffic. SageMaker Model Monitor detects input drift. Config tracks configuration changes.

questions.q: A company uses Amazon Bedrock and wants to ensure their FM application meets the AWS shared responsibility model requirements. Which security responsibility belongs to the CUSTOMER?
opts: Securing customer data, IAM access control, and application-level security for the Bedrock integration
Patching and maintaining the foundation model software and serving infrastructure
Managing network security between Bedrock's internal microservices
Physical security of the underlying data center infrastructure hosting Bedrock
questions.explain: Under the shared responsibility model, customers are responsible for: securing their data (encryption, access control), managing IAM permissions for who can call Bedrock APIs, and application-level security (secure coding, input validation). AWS is responsible for: physical infrastructure, model software maintenance, and internal network security. Customer data and access control are always customer responsibilities.

questions.q: A developer needs to monitor the quality of Amazon Bedrock FM responses in production to detect when response quality degrades over time. Which metric type BEST serves this purpose?
opts: Model configuration metrics like temperature settings and max token limits
Cost metrics like total token spend and cost per response from AWS Cost Explorer
Infrastructure metrics like API latency and token throughput from Amazon CloudWatch
Business outcome metrics like user satisfaction scores and task completion rates
questions.explain: Business outcome metrics (user satisfaction, task completion, escalation rates) are the most meaningful indicators of FM response quality degradation in production — they measure whether the AI is actually helping users achieve their goals. Infrastructure metrics measure operational health. Configuration metrics are settings, not quality measures. Cost metrics measure spend, not quality.

questions.q: A developer is building a RAG application using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. The knowledge base contains 200,000 product documents. Which component handles converting document content into searchable vector embeddings?
opts: Amazon Comprehend — extracting entities from documents before vector storage
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — filtering document content for safety before indexing
An embedding model specified in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases configuration
Amazon Kendra — providing keyword-based search across the product document corpus
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases uses a specified embedding model to automatically convert document chunks into vector embeddings during ingestion — storing them in the configured vector store (OpenSearch Service, Aurora, etc.). Guardrails filter content, not create embeddings. Kendra is a separate keyword/semantic search service. Comprehend extracts NLP features but doesn't create embeddings.

questions.q: A company wants to fine-tune an Amazon Bedrock foundation model on their proprietary customer service transcripts. Which data preparation step is MOST important for responsible fine-tuning?
opts: Maximizing the training dataset size by including all available transcripts without filtering
Reviewing and removing PII, offensive content, and biased examples before fine-tuning
Converting all transcripts to a standardized JSON format for efficient model training
Splitting transcripts into exactly equal train, validation, and test sets by timestamp
questions.explain: Before fine-tuning on customer service transcripts, reviewing and removing PII (GDPR/privacy), offensive content (safety), and biased examples (fairness) is the most critical responsible AI data preparation step. The fine-tuned model will amplify any patterns in the training data — including harmful ones. Format standardization and data splitting are important but secondary to data quality and safety.

questions.q: A company wants to make their internal code repositories searchable using natural language queries. Which AWS service enables intelligent search over code documentation?
opts: Amazon Kendra — to build an intelligent enterprise search index over code repositories
Amazon Textract — to extract text from scanned code documentation PDFs
Amazon Personalize — to recommend relevant code documentation based on developer behavior
Amazon Comprehend — to extract entities and keywords from code documentation files
questions.explain: Amazon Kendra is AWS's intelligent enterprise search service — it indexes content from multiple sources (code repos, documentation, wikis) and enables natural language queries. It uses ML to understand query intent and return relevant results beyond simple keyword matching. Comprehend extracts NLP insights. Textract reads scanned documents. Personalize makes recommendations.

questions.q: Which AWS service helps developers build agentic AI applications by providing tools for memory management, tool orchestration, and multi-agent communication?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — for applying safety controls to agent inputs and outputs
Amazon Q Developer — for assisting developers writing agent orchestration code
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases — for giving agents access to organizational documents
Strands Agents — an open-source SDK for building agentic AI applications on AWS
questions.explain: Strands Agents is AWS's open-source SDK specifically designed for building agentic AI applications — providing tools for memory management, tool use, workflow orchestration, and multi-agent communication patterns. Knowledge Bases gives agents document access. Guardrails adds safety controls. Q Developer assists with coding. Strands Agents is the SDK for building the agents themselves.

sections.title: Domain 1: AI/ML Fundamentals — Hard
sections.description: Inference types · SageMaker services · Metrics · MLOps · Edge cases · Service selection traps

questions.q: A team ranks these SageMaker inference options from LOWEST to HIGHEST latency: Batch Transform, Real-time Inference, Asynchronous Inference. What is the correct order?
opts: Real-time → Asynchronous → Batch Transform
Asynchronous → Real-time → Batch Transform
Batch Transform → Real-time → Asynchronous
Real-time → Batch Transform → Asynchronous
questions.explain: Real-time inference returns synchronous responses in milliseconds — lowest latency. Asynchronous inference queues requests for longer-running payloads — moderate latency. Batch Transform processes entire datasets offline — highest latency. Correct order: Real-time → Asynchronous → Batch Transform.

questions.q: Which metric is MOST appropriate for evaluating a recommendation system where the ranking order of results matters?
opts: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) — measuring ranking quality with position-weighted relevance
AUC-ROC — measuring discrimination between relevant and non-relevant items across thresholds
BLEU — evaluating the quality of generated recommendation descriptions against reference text
F1 score — balancing precision and recall for binary classification of relevant items
questions.explain: NDCG specifically measures ranking quality — it rewards placing highly relevant items earlier in the ranked list, discounting relevance by position. This is the standard metric for recommendation and information retrieval systems where the order of results matters. F1 measures binary classification. AUC-ROC measures discrimination without position weighting. BLEU evaluates text generation.

questions.q: A business intelligence team wants to query data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL without moving or transforming it. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon EMR — to run distributed Spark SQL queries on large S3 datasets
AWS Glue DataBrew — to prepare and transform S3 data before SQL analysis
Amazon Redshift — to load S3 data into a managed data warehouse for SQL querying
Amazon Athena — to run SQL queries directly on data stored in S3 without loading it
questions.explain: Amazon Athena runs SQL queries directly on data in S3 without any data loading, ETL, or infrastructure setup — serverless, pay-per-query. Redshift requires loading data into a warehouse. EMR runs distributed processing requiring cluster management. DataBrew prepares data but doesn't run analytical SQL queries.

questions.q: A team trains a neural network for image classification. During training, the loss decreases rapidly then plateaus despite more epochs. What does this indicate and what should they do?
opts: The learning rate is too high — reduce it to allow the optimizer to find a more precise minimum
The model is overfitting — add more training data or apply regularization techniques
The model has converged — the loss plateau indicates the model has reached its optimal performance given the data and architecture
The model is underfitting — increase model depth and width to improve representational capacity
questions.explain: A loss plateau after rapid initial decrease typically indicates convergence — the model has found a local or global optimum given the current data, architecture, and hyperparameters. The correct next step is to evaluate on validation/test data to determine if the plateau represents a good solution or if architecture changes, more data, or hyperparameter adjustments are warranted.

questions.q: A model trained on historical customer data from 2020-2023 is deployed in 2026. Performance is acceptable initially but degrades after 8 months. What is the MOST likely cause?
opts: The model is overfitting to recent production inputs that differ from the test set
Concept drift — the statistical relationship between features and the target variable has changed over time
The model's context window is saturated by accumulated conversation history in production
Data leakage — production inputs are contaminating the validation baseline used for monitoring
questions.explain: Gradual performance degradation months after deployment is the classic concept drift pattern — the relationship between input features and the target has changed over time (customer behavior, market conditions, external factors) such that the model's learned patterns no longer apply. This differs from data drift (input distribution shift) and overfitting (training vs. validation gap).

questions.q: Which combination of Amazon SageMaker features BEST supports the full MLOps lifecycle from experiment tracking to production monitoring?
opts: SageMaker JumpStart + SageMaker Ground Truth + SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Feature Store + SageMaker Autopilot + SageMaker Neo
SageMaker Canvas + SageMaker Edge Manager + SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Studio + SageMaker Pipelines + SageMaker Model Monitor
questions.explain: Studio provides the integrated development environment, Pipelines automates and orchestrates the ML workflow (CI/CD for ML), and Model Monitor tracks production model performance and data drift. This combination covers the key MLOps pillars: development, automation, and production monitoring. The other combinations miss one or more critical MLOps dimensions.

questions.q: An ML model in production receives inputs with a distribution that has shifted significantly from its training data. Which SageMaker feature detects this automatically?
opts: SageMaker Debugger — monitoring training gradient anomalies indicating distribution sensitivity
SageMaker Pipelines — retraining the model automatically when performance drops below threshold
SageMaker Clarify — detecting bias in production predictions relative to baseline training metrics
SageMaker Model Monitor — detecting data drift by comparing production input distributions to a baseline
questions.explain: SageMaker Model Monitor automatically detects data drift by comparing production input feature distributions against a baseline established from training/validation data. When distributions diverge significantly, it triggers alerts. Clarify detects bias. Debugger monitors training. Pipelines orchestrates workflows but doesn't automatically detect input drift.

questions.q: A healthcare company needs to label 50,000 medical images for model training. The task requires domain expert validation for quality assurance. Which AWS service manages this workflow?
opts: Amazon Mechanical Turk — to distribute labeling tasks to a large workforce without domain validation
Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels — to automatically label images using computer vision
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth — to manage human labeling workflows with built-in quality controls
Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) — to route low-confidence model predictions to human reviewers
questions.explain: SageMaker Ground Truth manages human labeling workflows at scale — including workforce management, labeling task design, automated quality controls, and annotation consolidation across multiple annotators. Rekognition Custom Labels uses existing labels, not human annotation workflows. A2I routes production inference to reviewers. Mechanical Turk is a labor marketplace without built-in ML-specific quality controls.

questions.q: A company wants to enable business users to ask natural language questions about their sales data and receive automated chart visualizations. Which AWS service provides this capability?
opts: Amazon QuickSight with Amazon Q — for natural language BI queries generating automated visualizations
Amazon Kendra — for intelligent search over structured sales database records
Amazon Athena with natural language interface — for SQL generation from plain English queries
Amazon Comprehend — for extracting insights and entities from sales report text documents
questions.explain: Amazon Q in QuickSight is the generative AI assistant in AWS's BI service — it lets business users ask plain language questions and receive dashboards, charts, and AI-written summaries with no SQL knowledge required. Kendra is for enterprise document search. Athena runs SQL. Comprehend analyzes text documents.

questions.q: A company wants to optimize ML model inference cost and latency for deployment on edge devices with limited compute. Which SageMaker capability is MOST relevant?
opts: SageMaker Neo — to compile and optimize ML models for specific hardware targets including edge devices
SageMaker Clarify — to ensure the optimized model maintains fairness metrics after compression
SageMaker Edge Manager — to deploy and monitor models on edge devices after optimization
SageMaker Ground Truth — to improve model quality through better training data labeling
questions.explain: SageMaker Neo compiles ML models for specific hardware targets (ARM, Intel, NVIDIA, Qualcomm) — optimizing inference performance and reducing model size for edge deployment. Edge Manager then deploys and monitors the optimized models on edge devices. Neo addresses the optimization step before Edge Manager handles deployment. Ground Truth handles labeling. Clarify handles bias.

questions.q: A solutions architect needs to choose between Amazon SageMaker Autopilot and a custom SageMaker training job for a tabular classification problem. When should Autopilot be preferred?
opts: When the model requires custom neural network architectures not available in standard libraries
When the training dataset exceeds 100GB and requires distributed training across multiple instances
When maximum model accuracy is the primary requirement and time-to-build is not a constraint
When rapid model development with automated feature engineering and algorithm selection is needed
questions.explain: SageMaker Autopilot automatically handles feature engineering, algorithm selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model evaluation — ideal when rapid model development matters and the data scientist doesn't need to control every step. Custom training jobs provide maximum control but require more implementation time. Autopilot has dataset size limits and may not support custom architectures.

questions.q: Which AWS service enables a company to build a custom conversational AI that understands specific intents and slots defined for their business domain?
opts: Amazon Kendra — to enable intelligent conversational search over enterprise documents
Amazon Transcribe — to convert customer voice inputs to text for processing
Amazon Lex — to build conversational interfaces with custom intent and slot definitions
Amazon Comprehend — to extract domain-specific entities and key phrases from conversations
questions.explain: Amazon Lex builds conversational interfaces with custom intents (user goals) and slots (required information) defined for specific business domains — the same technology powering Alexa. Transcribe converts speech to text. Comprehend extracts NLP features. Kendra enables intelligent search. Only Lex provides the intent/slot modeling for custom conversational AI.

questions.q: A company wants to train an ML model on sensitive patient data without the data leaving their on-premises environment. Which approach BEST meets this requirement?
opts: Use Amazon S3 with server-side encryption to store patient data before sending to SageMaker
Use federated learning — training model weights on local data without centralizing patient records
Use Amazon SageMaker with VPC endpoints to prevent data from traversing the public internet
Use AWS Direct Connect to transfer patient data to SageMaker with dedicated network throughput
questions.explain: Federated learning trains model weights locally on patient data without the data ever leaving the on-premises environment — only gradient updates are shared, not the raw data. S3 encryption and VPC endpoints protect data in transit but still move patient data to AWS. Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity but still transmits data to AWS.

questions.q: A data scientist wants to identify the minimum set of features that explains model predictions to satisfy regulatory explainability requirements. Which SageMaker tool provides this?
opts: Amazon SageMaker Clarify — for feature importance analysis and bias detection in model predictions
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor — for detecting data drift in production model inputs
Amazon SageMaker Experiments — for tracking and comparing model training runs and metrics
Amazon SageMaker Debugger — for monitoring training metrics and identifying anomalies during training
questions.explain: SageMaker Clarify provides SHAP-based feature importance analysis — identifying which features most influence model predictions, meeting regulatory explainability requirements. Debugger monitors training health. Model Monitor detects production drift. Experiments tracks training runs. Only Clarify provides prediction-level feature attribution.

questions.q: A model achieves 97% accuracy on a dataset where 96.5% of samples are negative (non-fraud). What does this indicate about the model's practical usefulness?
opts: The model shows signs of overfitting since accuracy exceeds the dataset's positive rate
The model requires more training data since 97% falls within statistical noise of the baseline
The model is performing well since 97% accuracy exceeds the 96.5% baseline
The model is likely predicting the majority class almost always and barely detecting fraud
questions.explain: A model that always predicts 'not fraud' achieves 96.5% accuracy on this dataset. The model's 97% accuracy is only marginally better and likely detects very little actual fraud. This is the class imbalance trap — high accuracy on imbalanced datasets is misleading. Precision and recall on the positive class are the meaningful metrics.

sections.title: Domain 2: GenAI Fundamentals — Hard
sections.description: Advanced Bedrock · Token economics · Inference parameters · Agentic patterns · Embeddings · Multi-modal

questions.q: A company uses Amazon Bedrock Agents with the ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) pattern. Which description BEST captures what this means in practice?
opts: The agent reacts to user input by selecting the most statistically likely response from its training
The agent alternates between generating reasoning traces and taking actions, using action outcomes to inform subsequent reasoning
The agent reacts to tool call failures by automatically retrying with modified parameters
The agent uses real-time internet access to react to current events before generating responses
questions.explain: ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) is an agentic pattern where the agent interleaves explicit reasoning traces ('I need to check the inventory for this product') with action executions (calling the inventory API), then uses the action results to inform the next reasoning step. This makes agent decision-making more transparent and reliable than black-box tool selection.

questions.q: Amazon Bedrock's pricing model charges separately for input and output tokens. A developer wants to minimize costs for a use case where the system prompt is 2,000 tokens and average user queries are 50 tokens, with responses of 200 tokens. Which optimization has the LARGEST impact?
opts: Enabling prompt caching for the 2,000-token system prompt shared across all requests
Reducing user query length from 50 to 25 tokens through query compression
Switching to a model with lower per-token pricing for the output token rate
Reducing average response length from 200 to 100 tokens through constrained prompting
questions.explain: Total tokens per request = 2,050 input + 200 output. The 2,000-token system prompt is 97.6% of input tokens. Caching it eliminates the dominant cost component for every repeated request. Reducing response length by half saves only 100 output tokens. Compressing queries saves only 25 tokens. Model switching affects all tokens but doesn't target the specific inefficiency. Caching the system prompt has the largest single impact.

questions.q: A company deploys a multi-agent system using Amazon Bedrock where Agent A researches a topic and Agent B writes a report. Agent B's report quality depends entirely on Agent A's research quality. What architectural risk does this represent?
opts: Context pollution — Agent A's research may contaminate Agent B's base instructions
Latency amplification — sequential agents multiply individual agent latency into compounding delays
Single point of failure — Agent A's errors propagate to Agent B with no intermediate validation
Race condition — both agents may access the same knowledge base simultaneously causing conflicts
questions.explain: Error propagation in sequential multi-agent pipelines is the critical architectural risk — Agent A's hallucinations, misinterpretations, or poor-quality research pass unchecked to Agent B, which then produces a confident-sounding report based on flawed inputs. The mitigation is intermediate validation steps, quality checks between agents, or human-in-the-loop review of Agent A's output before it reaches Agent B.

questions.q: An AI agent built with Amazon Bedrock Agents is calling an external API but receiving inconsistent results. The developer finds the agent sometimes calls the wrong action group for the same user intent. What is the MOST likely root cause?
opts: The AWS Lambda functions backing the action groups are experiencing timeouts
The agent's temperature is too high, causing random action group selection
The action group descriptions are ambiguous — the orchestrator cannot reliably determine which to call
The foundation model's context window is exceeded, causing the agent to lose action group definitions
questions.explain: Bedrock Agents uses action group names and descriptions to determine which action to invoke for a given user intent. Ambiguous or overlapping descriptions cause the orchestrator to make incorrect routing decisions. This is the most common Bedrock Agents reliability issue — descriptive, unambiguous action group names are critical for reliable routing. Temperature affects generation but not structured action routing.

questions.q: A developer sets Temperature=0 but still observes slight variations in responses across identical requests to the same Amazon Bedrock model. What is the MOST likely explanation?
opts: Temperature=0 introduces a rounding effect that creates minor variations in deterministic sampling
Model inference on distributed hardware may have floating-point non-determinism across runs
The model's system prompt is being modified between requests by an automated caching system
Top-P is not explicitly set and defaults to a value that overrides Temperature=0 determinism
questions.explain: Even at Temperature=0, distributed GPU inference can exhibit floating-point non-determinism — parallel hardware operations may produce slightly different rounding results across runs. This is a known characteristic of large-scale distributed inference. For strict reproducibility in research settings, exact reproducibility may require identical hardware and seeds. Top-P doesn't override Temperature=0 determinism when Temperature is already 0.

questions.q: A developer notices that an Amazon Bedrock FM application works well for short documents but produces incoherent responses for documents exceeding 50 pages. What is the MOST likely technical cause?
opts: The document exceeds the model's context window limit, causing early content to be dropped
Long documents require fine-tuning to process effectively with foundation models
The vector database's chunk size is too small to represent 50-page documents accurately
The model's maximum output token limit prevents generating responses about long documents
questions.explain: When a document exceeds the model's context window, the beginning of the document is dropped from the context — the model loses information about earlier content. This causes incoherent responses that only reflect the end of the document. Solutions include chunking + RAG (retrieve relevant sections), document summarization, or using a model with a larger context window.

questions.q: Which Amazon Bedrock feature allows developers to test a model's robustness against adversarial prompts before deploying a customer-facing application?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management — for organizing and versioning prompts used in testing
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases — for grounding model responses in verified content
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — for adding content filtering to deployed applications
Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation — for automated and human evaluation including adversarial testing
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation supports automated evaluation including adversarial prompt testing — running the model against test cases designed to elicit harmful, biased, or off-policy responses before deployment. Guardrails adds runtime filtering. Prompt Management organizes prompts. Knowledge Bases grounds responses. Model Evaluation is the pre-deployment testing tool.

questions.q: A developer configures Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and notices that semantically similar queries return different chunks each time. After investigation, the embedding model is correct. What should be investigated next?
opts: The knowledge base's S3 data source is being updated between queries causing index inconsistency
The foundation model's temperature setting is causing variable retrieval behavior
The vector database's approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search has inherent non-determinism
The chunking strategy is splitting related content across chunks, fragmenting semantic coherence
questions.explain: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) algorithms trade exact results for speed — they use probabilistic data structures (HNSW, IVF) that may return slightly different results for identical queries. For strict determinism in retrieval, exact nearest-neighbor search is required but computationally expensive at scale. Temperature affects generation, not retrieval. Chunking and S3 updates are also worth investigating but ANN non-determinism is the most technically precise answer.

questions.q: What distinguishes Amazon Nova models from third-party foundation models available in Amazon Bedrock?
opts: Nova models can only be used for text generation; third-party models support multi-modal inputs
Nova models are Amazon's own family of foundation models with native AWS ecosystem integration
Nova models are free to use; third-party models incur additional per-token charges
Nova models are only available in AWS GovCloud; third-party models are in all commercial regions
questions.explain: Amazon Nova is Amazon's own family of foundation models (Nova Micro, Nova Lite, Nova Pro) built by Amazon — not third-party. They offer native AWS ecosystem integration, competitive pricing, and are available alongside third-party models (Anthropic, Meta, Mistral) in the Bedrock model catalog. Both Nova and third-party models incur per-token charges. Nova models support multimodal inputs.

questions.q: Which Amazon Bedrock inference parameter, when set to 0.1 with temperature at 0, would MOST reliably produce deterministic outputs for a compliance document generation use case?
opts: Top-K set to 1 — restricting selection to only the single highest-probability next token
Max tokens set to 0.1 — reducing output length to near-zero for concise responses
Frequency penalty set to 0.1 — reducing repetition of tokens already generated
Top-P set to 0.1 — limiting the cumulative probability mass to the top 10% of tokens
questions.explain: Top-K=1 combined with Temperature=0 produces fully deterministic outputs — the model always selects the single highest probability token at each step, eliminating all randomness. Top-P=0.1 limits probability mass but can still produce variation. Max tokens is a length limit, not a numeric fraction. Frequency penalty reduces repetition but doesn't create determinism.

questions.q: A developer builds a RAG application and discovers that retrieved chunks are relevant to the query but the generated response ignores the retrieved content. What is the MOST likely cause?
opts: The number of retrieved chunks exceeds the model's context window, causing truncation of retrieved content
The foundation model is fine-tuned on conflicting information that overrides retrieved content
The embedding model's dimensionality is incompatible with the foundation model's input format
The prompt template does not correctly inject the retrieved content into the model's context
questions.explain: If retrieved content isn't properly injected into the prompt template — missing the retrieved chunks section, incorrect formatting, or wrong placement in the context — the model never actually sees the retrieved content and falls back to its parametric knowledge. This is a common RAG implementation error. Context window overflow would cause partial ignoring, not complete ignoring. Fine-tuning conflicts are rare in standard RAG setups.

questions.q: A company processes customer queries where the system prompt is identical for all users and accounts for 80% of total token consumption. Which Amazon Bedrock optimization reduces this cost WITHOUT changing the system prompt?
opts: Using batch inference to process multiple queries together at discounted rates
Switching to a smaller, cheaper foundation model to reduce per-token inference cost
Enabling prompt caching — storing the processed system prompt to reuse across requests
Reducing the max_tokens parameter to limit response length per query
questions.explain: Prompt caching processes the static system prompt once and caches the result — subsequent requests reuse the cached computation, dramatically reducing input token costs when the same system prompt appears in every request. At 80% of tokens being system prompt, this can reduce costs by up to 80%. Model switching may degrade quality. max_tokens affects output, not the repetitive system prompt.

questions.q: A company evaluates two Amazon Bedrock models for a technical support use case. Model X has lower latency but occasionally hallucinates product specifications. Model Y is accurate but 3x slower. The use case serves 500 concurrent users with 2-second SLA. What should guide the selection?
opts: Select Model X — latency SLA compliance takes priority over occasional hallucinations
Evaluate whether Model Y meets the 2-second SLA before accepting Model X's hallucination risk
Select Model Y and scale horizontally with more instances to meet the latency requirement
Test Model X with Bedrock Guardrails grounding checks to validate whether hallucinations are mitigated
questions.explain: The most rigorous approach: test whether Model X's hallucinations are caught by Bedrock Guardrails grounding checks (which verify responses against retrieved knowledge). If Guardrails effectively mitigate the hallucination risk, Model X's latency advantage is preserved. If not, evaluate whether Model Y can meet the 2-second SLA with infrastructure scaling. Neither model should be accepted without addressing both constraints.

questions.q: A developer compares two FM responses: Response A is factually accurate but uses different wording than the reference. Response B matches the reference wording but contains a subtle factual error. Which evaluation metric would incorrectly score Response B higher than Response A?
opts: ROUGE-1 — measuring unigram word overlap between generated and reference text
Human evaluation — using domain expert judgment to assess factual accuracy
G-Eval — using an LLM-as-a-judge to assess response quality and correctness
BERTScore — measuring semantic similarity using contextual embeddings
questions.explain: ROUGE-1 measures surface-level word overlap — a response with matching words but factual errors would score higher than one with accurate content but different wording. This is ROUGE's key limitation: it measures lexical similarity, not semantic accuracy. BERTScore captures semantic meaning, G-Eval assesses quality, and human evaluation catches factual errors that surface metrics miss.

questions.q: A team uses Amazon Titan Embeddings to index product descriptions and a different embedding model for query encoding. Semantic search returns poor results despite good individual embeddings. What is the MOST likely cause?
