questions.explain: The complete voice assistant pipeline: Amazon Transcribe captures and converts user voice questions to text, Amazon Lex understands intent and manages Q&A conversation, Amazon Polly synthesizes spoken responses. Textract processes documents but isn't needed for voice interaction.

questions.q: A company receives insurance claim forms as scanned PDFs. Each form has checkboxes, signature fields, and handwritten damage descriptions. They need to extract all field data including checkbox states. Which service handles this MOST comprehensively?
opts: Amazon Comprehend — to extract claim-related entities from form text content
Amazon Textract — to extract text, checkboxes, and form structure from documents
Amazon Transcribe — to convert any voice notes attached to insurance claims
Amazon Rekognition — to detect and classify form regions including checkboxes
questions.explain: Amazon Textract extracts text, tables, and form data including checkbox selection states from documents — handling the full complexity of insurance form extraction including the AnalyzeDocument API for forms specifically.

questions.q: A company transcribes all sales calls using Amazon Transcribe and wants to identify which competitor products are mentioned in each call. Which AWS service processes the transcripts?
opts: Amazon Lex — to understand competitor-related intents mentioned in sales calls
Amazon Kendra — to search transcripts for competitor product mentions by keyword
Amazon Transcribe custom vocabulary — to add competitor names to the transcription model
Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition — to detect competitor names in transcripts
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition trains a model to identify specific entity types — including competitor product names — from text. Transcribe custom vocabulary improves transcription accuracy but doesn't classify entities. Kendra enables search but doesn't systematically extract entities.

questions.q: A retail company wants to automatically detect whether product images uploaded by sellers contain inappropriate content before publishing. Which AWS service handles this?
opts: Amazon Macie — to scan uploaded images for sensitive personal data
Amazon Textract — to extract product text from uploaded images
Amazon Rekognition — to detect unsafe or inappropriate image content
Amazon Comprehend — to analyze product descriptions for policy violations
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition includes content moderation for images and video — detecting explicit, suggestive, or violent content. Textract extracts text from documents. Comprehend analyzes text. Macie scans S3 for sensitive data like PII, not image content moderation.

questions.q: A company wants to detect when unauthorized vehicles appear in restricted parking zones by recognizing license plates. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Textract — to extract license plate text from camera screenshots
Amazon Rekognition — to detect and analyze text and objects in video feeds
Amazon Comprehend — to process license plate data extracted from camera metadata
Amazon Transcribe — to process any audio from camera microphone feeds
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video — detecting objects, text (including license plates), and activities in real time. Textract extracts structured data from documents. Comprehend analyzes text. Transcribe converts audio.

questions.q: A theme park uses cameras at ride entrances to count how many people are waiting and estimate wait times. Which AWS service analyzes the camera feeds?
opts: Amazon Comprehend — to process queue data reported by ride operators via text
Amazon Rekognition — to detect and count people in real-time camera footage
Amazon Transcribe — to process verbal crowd count announcements from staff
Amazon Textract — to read queue number signs displayed at ride entrances
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition detects and analyzes people in images and video — including counting individuals in frames. This enables real-time queue length estimation from camera feeds. Textract extracts document text. Comprehend analyzes text.

questions.q: A company builds a voice-controlled smart home assistant. When users say 'Turn off the living room lights,' the system must understand the intent, the target, and the location. Which AWS service manages this?
opts: Amazon Lex — to understand the intent and slot values from the command
Amazon Polly — to generate the voice confirmation response to the user
Amazon Transcribe — to convert the spoken command to text for processing
Amazon Comprehend — to extract the entities from the transcribed command
questions.explain: Amazon Lex handles intent recognition (turn off) and slot filling (lights, living room). Transcribe converts speech to text (a prerequisite step). Comprehend extracts general entities. Polly generates voice responses.

questions.q: A company processes support tickets submitted as text and wants to detect when customers are expressing high urgency or distress — flagging tickets that need immediate response. Which AWS service provides this?
opts: Amazon Transcribe — to process any audio recordings attached to tickets
Amazon Lex — to understand the urgency intent expressed in ticket text
Amazon Kendra — to search similar high-urgency tickets from historical data
Amazon Comprehend — to analyze sentiment and detect distress in ticket text
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend performs sentiment analysis detecting negative emotional tone — including urgency and distress — in text, enabling automated routing of high-distress tickets. Lex handles conversational flows. Kendra searches documents.

questions.q: A company builds a retail loss prevention system that needs to detect when someone conceals merchandise under clothing while moving through a store. Which AWS service is MOST relevant?
opts: Amazon Textract — to extract product information from concealed item barcodes
Amazon Comprehend — to analyze security incident reports for concealment patterns
Amazon Rekognition — to detect custom activities and behaviors in video footage
Amazon Transcribe — to process verbal alerts from security staff about suspicious behavior
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels and activity detection can identify specific behaviors in video footage. With training it can detect custom activities. Textract extracts document text. Comprehend analyzes text. Transcribe converts audio.

questions.q: A bank processes loan applications that include handwritten income declarations. The system must read the handwritten figures accurately. Which AWS service handles handwritten text extraction?
opts: Amazon Comprehend — to extract financial figures from processed text
Amazon Textract — to extract handwritten and printed text from document images
Amazon Transcribe — to convert any verbal income declarations to text
Amazon Rekognition — to detect handwriting regions in application images
questions.explain: Amazon Textract extracts both printed and handwritten text from document images — including handwritten form fields. Rekognition detects text regions but Textract handles structured document extraction including handwriting. Comprehend analyzes extracted text.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical company needs to process research papers to extract drug names, adverse effects, and clinical trial outcomes for a regulatory database. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Kendra — for indexing research papers and enabling pharmacist search
Amazon Textract — for extracting text from scanned research paper PDFs
Amazon Comprehend — for general entity extraction from scientific text
Amazon Comprehend Medical — for extracting clinical and pharmaceutical entities
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend Medical extracts medical and pharmaceutical entities including drug names, dosages, adverse effects, and clinical trial outcomes. Regular Comprehend lacks pharmaceutical ontology. Kendra enables search. Textract extracts raw text.

questions.q: A company builds a document search tool for legal researchers. Researchers need to find relevant case law by describing what they're looking for in plain language. Which AWS service enables this?
opts: Amazon Lex — to build a conversational legal research assistant for natural language queries
Amazon Comprehend — to extract legal entities from case law documents for indexing
Amazon Textract — to extract and structure text from scanned legal case documents
Amazon Kendra — to enable intelligent natural language search over indexed legal documents
questions.explain: Amazon Kendra enables intelligent enterprise search with natural language query understanding — researchers can describe what they need and Kendra returns the most relevant case law documents. Comprehend extracts NLP features. Textract extracts text from scanned documents. Lex builds conversational interfaces.

questions.q: A company builds a multilingual customer service chatbot. When a Spanish-speaking customer interacts in Spanish, the bot must understand their intent directly. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Translate the Spanish input to English then use Amazon Lex for intent recognition
Amazon Lex with Spanish language support enabled for direct Spanish intent recognition
Amazon Comprehend to detect Spanish then Amazon Lex to process the translated text
Amazon Transcribe to process Spanish audio then Amazon Translate to convert for Lex
questions.explain: Amazon Lex supports multiple languages natively — you can configure Spanish as a supported language for direct intent recognition without translation. This is simpler, lower latency, and more accurate than translating first. Translate-then-Lex adds unnecessary complexity.

questions.q: A company wants to analyze 50,000 customer reviews to discover the main topics discussed without defining categories in advance. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Comprehend topic modeling to discover latent themes from review text
Amazon Kendra to index reviews and enable search by topic keyword
Amazon Lex to categorize reviews by the intents customers express
Amazon Comprehend sentiment analysis to score positive and negative reviews
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend topic modeling discovers latent themes from unlabeled text automatically without predefined categories. Sentiment analysis scores tone. Kendra enables search. Lex handles conversational intents.

questions.q: A company's customer service team reads emails in 8 different languages. They want all incoming emails automatically converted to English before agents review them. Which AWS service handles this?
opts: Amazon Translate — to convert email text from any language to English
Amazon Polly — to generate English audio versions of foreign language emails
Amazon Comprehend — to detect the language of each incoming email before processing
Amazon Transcribe — to process any audio attachments in the emails
questions.explain: Amazon Translate converts text between languages — translating emails to English automatically. Comprehend detects language and extracts insights but doesn't translate. Transcribe converts audio. Polly generates audio from text.

questions.q: A financial services company receives thousands of customer complaint emails daily. They want to score each email as positive, negative, or neutral and route high-negative emails to senior agents. Which AWS service provides this?
opts: Amazon Transcribe — to process any voice complaints in the email attachments
Amazon Lex — to understand the intent behind each customer complaint
Amazon Comprehend — to analyze email sentiment and classify emotional tone
Amazon Kendra — to search historical complaint emails for similar cases
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend provides sentiment analysis — classifying text as positive, negative, neutral, or mixed. Lex handles conversational flows. Kendra searches documents. Transcribe converts audio.

questions.q: A company wants to build a system where customers can call a number, speak their order naturally, and the order is processed automatically. Which combination of AWS services is required?
opts: Amazon Polly to capture the call audio then Amazon Comprehend to extract order items
Amazon Transcribe to convert speech then Amazon Textract to extract order structure
Amazon Transcribe to convert speech to text then Amazon Lex to understand intent and collect order items
Amazon Rekognition to process call metadata then Amazon Translate to normalize order language
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts customer speech to text, then Amazon Lex understands the ordering intent and uses slot filling to collect items and quantities through a conversational flow. Polly generates voice responses. Textract processes documents.

questions.q: A company wants to help agents find answers from a 50,000-article knowledge base using natural language questions and receive direct synthesized answers, not a list of links. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon OpenSearch Service — for full-text keyword search across the knowledge base
Amazon Comprehend — for extracting key entities from knowledge base articles automatically
Amazon Lex — for building a Q&A bot that queries the knowledge base by keyword
Amazon Kendra — for intelligent enterprise search with natural language Q&A and answer synthesis
questions.explain: Amazon Kendra provides intelligent enterprise search with natural language Q&A — indexing documents and synthesizing direct answers. OpenSearch requires query expertise and provides keyword search. Comprehend extracts NLP features. Lex builds conversational interfaces.

questions.q: A streaming platform wants to automatically detect and flag scenes containing violence or adult content in user-uploaded videos before they go live. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Rekognition — to detect inappropriate content in video frames automatically
Amazon Transcribe — to identify inappropriate dialogue in video audio tracks
Amazon Comprehend — to analyze video titles and descriptions for inappropriate content signals
Amazon Textract — to extract content warnings from video metadata fields
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition content moderation detects inappropriate visual content (explicit, suggestive, violence) in images and video frames. Comprehend analyzes text. Textract extracts document text. Transcribe analyzes audio — for audio content moderation Transcribe would detect dialogue, but the question asks about visual content in video frames.

questions.q: A media company produces video content and wants to automatically generate caption files for all their videos to meet accessibility requirements. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Lex — to understand video dialogue and generate structured caption data
Amazon Polly — to generate accessibility-friendly audio descriptions of video content
Amazon Rekognition — to detect spoken words and scenes in video for caption generation
Amazon Transcribe — to convert video audio to timestamped text for captions
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts audio from videos to timestamped text transcripts which can be formatted into caption files. It supports subtitle file export directly. Polly generates audio. Rekognition analyzes visual content.

questions.q: A travel company wants to analyze social media posts mentioning their brand to understand whether sentiment is improving or declining week-over-week. Which AWS service provides this at scale?
opts: Amazon Kendra — to search and index brand mentions across social platforms
Amazon Comprehend — to perform sentiment analysis on collected social text
Amazon Rekognition — to analyze images in social media posts for brand content
Amazon Lex — to build a bot that monitors and responds to brand mentions
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend performs sentiment analysis on text at scale — classifying each post and enabling trend tracking over time. Kendra searches indexed content. Rekognition analyzes images. Lex builds conversational interfaces.

questions.q: A logistics company scans thousands of delivery waybills daily. Each waybill has printed fields for sender name, recipient address, weight, and tracking number. They need to extract these fields automatically. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Comprehend — to extract named entities from waybill text content
Amazon Textract — to extract structured key-value pairs from document forms
Amazon Transcribe — to convert any handwritten annotations to digital text
Amazon Rekognition — to detect and read text regions in waybill images
questions.explain: Amazon Textract extracts structured data from forms — identifying key-value pairs from document images. Rekognition can detect text but Textract is purpose-built for structured document extraction. Comprehend analyzes already-extracted text. Transcribe converts audio.

questions.q: A company with global customers wants to detect the language of each incoming support email before routing it to the correct regional team. Which AWS service identifies the source language?
opts: Amazon Lex — which identifies the language of conversational inputs automatically
Amazon Transcribe — which detects the language of audio before transcription
Amazon Translate — which detects source language as part of its translation process
Amazon Comprehend — which provides language detection as a standalone capability
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend provides language detection — identifying the dominant language of text with confidence scores. While Translate also detects language, Comprehend provides this as a standalone feature without requiring translation. This is the cleaner answer for email routing.

questions.q: A company receives job applications as PDF resumes and wants to extract candidate names, email addresses, years of experience, and educational institutions. Which service first makes the PDF content processable?
opts: Amazon Lex — to build a resume parsing bot that extracts structured information
Amazon Rekognition — to detect and read text sections from resume PDF images
Amazon Textract — to extract text and structure from resume PDF documents
Amazon Comprehend — to identify named entities from resume text directly
questions.explain: Amazon Textract extracts text from PDF documents — converting resume content to processable text. Comprehend then identifies entities from the extracted text. Textract is the primary service for PDF text extraction. Rekognition handles general images, not structured PDF extraction.

questions.q: A company processes medical dictation recordings from radiologists. The transcriptions must use correct medical terminology for imaging studies, anatomical terms, and findings. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Transcribe — with custom vocabulary for radiology terms added
Amazon Transcribe Medical — purpose-built for clinical speech recognition accuracy
Amazon Comprehend Medical — for extracting radiology findings from dictation text
Amazon Lex — for building a structured radiology report input interface
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe Medical is purpose-built for clinical speech recognition — trained on medical language and dictation patterns with higher accuracy for clinical content than standard Transcribe. Comprehend Medical extracts entities from already-transcribed text. Custom vocabulary helps but Transcribe Medical has deeper medical language optimization.

questions.q: A company wants to help customer service agents by automatically summarizing long email threads before agents respond. The summaries should capture key issues and prior actions taken. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Kendra — to search the email thread for the most important messages
Amazon Bedrock with a foundation model — to generate abstractive email thread summaries
Amazon Textract — to extract text from email attachments included in the thread
Amazon Comprehend — to extract key entities and sentiment from email thread content
questions.explain: Abstractive summarization — generating a coherent summary capturing key issues and actions — requires a generative AI foundation model through Amazon Bedrock. Comprehend extracts entities and sentiment but doesn't generate summaries. Kendra searches documents.

questions.q: A company wants to extract data from thousands of financial statements and annual reports in PDF format to populate a research database. Which service is MOST appropriate for the initial text extraction step?
opts: Amazon Textract — to extract text, tables, and structured data from financial PDF documents
Amazon Kendra — to index financial reports and enable analyst search by financial metric
Amazon Comprehend — to identify financial entities and key metrics directly from PDFs
Amazon Rekognition — to detect and read financial data from annual report document images
questions.explain: Amazon Textract extracts text and structured data (tables with financial figures) from PDF documents — the essential first step before any downstream analysis. Comprehend analyzes extracted text. Rekognition handles general images. Kendra enables search of indexed content.

questions.q: A law firm receives contracts in PDF format and needs to identify all instances of specific legal clauses, party names, and effective dates across thousands of documents. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Rekognition — to detect and read text regions in PDF document images
Amazon Kendra — to enable search for specific clauses across indexed contracts
Amazon Textract — to extract text from PDF contracts for downstream processing
Amazon Comprehend with custom entity recognition — to identify legal-specific entities
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition trains a model to identify domain-specific entities (legal clause types, party roles) that general NLP doesn't recognize. Kendra enables search. Textract extracts raw text (a prerequisite). Rekognition handles images.

questions.q: A publishing company wants to create audiobook versions of their entire catalog of 10,000 books in multiple voice styles. Which AWS service provides this at scale?
opts: Amazon Transcribe — to process existing audiobook recordings for quality enhancement
Amazon Lex — to build interactive audiobook experiences with chapter navigation
Amazon Polly — to synthesize natural-sounding speech from book text at scale
Amazon Translate — to convert book text to audio-compatible phonetic format
questions.explain: Amazon Polly converts text to lifelike speech with multiple voice options and speaking styles — exactly what large-scale audiobook production requires. Transcribe converts audio to text. Lex builds conversational interfaces.

questions.q: A company's contact center wants to automatically assess customer emotional state during support calls so supervisors can intervene when frustration escalates. Which sequence is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Transcribe to convert call audio to text then Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis
Amazon Rekognition to analyze caller video then Amazon Comprehend for emotion detection
Amazon Lex to understand call intent then Amazon Translate to normalize emotional language
Amazon Polly to generate call audio then Amazon Comprehend to detect emotional tone
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts live or recorded call audio to text, then Amazon Comprehend performs sentiment analysis to detect negative or escalating emotional tone. Polly generates audio. Rekognition analyzes visual content.

questions.q: A content platform generates written articles and wants to add audio versions for podcast listeners. Which AWS service creates natural-sounding audio from article text?
opts: Amazon Polly — to synthesize natural-sounding speech from article text
Amazon Translate — to convert article text to audio-compatible formats
Amazon Transcribe — to process existing audio files and generate article transcripts
Amazon Lex — to create an interactive audio reading experience for listeners
questions.explain: Amazon Polly converts text to lifelike speech synthesis. Transcribe converts audio TO text (opposite direction). Lex builds conversational interfaces. Translate converts between languages.

questions.q: A hospital wants to process doctor notes to automatically extract patient diagnoses, medications, and dosage information. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
opts: Amazon HealthLake — for storing and querying medical records at scale
Amazon Comprehend — for general entity extraction from medical text
Amazon Transcribe Medical — for converting dictated notes to text
Amazon Comprehend Medical — for extracting clinical entities from medical text
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend Medical extracts clinical entities — diagnoses, medications, dosages, procedures — from medical text. Regular Comprehend lacks medical ontology. Transcribe Medical converts speech to text. HealthLake stores FHIR records.

questions.q: A multinational call center handles calls in 15 languages. They need to transcribe all calls AND detect the language spoken automatically. Which AWS service handles both?
opts: Amazon Translate with language detection followed by Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Transcribe with automatic language identification enabled
Amazon Comprehend for language detection followed by Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Lex with multilingual support for all 15 languages simultaneously
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe supports automatic language identification — detecting the spoken language and transcribing accordingly in a single service call. Translate handles text translation. Comprehend detects language in text after transcription. Lex builds conversational interfaces.

questions.q: A news website publishes articles in English and wants to automatically publish them in French, German, and Japanese simultaneously. Which AWS service handles this?
opts: Amazon Polly — to generate multilingual audio versions of each article
Amazon Translate — to convert article text between languages automatically
Amazon Lex — to build multilingual conversational interfaces for each market
Amazon Comprehend — to detect the source language and prepare text for translation
questions.explain: Amazon Translate converts text between languages — translating articles to multiple languages efficiently. Comprehend detects language but doesn't translate. Polly generates audio from text. Lex builds conversational bots.

questions.q: A company records all customer support calls and wants to make them searchable by keyword. Which AWS service converts the recordings to searchable text?
opts: Amazon Transcribe — to convert recorded audio to text transcripts
Amazon Comprehend — to extract key phrases from call recordings
Amazon Lex — to understand the intent of each support call
Amazon Polly — to generate audio summaries of call content
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts audio recordings to text. Lex builds conversational interfaces. Polly converts text TO audio (opposite direction). Comprehend analyzes text — but text must exist first, meaning Transcribe runs before Comprehend can process call content.

questions.q: A retail bank wants to process customer feedback surveys to understand whether satisfaction scores correlate with specific topics mentioned. They need both sentiment and entity extraction from a single service. Which AWS service provides both?
opts: Amazon Rekognition — for analyzing any images submitted with survey feedback
Amazon Lex — for understanding customer intent and entity extraction from surveys
Amazon Comprehend — for sentiment analysis and entity recognition from survey text
Amazon Kendra — for indexing survey responses and enabling topic-based search
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend provides multiple NLP capabilities from a single service — sentiment analysis, entity recognition, key phrase extraction, and topic modeling. No additional service is needed.

questions.q: A government agency scans thousands of paper forms from citizens. Each form has printed fields like Name, Date of Birth, and Address that need to be digitized into a database. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Rekognition — to identify and read text fields in scanned form images
Amazon Comprehend — to extract personal information entities from form content
Amazon Textract — to extract key-value pairs from structured form documents
Amazon Transcribe — to convert any voice recordings attached to form submissions
questions.explain: Amazon Textract is purpose-built for extracting key-value pairs from forms — identifying field names and their corresponding values from structured documents. Rekognition handles general image analysis. Comprehend analyzes unstructured text.

questions.q: A company stores 5 years of customer service call recordings in S3. A compliance team needs to find calls where specific regulatory disclosures were not made. Which sequence identifies non-compliant calls?
opts: Amazon Transcribe to convert recordings to text then Amazon Comprehend to detect missing disclosure phrases
Amazon Lex to replay calls through intent recognition then Amazon Translate to normalize compliance language
Amazon Polly to regenerate call audio then Amazon Textract to extract spoken content as text
Amazon Rekognition to analyze call recordings then Amazon Kendra to search for disclosure gaps
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts historical call recordings to text transcripts, then Amazon Comprehend (or custom classification) analyzes each transcript to detect whether required disclosure phrases are present or absent. Rekognition handles visual content. Kendra searches indexed documents.

questions.q: A company scans expense receipts submitted by employees. They need to extract merchant name, date, total amount, and individual line items from each receipt image. Which service handles this MOST accurately?
opts: Amazon Textract — to extract text, tables, and structured data from receipt documents
Amazon Lex — to build a receipt submission bot that collects expense information
Amazon Rekognition — to detect and read text regions from receipt images
Amazon Comprehend — to extract financial entities like amounts from receipt text
questions.explain: Amazon Textract extracts structured data from receipts — including tables (line items), key-value pairs (merchant name, date, total) — with the AnalyzeExpense API specifically for receipts. Rekognition handles general image analysis. Comprehend analyzes extracted text.

questions.q: A company wants to moderate comments on their platform in 12 different languages, detecting toxic or offensive content regardless of language. Which approach is MOST scalable?
opts: Use Amazon Rekognition content moderation extended to analyze text across languages
Build 12 separate Amazon Comprehend custom classifiers, one per language
Use Amazon Translate to convert all comments to English then Amazon Comprehend for moderation
Use Amazon Bedrock with a multilingual foundation model for cross-language content moderation
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock multilingual foundation models perform content moderation across languages in a single model without translation. Building 12 separate classifiers is expensive. Translate-then-Comprehend adds latency and translation errors. Rekognition handles image and video content, not text.

questions.q: A company receives audio messages from customers in a mobile app. Before storing them, the company needs to check if any audio contains PII like names or account numbers. Which sequence is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Rekognition to scan audio files then Amazon Macie to classify PII content
Amazon Transcribe to convert audio to text then Amazon Comprehend to detect PII entities
Amazon Polly to regenerate audio without PII then Amazon Textract to verify removal
Amazon Lex to process audio content then Amazon Translate to normalize PII terms
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts audio to text, then Amazon Comprehend detects PII entities (names, account numbers, phone numbers) in the transcript. Rekognition analyzes visual content. Macie scans S3 data at rest for files already stored.

questions.q: A company wants to build a customer service chatbot that understands when a customer says 'I want to check my order' and asks follow-up questions to collect the order number. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Transcribe — to convert customer voice messages to text for processing
Amazon Lex — to define the order checking intent and collect order number as a slot
Amazon Kendra — to search order documentation based on customer queries
Amazon Comprehend — to extract the order checking intent from customer messages
questions.explain: Amazon Lex defines intents (check order) and slots (order number) — building a conversational flow that asks follow-up questions to collect required information. Comprehend extracts entities from text but doesn't manage conversation flows.

questions.q: A company uses Amazon Rekognition to moderate user profile pictures. The system flags an image as unsafe but a human reviewer determines it is acceptable. How should the company handle this pattern systematically?
opts: Adjust Amazon Rekognition confidence threshold to reduce false positive detections broadly
Switch to Amazon Textract to analyze image metadata rather than visual content
Retrain Amazon Rekognition with the falsely flagged image as a negative example
Use Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) to route flagged images to human reviewers before rejection
questions.explain: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) is purpose-built for human-in-the-loop review of ML predictions — routing flagged outputs to human reviewers before action is taken. This creates a systematic review workflow. Threshold adjustment reduces sensitivity broadly for all users.

questions.q: A company uses cameras at its warehouse to verify that workers are wearing required safety equipment like hard hats and safety vests. Which AWS service enables this?
opts: Amazon Transcribe — to process supervisor verbal safety equipment checks
Amazon Textract — to extract safety equipment checklist data from warehouse documents
Amazon Comprehend — to analyze safety incident reports for equipment compliance patterns
Amazon Rekognition — to detect personal protective equipment in camera images
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition includes PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) detection — identifying whether individuals in images or video are wearing required safety equipment like hard hats, safety vests, and face masks.

questions.q: A company uses Amazon Comprehend to analyze customer reviews. They want to understand specifically which product features receive positive vs. negative sentiment. Which Comprehend capability addresses this?
opts: Comprehend topic modeling to cluster reviews by the features mentioned
Comprehend targeted sentiment to analyze sentiment toward specific entities
Comprehend custom classification to categorize reviews by feature type
Comprehend key phrase extraction to identify frequently mentioned feature terms
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend targeted sentiment analyzes sentiment toward specific entities — determining whether 'battery life' received positive sentiment while 'screen brightness' received negative sentiment in the same review. Topic modeling clusters by theme. Key phrase extraction identifies important terms.

questions.q: A company produces video tutorials and wants to generate both text transcripts AND translated subtitles in Spanish and Portuguese. Which sequence of AWS services achieves this?
opts: Amazon Rekognition to extract text then Amazon Translate to convert to target languages
Amazon Transcribe to generate transcripts then Amazon Translate to translate to target languages
Amazon Lex to process video dialogue then Amazon Comprehend to generate translated summaries
Amazon Polly to generate audio then Amazon Translate to convert to target languages
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts video audio to text transcripts, then Amazon Translate converts transcripts to Spanish and Portuguese. This is the standard subtitle pipeline. Polly generates audio. Rekognition analyzes visual content.

sections.title: AI, ML and Deep Learning — Core Definitions
sections.description: Domain 1 fundamentals · Definitions · Terminology · Short options · No dashes

questions.q: Which term describes the process of using a trained ML model to make predictions on new data?
opts: Training
Fine tuning
Inference
Evaluation
questions.explain: Inference is the process of using a trained model to generate predictions or outputs on new data. Training is the process of learning patterns from data. Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model. Evaluation measures model quality on test data.

questions.q: A company has labeled historical records showing which loan applications were approved and rejected. They want to predict whether new applications will be approved. Which ML type applies?
opts: Reinforcement learning
Transfer learning methods
Supervised learning
Unsupervised learning
questions.explain: Supervised learning trains on labeled data (applications with known approval outcomes) to predict labels for new inputs. The presence of labeled historical examples and a goal of predicting a known target are the hallmarks of supervised learning.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST describes the relationship between AI, machine learning, and deep learning?
opts: AI is the broadest field, machine learning is a subset of AI,...
Deep learning is the broadest field containing machine...
They are three separate unrelated fields that use similar...
Machine learning is the broadest field containing AI which...
questions.explain: AI is the broadest field. Machine learning is a subset of AI where systems learn from data. Deep learning is a subset of ML using multi-layered neural networks. The relationship is: AI → ML → Deep Learning (nested subsets).

questions.q: A system processes text, images, and audio using layers of artificial neurons to recognize complex patterns. Which technology is this?
opts: Rules based AI systems
Standard machine learning
Expert system programs
Deep learning
questions.explain: Deep learning uses multi-layered neural networks (many layers of artificial neurons) to learn complex patterns from unstructured data like text, images, and audio. Traditional ML uses simpler algorithms. Expert systems use hand-coded rules.

questions.q: A company wants a system that learns patterns from historical data and improves its predictions as it receives more examples. Which technology approach applies?
opts: Rules based programming
Machine learning systems
Expert system programs
Deterministic algorithms
questions.explain: Machine learning trains systems that learn patterns from data and improve with more examples — the defining characteristic that distinguishes it from rule-based programming where rules are explicitly coded.

questions.q: Which statement BEST describes how machine learning differs from traditional programming?
opts: Rules based systems learn from data while ML uses explicit rules
ML uses data and examples to learn rules; rules based uses rules plus data
ML always outperforms rules based approaches
Machine learning always requires more storage space
questions.explain: Traditional programming: rules + data = answers. Machine learning: data + answers (labeled examples) = rules (a model). ML discovers the rules from examples rather than having them explicitly coded. Accuracy comparison depends on the use case, not the approach.

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of machine learning over manually coded rule-based systems for complex tasks?
opts: ML discovers patterns too complex to code manually and adapts...
ML is always cheaper to build and maintain long term
ML always runs faster than rules based systems
Machine learning eliminates the need for any human...
questions.explain: ML discovers patterns from data that would be impossible or impractical to manually define as rules — especially for complex tasks like recognizing faces, understanding language, or detecting fraud in millions of transactions. It also adapts when retrained on new data.

questions.q: A company's AI system generates new marketing copy, images, and product descriptions it has never seen before. Which type of AI does this represent?
opts: Generative AI
Supervised learning
Reinforcement learning
Discriminative AI
questions.explain: Generative AI creates new content (text, images, code, audio) rather than just classifying or predicting from existing data. It is built on deep learning foundation models trained on vast datasets to learn patterns they can then generate novel content from.

sections.title: ML Types — Supervised vs Unsupervised vs Reinforcement
sections.description: Most tested Domain 1 topic · Classify any scenario instantly · No dashes

questions.q: An AI agent plays a video game, receives points when it wins, and loses points when it fails. Over millions of games it learns an optimal strategy. Which ML type is this?
opts: Supervised learning
Unsupervised learning
Transfer learning methods
Reinforcement learning
questions.explain: Reinforcement learning trains an agent that takes actions in an environment and learns through reward signals (points for winning, penalties for losing) without labeled examples. The agent learns through trial and error to maximize cumulative reward.

questions.q: An e-commerce company wants to identify unusual purchase patterns that might indicate credit card fraud without having seen all possible fraud patterns. Which ML approach is MOST appropriate?
opts: Supervised classification
Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised anomaly detection
Supervised regression
questions.explain: Unsupervised anomaly detection identifies statistical outliers without requiring labeled fraud examples. Since fraud patterns evolve and all variations cannot be labeled in advance, unsupervised approaches generalize better. Supervised classification requires comprehensive labeled fraud examples.

questions.q: A company wants to group their 5 million customers into segments based on purchasing behavior without defining the segments in advance. Which ML type applies?
opts: Semi supervised learning
Unsupervised learning
Supervised learning
Reinforcement learning
questions.explain: Unsupervised learning works with unlabeled data to discover hidden structure such as clusters. No predefined segments or labeled examples are needed — the algorithm finds natural groupings. Supervised learning requires labeled data with known target outcomes.

questions.q: A self-driving car learns to navigate by receiving positive feedback when it reaches the destination safely and negative feedback when it violates traffic rules. Which ML type is this?
opts: Reinforcement learning
Supervised learning
Unsupervised learning
Semi supervised learning
questions.explain: Reinforcement learning trains an agent to take actions in an environment to maximize cumulative reward — positive feedback for safe navigation, negative for violations. There are no labeled training examples of correct driving decisions.

questions.q: A company wants to predict the exact dollar amount of next quarter's revenue from historical financial data. Which ML problem type is this?
opts: Binary classification
Clustering
Reinforcement learning
Regression
questions.explain: Regression predicts a continuous numerical value (exact revenue amount). Binary classification predicts one of two categories. Clustering groups unlabeled data. Reinforcement learning uses reward-based trial and error.

questions.q: A security team has no examples of network attacks but wants a system that flags traffic patterns significantly different from normal. Which ML approach applies?
opts: Supervised regression
Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised anomaly detection
Supervised classification
questions.explain: Unsupervised anomaly detection identifies patterns that deviate significantly from normal without requiring labeled attack examples. Supervised approaches require labeled examples of both normal and attack traffic. Reinforcement learning uses reward signals.

questions.q: A hospital wants to automatically flag patient test results as 'normal' or 'abnormal' using 10 years of labeled historical results. Which ML type applies?
opts: Anomaly detection
Supervised learning
Unsupervised learning
Reinforcement learning
questions.explain: Supervised learning trains on labeled historical data (results with known normal/abnormal labels) to classify new results. Labeled examples and a predefined target (binary classification) are the key indicators of supervised learning.

questions.q: A company has images of products with labels indicating whether each is defective or not. They want to train a model to classify new product images. Which ML type applies?
opts: Supervised classification
Unsupervised clustering
Reinforcement learning
Anomaly detection
questions.explain: Supervised classification trains on labeled examples (images with defective/not-defective labels) to classify new inputs. Labeled data and a predefined categorical target are the indicators of supervised classification.

questions.q: A model predicts house prices based on square footage, number of bedrooms, and location from thousands of historical sales records with known prices. Which ML problem type is this?
opts: Binary classification
Clustering
Anomaly detection
Regression
questions.explain: Regression predicts a continuous numerical value (house price). The labeled historical sales data (with known prices as the target) and the continuous output value are the indicators of supervised regression.

questions.q: A company analyzes product reviews and wants to identify the main topic categories that customers discuss without defining the categories in advance. Which ML approach applies?
opts: Regression analysis
Reinforcement learning
Unsupervised topic modeling
Supervised classification
questions.explain: Unsupervised topic modeling discovers latent themes from unlabeled text without predefined categories. Supervised classification requires labeled examples of each category. Regression predicts continuous values. Reinforcement learning uses reward signals.

sections.title: Data Types, Model Concepts and ML Lifecycle
sections.description: Data structures · Overfitting · Underfitting · Train/test split · ML lifecycle stages

questions.q: After a model is deployed, its prediction error gradually increases over 3 months as customer behavior changes. Which ML lifecycle activity addresses this?
opts: Model deployment
Feature engineering
Business problem framing
Model monitoring and retraining
questions.explain: Model monitoring detects performance degradation after deployment and triggers retraining on recent data to restore model quality. The ML lifecycle is iterative — models require ongoing monitoring and maintenance, not just a one-time deployment.

questions.q: Which type of data includes emails, social media posts, customer reviews, images, and audio recordings with no predefined organizational format?
opts: Relational data
Metadata
Unstructured data
Structured data
questions.explain: Unstructured data has no predefined format or schema — text, images, audio, video, social media posts. Most real-world data is unstructured. Deep learning and NLP techniques are typically needed to extract patterns from unstructured data.

questions.q: Which type of data is BEST described as organized in rows and columns with predefined fields such as customer ID, age, and purchase amount?
opts: Streaming data
Structured data
Unstructured data
Semi structured data
questions.explain: Structured data is organized in tables with predefined schemas (rows and columns) — databases, CSV files, spreadsheets. Unstructured data has no predefined format (images, audio, text documents). Semi-structured data has some organization but not strict schema (JSON, XML).

questions.q: A company splits their dataset into training, validation, and test sets. What is the PRIMARY purpose of the held-out test set?
opts: To detect data drift after the model is deployed to production
To tune hyperparameters during training iterations
To provide additional training examples for complex models
To give an unbiased final performance estimate before deployment
questions.explain: The test set provides an unbiased final estimate of model performance on completely unseen data before deployment. The validation set is used for hyperparameter tuning during development. The test set must never be seen during training or model selection.

questions.q: A model achieves 58% accuracy on training data and 57% accuracy on test data. Both scores are well below acceptable performance. What does this indicate?
opts: Overfitting
Data poisoning
Concept drift
Underfitting
questions.explain: Underfitting occurs when a model cannot learn meaningful patterns from training data — it performs poorly on both training and test data (similar low scores). Overfitting shows a large gap between training and test performance.

questions.q: A team is preparing data for ML training and removes duplicate records, fills in missing values, and corrects formatting errors. Which stage of the ML lifecycle is this?
opts: Business problem framing
Data preparation and feature engineering
Model evaluation
Model deployment
questions.explain: Data preparation (also called data preprocessing or data cleaning) involves removing duplicates, handling missing values, correcting errors, and transforming raw data into a usable format for model training. This is one of the most time-consuming lifecycle stages.

questions.q: A model trained on data from January to December performs well in testing but degrades significantly in production 6 months later. What is the MOST likely cause?
opts: Concept drift from real world pattern changes after training
Data leakage in the original test set
Overfitting to training data
Model underfitting
questions.explain: Concept drift occurs when real-world data distributions change over time after a model is deployed — patterns the model learned no longer reflect current reality. Retraining on recent data addresses concept drift. Overfitting would show immediately at test time.

questions.q: A feature in the training dataset directly encodes the target variable, causing the model to score 100% accuracy on test data but fail completely in production. What occurred?
opts: Data leakage
Overfitting
Concept drift
Underfitting
questions.explain: Data leakage occurs when information from the target variable (or future data) is inadvertently included in the training features — producing unrealistically high evaluation scores that don't reflect true production performance.

questions.q: A model achieves 99% accuracy on training data but only 61% accuracy on test data. What does this indicate?
opts: Underfitting
Data leakage from training
Overfitting
Good generalization
questions.explain: Overfitting occurs when a model performs much better on training data than on unseen test data — it has memorized training patterns rather than learning generalizable rules. The large gap (99% vs 61%) is the signature of overfitting.

questions.q: A company collects raw transaction records into Amazon S3, applies transformations to remove PII and create aggregated features, then uses the result for training. Which two stages of the ML lifecycle does this represent?
opts: Model deployment then monitoring
Business framing then model training
Data collection then data preparation
Model training then model evaluation
questions.explain: Collecting raw data into S3 is the data collection stage. Applying transformations, removing PII, and creating aggregated features is the data preparation and feature engineering stage. These are the first two data-focused stages of the ML lifecycle.

sections.title: ML Evaluation Metrics — Precision, Recall and Beyond
sections.description: When to use which metric · Imbalanced datasets · Regression metrics · No dashes

questions.q: A model predicts whether loan applicants will default. The team must compare overall model discrimination ability across all possible classification thresholds. Which metric applies?
opts: F1 score
Precision
AUC ROC score
Recall
questions.explain: AUC-ROC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve) measures a model's ability to discriminate between classes across all classification thresholds — useful for comparing classifiers overall independent of a specific threshold choice.

questions.q: An ML team wants a single metric that balances both precision and recall equally for evaluating a model on an imbalanced dataset. Which metric provides this?
opts: AUC ROC score
MAE
F1 score
Accuracy
questions.explain: F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall — it balances both metrics and is preferred over accuracy for imbalanced datasets. AUC-ROC evaluates discrimination across all thresholds. MAE is for regression. Accuracy is misleading on imbalanced data.

questions.q: A company trains two models for customer churn prediction. Model A: precision=0.91, recall=0.42. Model B: precision=0.68, recall=0.89. The company loses $200 for each churned customer not identified and $5 for each false alarm. Which model should they deploy?
opts: Model A — precision above 0.90 is the industry standard for...
Model B — but only after retraining to improve precision...
Model A — higher precision reduces costly false alarms
Model B — higher recall catches more churning customers at...
questions.explain: Missing a churning customer costs $200 while a false alarm costs $5 — false negatives are 40x more expensive. Model B's high recall (0.89) catches far more churning customers at a manageable false alarm cost. The cost structure strongly favors high recall over high precision.

questions.q: A dataset contains 97% negative examples and 3% positive examples. A model predicts negative for every input and achieves 97% accuracy. What is the PRIMARY problem with using accuracy to evaluate this model?
opts: Accuracy should only be computed on the validation set not...
97% accuracy is too low for production use
Accuracy is only valid for balanced datasets above 10%...
Accuracy is misleading on imbalanced datasets — the model...
questions.explain: Accuracy is misleading on imbalanced datasets — a model predicting the majority class always achieves high accuracy without learning anything useful. On imbalanced datasets, precision, recall, and F1 score provide meaningful evaluation of the minority class performance.

questions.q: A company's email spam filter incorrectly classifying legitimate emails as spam costs $50 per incident while missing actual spam costs $2. Which metric should the team prioritize improving?
opts: Recall — to catch more spam
Accuracy — to maximize overall correct classifications
Precision — to reduce false spam flags on legitimate emails
F1 score — to balance catching spam and avoiding false flags
questions.explain: False positives (legitimate emails flagged as spam) cost $50 while false negatives (missed spam) cost $2 — false positives are 25x more expensive. Precision measures how many flagged items are truly positive — improving precision reduces costly false alarms.

questions.q: A cancer screening model tests 500 patients. 50 actually have cancer. The model correctly identifies 40 of the 50. What is the model's recall?
questions.explain: Recall = true positives / (true positives + false negatives) = 40 / (40 + 10) = 40/50 = 80%. Recall measures the proportion of actual positives correctly identified — minimizing missed detections.

questions.q: A disease detection model must catch as many actual cases as possible even if it flags some healthy patients. The cost of missing a disease is far greater than unnecessary follow-up tests. Which metric should be maximized?
opts: F1 score
Recall
Precision
Accuracy
questions.explain: Recall maximizes the proportion of actual cases correctly detected (minimizing false negatives). When missing a positive (failing to detect disease) is far more costly than false alarms, recall is the priority metric. Precision minimizes false alarms.

questions.q: A company trains a regression model to predict house prices. The model's predictions are sometimes $5,000 too high and sometimes $5,000 too low. Which metric quantifies this average prediction error?
opts: Mean Absolute Error
Precision
F1 score
Recall
questions.explain: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) measures the average magnitude of prediction errors — the average of |predicted - actual| across all examples. Lower MAE indicates smaller average prediction errors. Precision, recall, and F1 are for classification tasks, not regression.

questions.q: A fraud detection model flags 100 transactions as fraudulent. 80 are actually fraudulent and 20 are legitimate. What is the model's precision?
questions.explain: Precision = true positives / (true positives + false positives) = 80 / (80 + 20) = 80/100 = 80%. Precision measures how many of the flagged items are actually positive — minimizing false alarms.

questions.q: A team evaluates two models on a fraud dataset with 1% fraud rate. Model A achieves 99% accuracy. Model B achieves 95% accuracy but catches 90% of actual fraud cases. Which model is MORE appropriate for deployment?
opts: Model B — catches far more actual fraud despite lower overall...
Model A — because the dataset is imbalanced favoring higher...
Model B — but only if precision is also above 90%
Model A — higher overall accuracy means better performance
questions.explain: Model B catches 90% of actual fraud (high recall) which is the business objective. Model A likely predicts 'not fraud' always, achieving 99% accuracy on an imbalanced dataset while catching little actual fraud. On imbalanced datasets, recall (and F1) on the minority class matter far more than overall accuracy.

sections.title: GenAI Fundamentals — Tokens, Embeddings, Hallucination, RAG
sections.description: Domain 2 basics · Core GenAI vocabulary · How LLMs work · No dashes

questions.q: A developer adds 'Think through this step by step before answering' to their prompt and notices the model's reasoning quality improves significantly on complex problems. Which technique is this?
opts: Few shot prompting
Zero shot prompting
Negative prompting
Chain of thought prompting
questions.explain: Chain-of-thought prompting elicits explicit step-by-step reasoning before the final answer — proven to significantly improve accuracy on complex multi-step reasoning tasks. Few-shot provides examples. Zero-shot provides only the task. Negative prompting specifies what to avoid.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST describes what a token is in the context of large language models?
opts: A discrete unit such as a character or word that LLMs process...
A unique identifier assigned to each training example in the...
A mathematical weight parameter updated during model training
A security credential for authenticating API calls to LLM...
questions.explain: Tokens are the discrete units LLMs process — approximately 4 characters or 0.75 words in English. Vendors price API calls by input and output token count. A typical sentence is 15-25 tokens. Pricing, context window limits, and costs are all measured in tokens.

questions.q: A developer notices that changing one word in a prompt from 'summarize' to 'explain' significantly changes the LLM's response quality. What does this demonstrate?
opts: A bug in the LLM's tokenization system
Evidence that the model requires fine tuning
Model overfitting to specific vocabulary
The importance of prompt engineering in guiding LLM output
questions.explain: Prompt engineering — carefully crafting the input to an LLM — significantly influences output quality. LLMs are sensitive to exact wording, context, and instruction framing. Choosing precise verbs, tone, and structure directly shapes the model's response.

questions.q: Which inference parameter controls the randomness and creativity of an LLM's output — with higher values producing more varied responses and lower values producing more consistent predictable outputs?
opts: Temperature
Max tokens
Top K parameter
Top P parameter
questions.explain: Temperature controls output randomness. Temperature=0 produces the most deterministic consistent outputs (same input → same output). Higher temperature produces more varied creative outputs. Max tokens controls response length. Top-K and Top-P also control diversity but temperature is the primary and most commonly tested control.

questions.q: A developer includes 3 example input-output pairs in a prompt to show the model how to format its response before asking the actual question. Which technique is this?
opts: Zero shot prompting
Chain of thought prompting
Negative prompting
Few shot prompting
questions.explain: Few-shot prompting includes labeled examples within the prompt to demonstrate the desired input-output pattern — the model calibrates its output format and style from these examples. Zero-shot provides no examples. Chain-of-thought elicits step-by-step reasoning.

questions.q: A company's LLM gives a confident detailed answer about a recent court ruling that never actually happened. What is this called?
opts: Underfitting
Hallucination
Data poisoning
Bias
questions.explain: Hallucination is when an LLM generates confident factually incorrect responses — making up information that sounds plausible. It occurs when the model fills gaps in its training data with invented content rather than admitting uncertainty.

questions.q: A model converts words and sentences into numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning so that similar concepts are positioned close together in vector space. What are these numerical representations called?
opts: Embeddings
Weights
Tokens
Parameters
questions.explain: Embeddings are numerical vector representations that capture semantic meaning — similar concepts have vectors close together in the embedding space. 'Car' and 'automobile' have similar embeddings. They enable semantic search, similarity comparison, and RAG retrieval. Tokens are input units. Parameters and weights are model components.

questions.q: A company's LLM generates harmful content about violence and illegal activities because similar content appeared in its internet training data. Which responsible AI risk does this represent?
opts: Toxic content generation
Model inversion
Data poisoning
Prompt injection
questions.explain: Toxic content generation occurs when an LLM reproduces offensive, harmful, or illegal content learned from its training data. This is a key responsible AI risk requiring content filters, guardrails, and training-time safety measures like RLHF to mitigate.

questions.q: An LLM answers questions about events from two years ago accurately but cannot answer questions about events from last month. What is the MOST likely cause?
opts: The model is overfitting to older training examples
The model has too few parameters to store recent knowledge
The model's training data has a cutoff date and lacks recent...
The context window is too small to process recent event...
questions.explain: LLMs have a knowledge cutoff date — the date after which their training data ends. Events after this cutoff are unknown to the model unless provided via RAG or fine-tuning. Context window size affects how much text the model can process at once, not its knowledge cutoff.

questions.q: A company wants their LLM to answer questions about their internal product documentation without retraining the model. They store documents and retrieve relevant sections at query time. Which technique is this?
opts: RLHF
Prompt caching
Retrieval Augmented Generation
Fine tuning
questions.explain: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant external documents at query time and provides them as context to the LLM — enabling current knowledge responses without model retraining. Fine-tuning updates model weights. RLHF aligns model behavior with human preferences. Prompt caching reduces repeat processing costs.

Amazon Comprehend

questions.q: A publishing company wants to automatically generate captions files for 5,000 video tutorials to meet accessibility requirements. Which service is used first in this pipeline?

Amazon Polly

questions.q: A company wants to build a customer service chatbot that collects customer name, account number, and issue type through a natural conversation before routing to an agent. Which service handles this?

Amazon Kendra

questions.q: A bank needs to extract structured data including names, dates, amounts, and table data from thousands of scanned loan application forms. Which service handles this?

questions.q: A retail company wants to analyze 100,000 product reviews to determine whether each review is positive, negative, or neutral. Which service provides this?

questions.q: A company wants to detect objects, read license plates, and identify unauthorized vehicles in parking lot camera footage in real time. Which service applies?

Amazon Textract

questions.q: A company wants to route incoming support emails to one of 8 departments automatically using a model trained on 10,000 labeled historical emails. Which service requires the LEAST custom development?

Kendra searches documents but doesn't classify. Bedrock FM inference per email is expensive at scale for classification tasks.

questions.q: A global company receives customer emails in 20 different languages and wants them automatically converted to English before agents review them. Which service handles this?
opts: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Translate
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Lex

questions.q: A media company wants to create audio versions of their written news articles for podcast listeners. Which service handles this?
opts: Amazon Translate
Amazon Polly
Amazon Lex
Amazon Transcribe
questions.explain: Amazon Polly converts text to natural-sounding speech. Transcribe converts speech to text (opposite direction). Translate converts between languages. Lex builds conversational chatbots.

questions.q: A telehealth platform records doctor-patient consultations and needs to convert audio to text while preserving clinical accuracy for medical terminology. Which service is MOST appropriate?

Amazon Polly
Amazon Transcribe Medical
Amazon Transcribe
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe Medical is purpose-built for clinical speech recognition with higher accuracy for medical terminology, drug names, and clinical language. Standard Transcribe handles general audio. Comprehend Medical extracts clinical entities from already transcribed text. Polly generates audio.

Amazon Kinesis

Amazon Athena

questions.q: A media streaming company wants to show each user a personalized list of movies they are likely to enjoy based on their viewing history and ratings. Which service is purpose-built for this recommendation use case?

Amazon Forecast
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Kendra

questions.q: A company needs to give all 800 employees access to an AI assistant that answers questions from internal company wikis, HR policy documents, and project documentation with each employee only seeing content they are permitted to access. Which service is purpose-built for this?

Amazon Kendra
Amazon SageMaker
Amazon Q Business

questions.q: A company needs to run SQL queries on 5 years of training log files stored in Amazon S3 without building or managing any database infrastructure. Which service provides this?

Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon Athena

questions.q: A company needs to automatically extract, transform, and load data from 6 different relational databases into Amazon S3 on a nightly schedule before ML training begins. Which service handles this ETL pipeline?

sections.title: SageMaker Services — Tricky Scenarios

SageMaker Ground Truth
SageMaker Feature Store
SageMaker Autopilot

SageMaker Clarify

SageMaker Model Monitor

questions.q: An ML team wants to reuse the same customer features like purchase frequency and average order value across 5 different models without recomputing them each time. Which SageMaker feature centralizes feature management?

SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Feature Store

SageMaker Clarify

SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Model Monitor

questions.q: A company deploys a credit card fraud model. 3 months later the team notices the model's false positive rate has doubled. They want an automated system that would have detected this degradation and triggered a retraining alert. Which SageMaker feature provides this?

SageMaker Model Monitor
SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Debugger

sections.title: Security and Compliance — Round 3
sections.description: Trickier security scenarios · Service names only · No dashes

questions.q: A company's SOC team wants automatic detection when an IAM role that normally only accesses SageMaker suddenly starts making API calls to EC2, RDS, and Lambda at 2 AM. Which service detects this behavioral change?
opts: AWS Config
Amazon Macie
Amazon Inspector
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explain: Amazon GuardDuty uses ML to detect unusual behavioral patterns including unexpected service access, unusual times, and anomalous API call volumes. Config monitors configurations. Macie discovers sensitive data. Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities.

questions.q: A company has 300 employees who all need the same set of SageMaker permissions. The security team wants a single policy change to update permissions for all 300 simultaneously without touching individual users. Which IAM construct enables this?
opts: IAM Policies
IAM Groups
IAM Users
IAM Roles
questions.explain: IAM Groups allow a single policy to be assigned once and automatically apply to all member users. Updating the group policy updates permissions for all 300 simultaneously. IAM Roles provide temporary credentials for services. IAM Policies are the permission documents. IAM Users are individual identities.

questions.q: A company wants all API traffic between their VPC and Amazon Bedrock to stay on the AWS private network and never traverse the public internet. Which AWS networking feature enables this?
opts: AWS Managed VPN Service
AWS PrivateLink
AWS Direct Connect
Amazon CloudFront
questions.explain: AWS PrivateLink creates a VPC interface endpoint routing all Amazon Bedrock API traffic through the AWS private network. Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity from on-premises to AWS. CloudFront is a CDN. Site-to-Site VPN encrypts traffic between on-premises and AWS over the internet.

questions.q: A regulated bank must demonstrate to external regulators that its AWS environment meets ISO 27001 information security standards. The regulator requires official certification documents not internal reports. Which AWS service provides these?
opts: AWS Artifact
AWS Audit Manager
AWS Config
AWS CloudTrail
questions.explain: AWS Artifact provides official third-party auditor compliance reports and certifications including ISO 27001, SOC 2, and PCI DSS that can be shared with external regulators. Audit Manager assesses customer workload compliance. Config monitors configurations. CloudTrail provides operational logs.

questions.q: A company's Bedrock application EC2 backend was found to have an outdated TLS library with a known critical CVE. The security team wants automated scanning to catch similar issues across all inference servers going forward. Which service provides this?
opts: Amazon Macie
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
questions.explain: Amazon Inspector automatically scans EC2 instances and containers for software vulnerabilities including outdated libraries with known CVEs. Macie discovers sensitive data in S3. GuardDuty detects behavioral threats. Config monitors resource configurations.

questions.q: An ML engineer is investigated for data exfiltration. Legal needs to know every S3 object they accessed, when they accessed it, and from which IP address over the past 180 days. Which service provides this forensic evidence?
opts: AWS Config
Amazon Macie
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explain: AWS CloudTrail logs every API call with the caller's IAM identity, exact timestamp, source IP address, and resources accessed providing comprehensive forensic evidence. GuardDuty detects anomalies. Config tracks configurations. Macie classifies sensitive data.

questions.q: A company needs to prove to a HIPAA auditor that their SageMaker endpoints, S3 training buckets, and IAM configurations all comply with specific HIPAA technical safeguard controls. Which service generates the compliance evidence report?
opts: AWS Config
AWS Audit Manager
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon Inspector
questions.explain: AWS Audit Manager has pre-built HIPAA framework support automatically collecting evidence from CloudTrail, Config, and IAM and mapping it to HIPAA controls generating audit-ready assessment reports. CloudTrail provides raw logs. Inspector scans vulnerabilities. Config monitors configurations.

questions.q: A company migrates from long-lived IAM user access keys to a more secure authentication pattern for their ML training jobs running on EC2. Which IAM construct eliminates the need for stored long-lived credentials?
opts: IAM Roles
IAM Groups
IAM Policies
IAM Users
questions.explain: IAM Roles provide temporary security credentials that are automatically issued and expire — EC2 instances assume a role through the instance metadata service with no stored access keys. IAM Groups manage user permissions. IAM Policies define permissions. IAM Users have permanent long-lived credentials.

questions.q: A company processes sensitive genomic data in S3 for ML research. They need continuous automated scanning to ensure no patient identifiers, SSNs, or insurance IDs are stored in any of their 200 research buckets. Which service provides this?
opts: AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Inspector
Amazon Macie
questions.explain: Amazon Macie uses ML and pattern matching to continuously scan S3 buckets and automatically alert when sensitive data including patient identifiers, SSNs, and insurance IDs is detected. Config monitors configurations. GuardDuty detects behavioral threats. Inspector scans compute workloads.

questions.q: A company runs ML training on sensitive patient data. After training, the security team discovers the training bucket was accessible to all authenticated AWS users for 72 hours due to a misconfigured bucket policy. Which service would have detected and remediated this automatically?
opts: Amazon Macie
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explain: AWS Config continuously monitors resource configurations against defined rules and can automatically remediate non-compliant configurations like overly permissive bucket policies. GuardDuty detects behavioral threats. Macie discovers sensitive data content. CloudTrail logs the change but does not remediate.

sections.title: Data Services and Full Mix — Round 3
sections.description: All categories mixed · Service names only · No dashes · Balanced options

questions.q: A news streaming service wants to show each subscriber a personalized news feed ranked by what stories they are most likely to read based on their reading history. Which service generates these personalized recommendations?
opts: Amazon Forecast
Amazon Kendra
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Personalize
questions.explain: Amazon Personalize generates real-time personalized content rankings and recommendations based on individual user behavior history. Forecast predicts time-series values. Kendra enables document search. Comprehend performs NLP analysis.

questions.q: A company needs to ingest customer purchase events from 50 retail stores in real time, enrich each event with product metadata, and trigger fraud alerts within 2 seconds of suspicious patterns. Which service handles the real-time stream?
opts: Amazon Redshift
Amazon Athena
Amazon Kinesis
AWS Glue
questions.explain: Amazon Kinesis processes high-volume real-time streaming data enabling enrichment and processing within seconds of event arrival. Glue handles batch ETL. Redshift is a warehouse for batch analytics. Athena queries static S3 data.

questions.q: A biotech company has genomic datasets spread across 15 S3 buckets and 4 database systems. Research teams need to discover what data is available, understand its lineage, and request access to specific datasets. Which service provides the unified data catalog and governance layer?
opts: Amazon Redshift
AWS Lake Formation
Amazon Macie
Amazon Athena
questions.explain: AWS Lake Formation provides centralized data lake management with unified cataloging, data lineage, and fine-grained access control across S3 and database sources. Macie discovers sensitive data. Athena queries S3 data. Redshift is a data warehouse.

questions.q: A data team needs to run complex SQL analytics on 3 years of ML training logs stored in S3 without loading them into any database and without provisioning any servers. Which service provides this?
opts: Amazon Athena
Amazon Redshift
Amazon RDS
Amazon Kinesis
questions.explain: Amazon Athena runs serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data with no infrastructure provisioning or data loading required. Redshift requires data to be loaded into a warehouse. RDS is a managed relational database. Kinesis handles real-time streaming.

questions.q: A company wants a single AI assistant where every employee from HR to engineering can ask questions about internal company knowledge including policies, project documentation, and engineering runbooks, with role-based content filtering. Which service is purpose-built for this?
opts: Amazon Bedrock
Amazon SageMaker
Amazon Kendra
Amazon Q Business
questions.explain: Amazon Q Business is purpose-built for enterprise AI assistance with native connectors to enterprise content sources and identity-aware access controls ensuring each user only sees authorized content. Bedrock requires custom pipeline development. SageMaker handles ML model building. Kendra provides search without the full AI assistant and access control layer.

questions.q: A company needs to move clickstream data from 5 web applications, transform it by removing PII and normalizing timestamps, and load it into Amazon S3 every 3 hours for downstream ML training. Which service handles this?
opts: Amazon Athena
Amazon Redshift
AWS Glue
Amazon Kinesis
questions.explain: AWS Glue is the fully managed ETL service that extracts from multiple sources, applies transformations including PII removal and normalization, and loads to S3 on a scheduled basis. Kinesis handles real-time streaming. Athena queries existing S3 data. Redshift is a data warehouse.

questions.q: A company's DevOps team of 200 engineers needs an AI assistant that understands their codebase, can generate infrastructure-as-code, explain AWS CLI commands, and detect security issues in pull requests all within their IDE. Which service is purpose-built for this?
opts: Amazon SageMaker
Amazon Q Developer
Amazon Q Business
Amazon Bedrock
questions.explain: Amazon Q Developer is the AI coding assistant purpose-built for developers providing code generation, IaC generation, CLI explanation, security scanning, and codebase-aware assistance integrated directly into developer IDEs. Q Business handles enterprise knowledge Q&A. Bedrock requires custom IDE integration. SageMaker handles ML model development.
