questions.q: An airline needs to predict passenger demand for each of 500 routes over the next 90 days to optimize pricing and crew scheduling, incorporating seasonality, holidays, and historical booking patterns. Which service handles this?
opts: Amazon Forecast
Amazon Personalize
Amazon Kendra
Amazon Comprehend
questions.explain: Amazon Forecast is purpose-built for time-series demand forecasting incorporating seasonality, holidays, and related time series automatically. Personalize generates recommendations for individual users. Kendra searches documents. Comprehend analyzes text.

questions.q: A company's executives want to ask their business intelligence tool questions like 'What caused our Q3 revenue dip?' and receive an automatically generated analysis with charts without any SQL knowledge. Which service provides this?
opts: Amazon Kendra
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Athena
Amazon QuickSight
questions.explain: Amazon QuickSight with Amazon Q provides natural language BI queries generating automatic analysis charts and AI-written narrative explanations. Kendra searches documents. Comprehend analyzes text. Athena runs SQL queries on S3 data.

questions.q: A company builds a semantic search engine for job postings. Each job description must be converted to a vector embedding and stored for nearest neighbor retrieval when candidates search by skill or role description. Which service stores and queries these vectors?
opts: Amazon RDS
Amazon Redshift
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Amazon DynamoDB
questions.explain: Amazon OpenSearch Service natively supports vector storage and approximate nearest neighbor ANN search enabling semantic similarity queries at scale. DynamoDB, RDS, and Redshift are not designed for vector ANN search workloads.

sections.title: NLP and Vision — Tricky Service Pairs
sections.description: Rekognition vs Textract vs Comprehend vs Transcribe · Confirmed exam traps

questions.q: A company wants to read the text printed on road signs and product labels in photos taken by field inspectors. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Textract
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Transcribe
questions.explain: Text in natural scenes (signs, labels on products) → Amazon Rekognition DetectText. Textract is for structured document text. This is the confirmed Rekognition vs Textract exam trap.

questions.q: A company scans thousands of insurance claim forms and needs to extract claimant name, policy number, and claim amount from each form. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Textract
questions.explain: Structured text in documents and forms → Amazon Textract. Textract extracts key-value pairs, tables, and form fields. Rekognition reads text in natural scenes not structured form fields.

questions.q: A company wants to detect when customers sound angry during phone support calls recorded as audio files. Which two services in order achieve this?
opts: Amazon Polly then Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition then Amazon Textract
Amazon Transcribe then Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Lex then Amazon Kendra
questions.explain: Transcribe converts audio to text first. Comprehend then analyzes the text for sentiment. Polly converts text to audio (wrong direction).

questions.q: A logistics company needs to verify delivery driver identity by comparing their face in a live camera feed against a database of registered employee photos. Which service handles this?
opts: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Textract
Amazon Comprehend
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition SearchFacesByImage compares detected faces against a collection for identity matching. Textract extracts documents. Comprehend analyzes text. Transcribe converts audio.

questions.q: A hospital processes clinical notes in text format and needs to extract all mentions of medications, dosages, and diagnoses for a pharmacovigilance study. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Textract
Amazon Transcribe Medical
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Comprehend Medical
questions.explain: Comprehend Medical extracts clinical entities from text including medications, dosages, diagnoses. Transcribe Medical converts audio to text — not needed here since notes are already text.

questions.q: A media company uploads videos to S3 and needs to automatically generate captions for accessibility compliance. Which service creates timestamped transcripts from video audio?
opts: Amazon Textract
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Polly
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts video audio to timestamped text transcripts formattable as captions. Polly converts text to audio (opposite direction). Textract extracts text from documents not video audio.

questions.q: A retail company receives customer reviews in Spanish, German, Japanese, and English. They want to analyze sentiment of all reviews without translating them first. Which service handles multilingual sentiment natively?
opts: Amazon Translate
Amazon Polly
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Lex
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend performs sentiment analysis supporting multiple languages natively. Translate converts between languages — a separate step not needed here. Polly converts text to audio. Lex builds conversational interfaces.

questions.q: A manufacturing company has safety cameras at warehouse exits. They want to detect when workers leave without wearing hard hats and high-visibility vests. Which service provides PPE detection?
opts: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Textract
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition includes built-in PPE detection specifically for safety compliance — identifying hard hats, vests, safety glasses in images and video.

questions.q: A company wants to build a voice customer service chatbot that understands commands, collects account number and issue type through conversation, then routes to the right team. Which combination is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Transcribe then Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Polly then Amazon Kendra
Amazon Rekognition then Amazon Textract
Amazon Transcribe then Amazon Lex
questions.explain: Transcribe converts voice to text. Lex understands intent, collects information through slot filling, and routes calls. Lex manages the full conversational flow — Comprehend extracts insights but does not manage conversation or routing.

questions.q: A company wants to convert 50,000 product description texts into audio files in 12 languages for a podcast platform. Which service handles text-to-audio conversion?
opts: Amazon Lex
Amazon Kendra
Amazon Polly
Amazon Transcribe
questions.explain: Amazon Polly converts text to natural-sounding speech in dozens of languages. Transcribe converts audio TO text (opposite direction). Lex builds conversational interfaces. Kendra provides enterprise search.

questions.q: A company receives employee expense reports as handwritten forms and needs to extract vendor name, date, amount, and category into their accounting system. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Textract
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition
questions.explain: Amazon Textract extracts handwritten and printed text from forms including key-value pairs. The AnalyzeExpense API is specifically for receipts and expense forms.

questions.q: A company needs to detect PII such as SSNs, credit card numbers, and email addresses within scanned documents. Which service handles the text extraction step from scanned images?
opts: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Textract
questions.explain: Textract first extracts text from scanned documents. Comprehend then detects PII in the extracted text. Rekognition analyzes images for objects not PII in documents.

sections.title: SageMaker Services — Tricky Distinctions
sections.description: Clarify vs Monitor vs Debugger vs A2I vs Ground Truth · Confirmed exam traps

questions.q: A loan approval model produces lower approval rates for a specific demographic group despite identical financial profiles. The data science team wants to quantify this disparity. Which SageMaker feature should they use?
opts: SageMaker Model Monitor
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Experiments
questions.explain: SageMaker Clarify detects bias measuring disparate impact across demographic subgroups. Model Monitor detects production data drift. Debugger monitors training anomalies. Experiments tracks training run comparisons.

questions.q: A deployed churn prediction model was accurate at launch but performance degraded over 6 months as customer behavior changed. The team wants automatic alerts when this happens. Which SageMaker feature detects this?
opts: SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Ground Truth
SageMaker Model Monitor
questions.explain: SageMaker Model Monitor continuously monitors production model inputs and outputs detecting data drift and quality degradation over time. Clarify detects bias. Ground Truth manages labeling. Debugger monitors anomalies DURING training not production.

questions.q: A company needs to label 80,000 X-ray images as showing pneumonia or not before training a diagnostic model. Which SageMaker feature manages this human labeling workflow?
opts: SageMaker Model Monitor
Amazon Augmented AI
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Ground Truth
questions.explain: SageMaker Ground Truth manages human labeling workflows for TRAINING data. A2I routes PRODUCTION predictions for human review. Ground Truth is for labeling before training. A2I is for reviewing predictions after deployment.

questions.q: A radiology AI predicts tumor probability from scans. Hospital protocol requires predictions below 85% confidence to be reviewed by a radiologist before adding to the patient record. Which service implements this?
opts: SageMaker Ground Truth
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Model Monitor
Amazon Augmented AI
questions.explain: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) routes PRODUCTION ML predictions to human reviewers based on confidence thresholds. Ground Truth labels TRAINING data. Clarify detects bias. Model Monitor detects production drift. A2I is specifically for human review of live production inferences.

questions.q: An ML engineer training a deep neural network wants to detect vanishing gradients and exploding gradients in real time during the training run. Which SageMaker feature provides this?
opts: SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Model Monitor
questions.explain: SageMaker Debugger captures and analyzes training tensors in real time detecting gradient anomalies DURING training. Model Monitor detects production drift. Clarify detects bias. Experiments tracks run comparisons after training.

questions.q: A company publishes documentation about a deployed fraud detection model including intended use, performance metrics across demographic groups, and known limitations for regulatory review. Which SageMaker feature creates this?
opts: SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Model Monitor
SageMaker Model Cards
SageMaker Clarify
questions.explain: SageMaker Model Cards is the governance artifact capturing intended use, training data characteristics, performance metrics, known limitations, and out-of-scope applications. Clarify detects bias. Experiments tracks training runs. Model Monitor tracks production drift.

questions.q: A business analyst with no ML experience needs to build a customer lifetime value prediction model using transaction data without involving the data science team. Which SageMaker feature enables this?
opts: SageMaker Canvas
SageMaker Pipelines
SageMaker Studio
SageMaker Autopilot
questions.explain: SageMaker Canvas provides a no-code visual interface for non-technical business users. Studio is an IDE for data scientists requiring coding. Autopilot generates technical notebooks requiring ML knowledge. Pipelines orchestrates ML workflows with code.

questions.q: A data science team runs 200 training experiments varying learning rate, batch size, and layer count. They need to compare accuracy across all runs and reproduce the best configuration exactly. Which SageMaker feature manages this?
opts: SageMaker Canvas
SageMaker Pipelines
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Experiments
questions.explain: SageMaker Experiments tracks metrics, hyperparameters, and artifacts across all training runs enabling comparison and reproducibility. Canvas is for no-code users. Pipelines orchestrates workflows. Debugger monitors anomalies during individual runs.

questions.q: A company's ML features are recomputed differently for each model causing inconsistencies between training and inference. Which SageMaker feature centralizes feature management?
opts: SageMaker Ground Truth
SageMaker Feature Store
SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Data Wrangler
questions.explain: SageMaker Feature Store centralizes feature management — compute once, reuse across models with online (real-time) and offline (batch) stores ensuring training and production consistency.

questions.q: A company needs to automatically tune learning rate, regularization, and epochs for their SageMaker training job to maximize validation accuracy. Which SageMaker feature provides automated hyperparameter optimization?
opts: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Experiments
questions.explain: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning automatically searches the hyperparameter space using Bayesian optimization. Debugger monitors training anomalies. Clarify detects bias. Experiments tracks run comparisons but requires manual configuration per run.

questions.q: A company needs ML model predictions from an endpoint in under 200ms for a mobile app where users submit individual requests and wait for responses. Which SageMaker inference type meets this requirement?
opts: SageMaker Serverless Inference
SageMaker Real Time Endpoint
SageMaker Batch Transform
SageMaker Asynchronous Inference
questions.explain: SageMaker Real-Time Endpoints provide persistent low-latency inference for interactive applications. Batch Transform processes large offline datasets. Asynchronous handles large payloads without immediate response. Serverless may have cold-start delays.

questions.q: A company wants to process 2 million customer records in S3 overnight using a SageMaker model to generate recommendations with no real-time requirement. Which inference type is MOST cost-effective?
opts: SageMaker Real Time Endpoint
SageMaker Serverless Inference
SageMaker Asynchronous Inference
SageMaker Batch Transform
questions.explain: SageMaker Batch Transform processes large datasets from S3 without a persistent endpoint — most cost-effective for offline workloads. Real-Time Endpoints require persistent infrastructure. Serverless scales for intermittent interactive traffic.

sections.title: Bedrock and GenAI Services — Tricky Distinctions
sections.description: Guardrails vs Prompts vs Agents vs Knowledge Bases · Confirmed exam traps

questions.q: A company wants to offer transparency into their deployed ML model decision-making processes to regulators. Which AWS service creates this governance documentation?
opts: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
Amazon Lex
Amazon Rekognition
questions.explain: SageMaker Model Cards document model details, intended use, performance metrics, and risk considerations for responsible AI governance. This exact question is confirmed from real exam candidates.

questions.q: A company wants private access to Amazon Bedrock APIs so data never travels over the public internet. Which AWS feature achieves this?
opts: AWS PrivateLink VPC interface endpoint
AWS WAF
AWS Shield Advanced
Amazon CloudFront
questions.explain: AWS PrivateLink creates a VPC interface endpoint routing Bedrock API traffic through the AWS private network — data never touches the public internet.

questions.q: A developer using Amazon Bedrock generates marketing copy but outputs are too creative and factually inconsistent. Which parameter adjustment makes outputs more deterministic?
opts: Decrease temperature
Increase Top P
Increase max tokens
Increase Top K
questions.explain: Lower temperature makes the model more deterministic and focused. This exact scenario is confirmed as a real AIF-C01 exam question.

questions.q: A company wants to detect bias in their custom ML recommendation model during training and evaluation. Which AWS service is designed specifically for this purpose?
opts: Amazon Q Developer
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
Amazon SageMaker Clarify
Amazon Rekognition
questions.explain: SageMaker Clarify detects and explains bias in ML models during training. Bedrock Guardrails prevents harmful outputs at inference time — not for detecting bias in custom ML training.

questions.q: AWS publishes a document for their pre-built sentiment analysis service describing its intended use cases, limitations, and responsible AI practices. What type of document is this?
opts: Bedrock Model Evaluation report
AWS AI Service Card
SageMaker Clarify report
SageMaker Model Card
questions.explain: An AWS AI Service Card is published by AWS for pre-built AI services describing intended use, limitations, and responsible AI practices. A Model Card is published by the MODEL DEVELOPER for a trained model.

questions.q: A company's Bedrock chatbot blocks legitimate product questions because the grounding threshold is set to 0.80 causing accurate paraphrased responses to be incorrectly blocked. What is the fix?
opts: Run the knowledge base sync after the latest S3 updates
Raise the threshold to block more unsafe outputs
Rebuild the vector database index
Lower the grounding threshold to reduce false positive blocks
questions.explain: A threshold of 0.80 blocks accurate responses that paraphrase using different words. Lowering the threshold reduces false positive blocks. This is threshold miscalibration not hallucination.

questions.q: A company needs to identify whether their Bedrock foundation model produces different quality responses for different demographic groups. Which service measures this disparity?
opts: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
Amazon SageMaker Clarify
Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
questions.explain: SageMaker Clarify measures bias metrics across demographic subgroups. Bedrock Guardrails filters content. Bedrock Model Evaluation compares FM quality on datasets. Model Monitor tracks production drift.

questions.q: A company uses Amazon Bedrock and wants to log every complete conversation including full prompts and responses for compliance. Which destination does Bedrock invocation logging send this data to?
opts: Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon S3
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon CloudWatch Logs
questions.explain: Bedrock invocation logging sends complete conversation content to Amazon S3. CloudTrail captures API metadata not full conversation content. DynamoDB is not a Bedrock invocation logging destination.

questions.q: Which AWS service makes foundation models from multiple providers available through a single API so developers can build and scale generative AI applications?
opts: Amazon Bedrock
AWS Lambda
Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
Amazon EC2 with GPU instances
questions.explain: Amazon Bedrock provides a fully managed service making foundation models from leading AI providers available through a single API. This exact question is confirmed from real exam reports.

questions.q: A company needs intelligent enterprise search for employees to search internal HR and legal documentation using natural language questions and receive direct synthesized answers. Which service is purpose-built for this?
opts: Amazon Kendra
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Amazon OpenSearch Service
questions.explain: Amazon Kendra provides intelligent enterprise search with natural language understanding and direct answer synthesis. Bedrock Knowledge Bases provides RAG retrieval for FM applications requiring custom pipeline development.

questions.q: A company wants Amazon Lex combined with Amazon Bedrock for their customer service chatbot. Which statement about this combination is correct?
opts: Lex handles conversation flow while Bedrock provides the generative AI intelligence
Bedrock replaces Lex entirely when used for customer service
Comprehend must be added between Lex and Bedrock for intent detection
SageMaker is required as middleware between Lex and Bedrock
questions.explain: Lex handles the conversation flow — intent recognition, slot filling, dialogue management. Bedrock provides the generative FM intelligence behind the responses. This is a confirmed real exam question.

questions.q: A company wants to block all competitor product discussions from their Bedrock chatbot reliably regardless of how the query is phrased. Which Bedrock feature achieves this?
opts: Bedrock Prompt Management
Bedrock Model Evaluation
Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Bedrock Guardrails
questions.explain: Bedrock Guardrails denied topics blocks subject areas at the infrastructure layer independent of model instruction following — cannot be bypassed through prompt injection.

sections.title: Security and Data Services — Tricky Distinctions
sections.description: CloudTrail vs Config vs GuardDuty vs Macie vs Forecast vs Personalize · Service names only

questions.q: A CISO needs to prove to a HIPAA auditor that their Bedrock application AWS controls map to HIPAA technical safeguards with automated evidence collection. Which service provides this?
opts: AWS Audit Manager
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon Inspector
AWS Config
questions.explain: AWS Audit Manager has pre-built HIPAA framework support automatically collecting evidence and mapping to HIPAA controls. CloudTrail provides raw API logs. Inspector scans vulnerabilities. Config monitors configurations.

questions.q: A company needs a complete forensic record of every S3 bucket accessed, every SageMaker API called, and every IAM action taken using compromised access keys. Which service provides this?
opts: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon CloudWatch
questions.explain: AWS CloudTrail logs every API call with the exact IAM identity, timestamp, source IP, and action taken — the complete forensic record for incident investigation.

questions.q: A company wants continuous automated scanning of ML training data S3 buckets to detect unencrypted social security numbers, credit card numbers, and PII. Which service provides this?
opts: AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Inspector
Amazon Macie
questions.explain: Amazon Macie uses ML to continuously scan S3 and automatically detect sensitive data including PII and financial data. Config monitors configurations. GuardDuty detects behavioral threats. Inspector scans EC2 not S3 object content.

questions.q: A company's training S3 bucket was accidentally made publicly readable. They want automatic detection and remediation of such misconfigurations going forward. Which service provides this?
opts: Amazon Macie
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explain: AWS Config continuously monitors resource configurations against compliance rules and can auto-remediate violations using Systems Manager Automation. GuardDuty detects behavioral threats. Macie discovers sensitive data. CloudTrail logs changes but does not auto-remediate.

questions.q: A company's SOC team wants ML-driven detection when an EC2 inference instance makes unexpected API calls to unusual services at 3 AM — a pattern never seen before in normal operations. Which service provides this?
opts: Amazon Inspector
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
Amazon Macie
questions.explain: Amazon GuardDuty uses ML to detect unusual behavioral patterns including unexpected service access and anomalous access times. Config monitors configurations. Macie discovers sensitive data. Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities.

questions.q: An ISO 27001 auditor needs official certification documents proving AWS infrastructure meets the standard. Which service provides official third-party compliance reports?
opts: AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config
AWS Artifact
AWS Audit Manager
questions.explain: AWS Artifact provides official third-party compliance reports and certifications including ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS. Audit Manager assesses customer workload compliance not AWS infrastructure compliance.

questions.q: A retail company needs to predict daily demand for 2,000 products across 100 stores for the next 8 weeks incorporating weekday and seasonal patterns. Which service is purpose-built for this?
opts: Amazon Forecast
Amazon Personalize
Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
Amazon Comprehend
questions.explain: Amazon Forecast is purpose-built for time-series demand forecasting automatically handling seasonality and weekday patterns. Personalize generates user-specific recommendations. Comprehend analyzes text.

questions.q: A media streaming service wants to show each subscriber a personalized list of movies they are most likely to watch next based on their viewing history and ratings. Which service generates these recommendations?
opts: Amazon Personalize
Amazon Forecast
Amazon Kendra
Amazon Comprehend
questions.explain: Amazon Personalize generates real-time personalized recommendations based on individual user behavior. Forecast predicts time-series values like inventory demand. Kendra enables document search.

questions.q: A company needs to run SQL queries on 4 years of ML training logs stored in S3 without provisioning or managing any database infrastructure. Which service provides serverless SQL on S3?
opts: Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon Athena
Amazon Redshift
Amazon RDS
questions.explain: Amazon Athena runs serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data with no infrastructure to provision. Redshift requires loading data into a warehouse. RDS is a managed relational database.

questions.q: A company receives IoT sensor data from 500 factory machines at 50,000 events per second and needs to trigger maintenance alerts within 2 seconds. Which service handles real-time stream ingestion?
opts: Amazon Kinesis
AWS Glue
Amazon Redshift
Amazon Athena
questions.explain: Amazon Kinesis processes high-volume real-time streaming data enabling sub-second processing. Glue handles batch ETL. Redshift is a data warehouse. Athena queries static S3 data.

questions.q: A company needs to extract, clean, and transform data from 8 different source databases into a unified format in S3 every night before ML training. Which service handles this ETL pipeline?
opts: Amazon Redshift
AWS Glue
Amazon Kinesis
Amazon Athena
questions.explain: AWS Glue is the fully managed ETL service extracting from multiple sources, applying transformations, and loading to S3 on schedules. Kinesis handles real-time streaming. Athena queries existing S3 data.

questions.q: A company needs to store 10 million product embedding vectors and perform approximate nearest neighbor semantic similarity search with millisecond latency. Which service natively supports vector ANN search?
opts: Amazon OpenSearch Service
Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
Amazon Redshift
questions.explain: Amazon OpenSearch Service natively supports vector ANN search over millions of embeddings with millisecond latency. DynamoDB and RDS standard indexes are not designed for high-dimensional vector similarity search.

sections.title: NLP and Vision — Round 2 Harder Pairs
sections.description: Trickier scenarios · Multi step pipelines · Edge cases · Service names only

questions.q: A company receives thousands of PDF contracts with handwritten signatures, printed clauses, and embedded tables. They need to extract the contract value, effective date, and party names from each document into a database. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Textract
questions.explain: Textract is built for extracting structured data from complex documents — printed text, handwritten content, tables, and forms in PDFs. Rekognition handles images and video for objects, faces, and text in natural scenes. Comprehend analyzes already extracted text for entities and sentiment.

questions.q: A company processes doctor patient audio consultation recordings and needs to extract diagnoses, prescribed medications, and dosages for electronic health records. Which combination in correct order handles this?
opts: Amazon Lex then Amazon Kendra
Amazon Polly then Amazon Comprehend Medical
Amazon Transcribe Medical then Amazon Comprehend Medical
Amazon Rekognition then Amazon Textract
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe Medical converts clinical audio to text with medical vocabulary accuracy. Amazon Comprehend Medical then extracts clinical entities — diagnoses, medications, dosages — from the transcript. Polly converts text to audio (wrong direction). Rekognition analyzes images.

questions.q: A news agency publishes articles in 15 languages and wants to classify each article into topics like politics, sports, and technology without training a custom model for each language. Which AWS service provides built in multilingual topic detection?
opts: Amazon Polly
Amazon Translate
Amazon Lex
Amazon Comprehend
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend performs topic modeling and classification natively across multiple languages without translation. Translate converts text between languages — a separate unnecessary step. Lex builds conversational interfaces. Polly converts text to audio.

questions.q: A retailer wants to automatically detect when a competitor's product is displayed prominently in social media images that mention their brand. Which service detects and classifies objects within photos?
opts: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Textract
Amazon Transcribe
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels detects and classifies specific objects in images — training it to recognize competitor products in photos. Textract extracts structured text from documents. Comprehend analyzes text content. Transcribe converts audio to text.

questions.q: A company has customer feedback in 8 languages stored as text in S3. They want to identify the most frequently discussed complaint topics across all languages without translating the documents first. Which service should they use?
opts: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Kendra
Amazon Translate
Amazon Polly
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend topic modeling works natively across multiple languages identifying dominant themes without requiring translation. Kendra provides document search. Translate converts languages. Polly converts text to audio.

questions.q: A bank needs to verify that the signature on a physical check image matches the signature on file for an account holder. Which service is MOST appropriate for detecting and comparing handwritten signatures in images?
opts: Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Textract
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Transcribe
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition analyzes visual content in images including custom visual matching. Textract extracts structured text and data from documents but does not perform visual signature comparison. Comprehend analyzes text. Transcribe converts audio.

questions.q: A company wants to build a voice activated smart home device that understands spoken commands like 'Turn off the lights in the bedroom' and triggers the correct automation. Which combination is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Rekognition then Amazon Lex
Amazon Transcribe then Amazon Lex
Amazon Transcribe then Amazon Kendra
Amazon Polly then Amazon Comprehend
questions.explain: Transcribe converts spoken commands to text. Lex understands the intent (TurnOff), extracts slots (room: bedroom, device: lights), and triggers the automation. Kendra searches documents. Polly converts text to audio. Lex is built specifically for intent based voice and text interfaces.

questions.q: A content platform ingests user uploaded images and must automatically detect nudity, graphic violence, and explicit content before publishing. Which service provides this content moderation capability?
opts: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Textract
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Translate
questions.explain: Amazon Rekognition Content Moderation detects unsafe or inappropriate content in images and videos including nudity, violence, and explicit material. Comprehend analyzes text content. Textract extracts document data. Translate converts text between languages.

questions.q: A legal firm scans thousands of case documents as image files. Before running NLP analysis for entity extraction, they need to convert the images to machine readable text. Which service handles this document OCR step?
opts: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Textract
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition
questions.explain: Amazon Textract extracts text from scanned document images using OCR. Comprehend performs NLP on already extracted text — it is the NEXT step after Textract. Rekognition reads text in natural scenes not structured legal documents. Transcribe converts audio not images.

questions.q: A company's call center records thousands of customer calls. They want to automatically detect calls where the agent interrupted the customer more than 3 times and flag them for coaching. Which combination in order achieves this?
opts: Amazon Rekognition then Amazon Textract
Amazon Transcribe then Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Lex then Amazon Kendra
Amazon Polly then Amazon Comprehend
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe converts call audio to text with speaker diarization identifying who spoke when. Amazon Comprehend then analyzes the transcript to detect interruption patterns. Transcribe Call Analytics specifically adds speaker labels and turn taking detection. Polly goes text to audio.

questions.q: A company needs to translate their product catalog website content, marketing PDFs, and help videos into Japanese and Korean for market expansion. They need one service handling all three content formats. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Polly
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Lex
Amazon Translate
questions.explain: Amazon Translate handles text, document, and real time translation across multiple languages. For video subtitle translation, Transcribe first extracts audio then Translate converts the text. Amazon Translate is the core translation service across content types. Polly converts text to audio. Comprehend analyzes content.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical company receives research papers as PDFs with complex tables showing drug trial results. They need to extract specific cell values from these tables for automated data analysis. Which service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Textract
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Transcribe
questions.explain: Amazon Textract AnalyzeDocument with TABLE feature specifically extracts table structures including individual cell values from complex PDFs. Rekognition reads text in natural scenes not structured table data. Comprehend analyzes extracted text for entities. Transcribe converts audio.

sections.title: SageMaker — Advanced Scenario Distinctions
sections.description: Multi constraint scenarios · Cost and latency tradeoffs · Pipeline vs endpoint · All new

questions.q: A company's production fraud model is generating increasing numbers of false positives. They suspect the distribution of transaction amounts has shifted significantly since training. Which SageMaker feature specifically monitors this input data distribution shift?
opts: SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Model Monitor
questions.explain: SageMaker Model Monitor detects data drift by monitoring the statistical distribution of production inputs against a training baseline — specifically catching distribution shifts like changed transaction amounts. Clarify detects bias. Debugger catches training time anomalies. Experiments tracks training run comparisons.

questions.q: A company has labeled 500 support tickets and wants to train a text classifier using a fully automated ML pipeline that selects the best algorithm, trains, and deploys with minimal engineering. Which SageMaker feature provides this automation?
opts: SageMaker Canvas
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Autopilot
SageMaker Experiments
questions.explain: SageMaker Autopilot automatically selects algorithms, trains multiple models, and deploys the best one. Canvas is a no code UI for business users without ML knowledge requiring no coding or algorithm selection. Autopilot generates Python notebooks and requires some ML interpretation. For 500 labeled examples, Autopilot is the correct automated ML choice.

questions.q: An ML team needs to ensure that the same feature transformations used during model training are applied identically at inference time. Which SageMaker feature guarantees this training serving consistency?
opts: SageMaker Data Wrangler
SageMaker Ground Truth
SageMaker Feature Store
SageMaker Pipelines
questions.explain: SageMaker Feature Store provides an online store for real time inference and offline store for training that guarantee identical feature values — eliminating training serving skew. Data Wrangler prepares data interactively. Ground Truth labels data. Pipelines orchestrates workflows but does not guarantee feature consistency across training and inference.

questions.q: A company needs ML inference for an endpoint that receives requests unpredictably — sometimes none for hours, then bursts of 500 per minute. They want to pay only when requests arrive with no idle compute cost. Which SageMaker inference type is MOST appropriate?
opts: SageMaker Real Time Endpoint
SageMaker Batch Transform
SageMaker Asynchronous Inference
SageMaker Serverless Inference
questions.explain: SageMaker Serverless Inference scales automatically from zero — no idle compute cost during quiet periods, instant scale up for bursts. Real Time Endpoints maintain persistent infrastructure incurring costs during idle periods. Batch Transform is for large offline datasets. Asynchronous Inference handles large individual payloads without immediate response.

questions.q: A hospital deploys a model that classifies radiology images. During a training anomaly review, the team discovered the model was performing well on training data but incorrectly learning from shortcut features. Which SageMaker feature would have caught this during training?
opts: SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Model Monitor
SageMaker Ground Truth
questions.explain: SageMaker Debugger monitors tensors and gradients during training in real time — catching overfitting, shortcut learning, and anomalous training dynamics before the job completes. Model Monitor detects production issues. Ground Truth labels data. Clarify detects demographic bias not shortcut feature learning.

questions.q: A startup wants to deploy a pre trained Hugging Face text summarization model to a SageMaker endpoint with minimal custom code. Which SageMaker feature supports one click deployment of pre trained open source models?
opts: SageMaker Canvas
SageMaker JumpStart
SageMaker Pipelines
SageMaker Autopilot
questions.explain: SageMaker JumpStart provides a hub of pre trained models from Hugging Face, TensorFlow Hub, and other sources deployable with minimal code. Autopilot automates training on custom datasets. Canvas is for no code business users. Pipelines orchestrates ML workflows.

questions.q: A company's ML team needs to run a complex production pipeline that automatically retrains their churn model every Sunday, evaluates it against held out data, and only promotes it to production if accuracy exceeds 85%. Which SageMaker feature orchestrates this automated workflow?
opts: SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Canvas
SageMaker Pipelines
SageMaker Experiments
questions.explain: SageMaker Pipelines orchestrates multi step ML workflows including scheduled retraining, conditional evaluation steps, and automated model promotion logic. Experiments tracks run metrics. Debugger monitors training anomalies. Canvas is a no code interface for business users.

questions.q: A company must make real time loan decisions but their ML model takes 45 seconds to process each large applicant document. They need async processing where each result is retrieved when ready. Which SageMaker inference type handles large individual payloads without a synchronous timeout?
opts: SageMaker Serverless Inference
SageMaker Real Time Endpoint
SageMaker Batch Transform
SageMaker Asynchronous Inference
questions.explain: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference handles large individual payloads with long processing times — requests are queued and results retrieved via S3 when complete. Real Time Endpoints have synchronous timeouts. Batch Transform processes entire datasets offline. Serverless handles lightweight unpredictable traffic.

questions.q: A data scientist needs to explain to a credit officer exactly why the model denied a specific loan application — which features drove the decision and how much each contributed. Which SageMaker feature provides per prediction feature importance?
opts: SageMaker Ground Truth
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Model Monitor
SageMaker Experiments
questions.explain: SageMaker Clarify provides SHAP based per prediction feature importance — quantifying each feature's contribution to a specific model output. This enables per applicant adverse action notices. Model Monitor tracks production drift. Experiments tracks training runs. Ground Truth labels training data.

questions.q: A company wants to version their trained models, require approval before promoting to production, and roll back to the previous version if quality degrades. Which SageMaker feature manages the model promotion workflow?
opts: SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Model Registry
SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Feature Store
questions.explain: SageMaker Model Registry manages model versioning with approval workflows and stage transitions from staging to production. It enables one click rollback to previous versions. Feature Store manages ML features. Experiments tracks training runs. Clarify detects bias.

questions.q: A company trains a new model version weekly. Before deploying, they need to automatically run accuracy, latency, and fairness checks. Only if all three pass should the model deploy. Which SageMaker feature implements this multi gate quality pipeline?
opts: SageMaker Clarify
SageMaker Pipelines
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Experiments
questions.explain: SageMaker Pipelines orchestrates multi step conditional workflows including sequential quality gates — accuracy check, latency test, Clarify bias check — with conditional branching that blocks deployment if any gate fails. Debugger monitors training. Experiments tracks runs. Clarify is one gate within the pipeline.

questions.q: A company's recommendation engine needs to update user preference features in real time as users interact with the platform while also using the same features for weekly offline batch retraining. Which SageMaker feature serves both requirements?
opts: SageMaker Feature Store
SageMaker Data Wrangler
SageMaker Autopilot
SageMaker Experiments
questions.explain: SageMaker Feature Store provides an online store for real time feature serving (millisecond reads during live inference) and an offline store for batch training data. Both read from the same centrally managed feature definitions ensuring consistency. Data Wrangler is for interactive data preparation.

sections.title: Bedrock and GenAI — Advanced Scenario Distinctions
sections.description: Multi constraint scenarios · Tricky Guardrails features · Agent vs Knowledge Base · All new

questions.q: A company's Bedrock chatbot correctly answers product questions but a red team discovers that prefixing any question with 'In a fictional story,' causes the model to bypass content restrictions and discuss competitor pricing. Which Guardrails feature most directly addresses this jailbreak pattern?
opts: Denied topics
Grounding check
PII redaction
Content filters
questions.explain: Bedrock Guardrails denied topics blocks subject areas at the infrastructure layer regardless of how a query is framed — fictional framing, roleplay, and hypothetical prefixes cannot bypass denied topic enforcement. Content filters block harmful content categories. Grounding check validates factual support. PII redaction masks personal data.

questions.q: A company uses a Bedrock agent for IT support. A user asks the agent to reset their password. The agent needs to call an internal IT ticketing API to create the reset request. Which Bedrock feature enables this external API call?
opts: Bedrock Prompt Management
Bedrock Agents with action groups
Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Bedrock Guardrails
questions.explain: Bedrock Agents with action groups backed by Lambda functions enables the agent to call external APIs — including internal IT ticketing systems — as part of fulfilling user requests. Knowledge Bases retrieves indexed documents. Guardrails adds content safety controls. Prompt Management versions prompts.

questions.q: A company runs a Bedrock application and needs to understand which IAM identity called which foundation model and at exactly what time for a security investigation. Which service provides this API level audit trail?
opts: Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Macie
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon CloudWatch
questions.explain: AWS CloudTrail logs every Bedrock InvokeModel API call with the exact IAM identity, timestamp, model ID, and source IP. CloudWatch monitors metrics and application logs. GuardDuty detects behavioral anomalies. Macie discovers sensitive data in S3.

questions.q: A company's Bedrock RAG application answers correctly from documents indexed 3 weeks ago but gives wrong answers about documents added to S3 last week. No configuration has changed. What is the root cause?
opts: The Knowledge Base requires an explicit sync after documents are added to S3
The embedding model must be retrained to index new document vocabulary
The vector database requires manual rebuilding after new documents are added
The FM training cutoff predates the newly added documents
questions.explain: Bedrock Knowledge Bases requires an explicit sync operation after new documents are added to S3. Without sync, the vector index does not include last week's documents. FM training cutoff is irrelevant for RAG retrieved content. Embedding models and vector databases do not require retraining for standard document updates.

questions.q: A company's Bedrock powered legal assistant confidently cites cases that do not exist. The team wants to automatically block responses where the model fabricates content not present in the retrieved legal documents. Which Guardrails feature handles this?
opts: Content filters
Denied topics
PII redaction
Grounding check
questions.explain: Bedrock Guardrails grounding check evaluates semantic similarity between the response and retrieved source content — blocking responses that include fabricated citations not supported by the retrieved legal documents. Content filters block harmful categories. Denied topics block subject areas. PII redaction masks personal data.

questions.q: A company wants to reduce Bedrock costs significantly for a use case where the same 4,000-token system prompt is sent with every request across millions of daily API calls. Which optimization reduces the repeated processing cost of this system prompt?
opts: Bedrock Prompt Caching
Bedrock Cross Region Inference
Bedrock Batch Inference
Bedrock Provisioned Throughput
questions.explain: Bedrock Prompt Caching stores processed prompt prefixes so repeated identical system prompts are not recomputed — dramatically reducing token processing costs for high volume applications with static system prompts. Batch Inference requires asynchronous processing. Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity. Cross Region Inference optimizes latency.

questions.q: A company building a Bedrock multi agent system needs one orchestrator agent to break down complex tasks and delegate subtasks to specialized sub agents for research, writing, and fact checking. Which Bedrock feature supports this multi agent orchestration?
opts: Bedrock Guardrails
Bedrock Prompt Management
Bedrock Agents with inline agents
Bedrock Knowledge Bases
questions.explain: Bedrock Agents supports multi agent collaboration where an orchestrator agent delegates to specialized sub agents — each configured with their own tools, knowledge bases, and instructions. Knowledge Bases provides document retrieval. Guardrails adds safety controls. Prompt Management versions prompts.

questions.q: A financial company wants to systematically compare how three different foundation models perform on their specific earnings call summarization task before committing to one model for production. Which Bedrock feature enables this structured comparison?
opts: Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Bedrock Prompt Management
Bedrock Model Evaluation
Bedrock Guardrails
questions.explain: Bedrock Model Evaluation runs structured comparisons of multiple foundation models against a custom evaluation dataset with defined quality metrics — the purpose built pre deployment model selection tool. Guardrails adds safety controls. Knowledge Bases provides retrieval. Prompt Management versions prompts.

questions.q: A company's Bedrock application processes customer financial data. Their compliance team requires that all data processed by Bedrock remain within the AWS us east 1 region and never cross regional boundaries. Which configuration enforces this?
opts: VPC endpoints with data residency SCPs blocking cross region API calls
Bedrock Cross Region Inference routing to nearest available region
Bedrock Guardrails with regional content filtering enabled
Bedrock Provisioned Throughput locking capacity to us east 1
questions.explain: VPC endpoints (PrivateLink) keep traffic within AWS private network combined with Service Control Policies (SCPs) blocking cross region Bedrock API calls enforces strict data residency in us east 1. Cross Region Inference actively routes to other regions (opposite requirement). Guardrails manages content not regional routing. Provisioned Throughput manages capacity.

questions.q: A company's Bedrock agent for customer service is slow — taking 18 seconds per response. Profiling shows Lambda action groups complete in 80ms but the agent makes 6 to 8 tool calls per simple query. What should they investigate first?
opts: Overlapping action group descriptions causing the agent to loop unnecessarily
The knowledge base vector search is adding cumulative latency per retrieval
The IAM role is causing authorization delays on each Lambda call
The FM max tokens setting is too high causing slow generation
questions.explain: 6 to 8 tool calls for a simple query with Lambda completing in 80ms indicates the orchestration loop is iterating excessively — overlapping or ambiguous action group descriptions cause the agent to try multiple tools before finding the right one. Clarifying descriptions to be distinct and specific reduces unnecessary iterations.

questions.q: A company wants to give their Bedrock FM access to their company's internal product catalog, pricing tables, and support documentation to answer customer questions accurately. Which Bedrock feature indexes and retrieves this private content?
opts: Bedrock Guardrails
Bedrock Model Evaluation
Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Bedrock Agents
questions.explain: Bedrock Knowledge Bases indexes private documents from S3 into a vector store enabling semantic retrieval at query time — grounding FM responses in the company's actual product catalog, pricing, and documentation. Agents orchestrate multi step workflows. Guardrails adds safety controls. Model Evaluation compares FM quality.

questions.q: A company's Bedrock application occasionally generates responses containing customer email addresses and phone numbers that were retrieved from their CRM. Which Guardrails feature automatically removes this before the response reaches the user?
opts: Denied topics
Grounding check
PII redaction
Content filters
questions.explain: Bedrock Guardrails PII redaction automatically detects and masks personally identifiable information including email addresses and phone numbers in both inputs and outputs. Content filters block harmful content categories. Denied topics block subject areas. Grounding check validates factual support.

sections.title: Mixed Hardest — Multi Constraint Service Selection
sections.description: Two correct looking options · Cost vs latency vs accuracy tradeoffs · Confirmed exam traps

questions.q: A company wants to give employees an AI assistant that answers HR and IT questions from internal documents with role based access — so engineers see technical docs but not salary bands, and HR sees all docs. Which service handles this natively?
opts: Amazon OpenSearch Service
Amazon Q Business
Amazon Kendra
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
questions.explain: Amazon Q Business provides enterprise AI assistance with native identity aware access controls enforcing per user document permissions through enterprise identity provider integration. Kendra requires custom access control layers. Bedrock Knowledge Bases requires custom ACL implementation. OpenSearch needs custom identity integration.

questions.q: A company's data science team receives a new batch of 10,000 unlabeled customer images daily that need human annotation before retraining their product recognition model. Which service manages this labeling workflow at scale?
opts: Amazon Rekognition
SageMaker Model Monitor
SageMaker Ground Truth
Amazon Augmented AI
questions.explain: SageMaker Ground Truth manages human labeling workflows for TRAINING data at scale — workforce management, task distribution, annotation consolidation, quality control. A2I routes PRODUCTION predictions for human review of low confidence inferences. Ground Truth is pre training labeling. A2I is post deployment review.

questions.q: A company's deployed product classification model confidence scores drop below 60% for a new category of products added after training. These low confidence predictions must be reviewed by a human before the classification is stored. Which service routes these specific predictions for human review?
opts: SageMaker Model Monitor
Amazon Augmented AI
SageMaker Ground Truth
SageMaker Clarify
questions.explain: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) routes PRODUCTION predictions below a confidence threshold to human reviewers before the result is used. Ground Truth labels TRAINING data. Clarify detects demographic bias. Model Monitor tracks distribution drift. A2I is specifically for confidence based routing of live predictions to human review.

questions.q: A company needs to build a customer support chatbot that handles 500 concurrent sessions, understands free form questions, and generates varied natural language responses. Cost per session must be under $0.001. Which combination is MOST appropriate?
opts: Amazon Polly then Amazon Translate
Amazon Lex then Amazon Kendra
Amazon Transcribe then Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Lex then Amazon Bedrock
questions.explain: Amazon Lex handles the conversational interface and intent management. Amazon Bedrock provides the foundation model for generating natural varied responses. Lex handles conversation flow while Bedrock provides generative AI intelligence — the confirmed exam combination for generative chatbots. Kendra provides search not generation.

questions.q: A company stores model training artifacts, evaluation reports, and experiment configs in S3. A security audit finds that S3 access logs show an unusual spike in downloads at 2 AM by an IAM principal never seen before. Which service would have proactively detected this behavioral anomaly?
opts: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
Amazon Macie
AWS CloudTrail
questions.explain: Amazon GuardDuty uses ML to detect unusual behavioral patterns including anomalous access times and unexpected IAM principals accessing resources — it would flag the 2 AM spike from an unknown principal. Config monitors resource configurations. Macie discovers sensitive data content. CloudTrail logs the activity but does not generate behavioral anomaly alerts.

questions.q: A company needs to automatically enrich their ML training dataset by finding and filling missing ZIP codes, income brackets, and industry codes for 5 million customer records using batch transformations before training begins. Which service handles this batch data enrichment?
opts: Amazon Kinesis
Amazon Athena
Amazon Redshift
AWS Glue
questions.explain: AWS Glue is the managed ETL service for large scale batch data transformations including enrichment, joins, and derived field computation before ML training. Kinesis handles real time streaming. Athena queries existing S3 data. Redshift is a data warehouse for analytical queries not ETL orchestration.

questions.q: A healthcare company trains a model predicting readmission risk. The model achieves 91% accuracy overall but only 54% recall for elderly patients despite them being 30% of the dataset. Which service detects and quantifies this subgroup performance gap?
opts: SageMaker Model Monitor
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Experiments
SageMaker Clarify
questions.explain: SageMaker Clarify measures bias metrics and performance across demographic subgroups — quantifying disparate recall for elderly patients versus the overall population. Model Monitor detects production data drift. Debugger catches training anomalies. Experiments tracks run comparisons. Clarify is the answer to subgroup performance gap questions.

questions.q: A company needs to make 8 million inference calls per month using Amazon Bedrock at predictable high volume. After 3 months the finance team flags that on demand costs are 40% over budget. What pricing model should they evaluate?
opts: Bedrock Batch Inference
Bedrock Cross Region Inference
Bedrock On Demand
Bedrock Provisioned Throughput
questions.explain: Bedrock Provisioned Throughput reserves dedicated model capacity at a lower effective cost than on demand at sustained high volume. 8 million calls per month at predictable rate justifies provisioned commitment. Batch Inference requires asynchronous processing. Cross Region Inference optimizes latency not cost.

questions.q: A company's Bedrock application needs to generate product descriptions in English, Spanish, and French from the same product database. The team wants all content filtered for safety regardless of which language the output is in. Which Guardrails feature applies across all output languages?
opts: Content filters
Grounding check
Prompt injection detection
PII redaction
questions.explain: Bedrock Guardrails content filters apply to outputs in any language — they operate at the semantic level not keyword matching, so Spanish and French outputs are filtered as effectively as English. Grounding check validates factual support. Prompt injection detects override attacks. PII redaction masks personal data.

questions.q: A company needs ML predictions from a SageMaker endpoint for a user facing mobile app. Each request is a simple product image, model response time must be under 300ms, and the endpoint receives 1,000 requests per minute consistently throughout the day. Which deployment is MOST appropriate?
opts: SageMaker Batch Transform
SageMaker Asynchronous Inference
SageMaker Real Time Endpoint
SageMaker Serverless Inference
questions.explain: SageMaker Real Time Endpoint meets all three constraints: sub-300ms latency for user facing mobile, handles consistent 1,000 rpm throughput with auto scaling, and provides synchronous responses. Serverless has cold start latency risks at consistent volume. Batch Transform is offline. Asynchronous does not return immediate responses.

questions.q: A company wants to detect when their S3 training data bucket is publicly accessible and automatically revert it to private within 5 minutes of the misconfiguration occurring. Which service provides automated compliance remediation?
opts: AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Macie
Amazon Inspector
questions.explain: AWS Config continuously monitors resource configurations against rules and triggers automatic remediation using Systems Manager Automation — reverting S3 bucket ACLs to private within minutes. GuardDuty detects behavioral threats. Macie discovers sensitive data content in S3. Inspector scans EC2 and containers for software vulnerabilities.

questions.q: A company provides AWS compliance reports to their enterprise customers to prove their shared infrastructure meets SOC 2 Type II requirements. Which AWS service provides these official third party audit reports?
opts: AWS Audit Manager
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config
AWS Artifact
questions.explain: AWS Artifact provides on demand access to official third party compliance reports including SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS that customers can share with their own auditors and enterprise customers. Audit Manager assesses customer workload compliance. CloudTrail provides operational logs. Config monitors resource configurations.

sections.title: Domain 1: GenAI Fundamentals (30% of exam)
sections.description: AI vs ML vs GenAI vs Deep Learning · Foundation models · Data types · Hallucination · RAG concepts

questions.q: A company wants to build an application that can generate new marketing copy, create original images, and produce audio narrations from text. Which type of AI makes all three of these possible?
opts: Generative AI
Traditional rule based AI
Unsupervised clustering
Supervised machine learning
questions.explain: Generative AI creates new content across multiple modalities — text, images, audio, video, and code. The study guide defines GenAI as 'an application of ML that focuses on creating new content.' Supervised ML classifies or predicts. Rule-based AI follows coded rules. Clustering groups unlabeled data.

questions.q: A video game company wants their AI character to learn navigation and decision-making through trial and error in a complex game environment, receiving rewards for good moves and penalties for bad ones. Which ML approach applies?
opts: Transfer learning from pretrained navigation models
Supervised learning on labeled gameplay recordings
Unsupervised clustering of player behavior
Reinforcement learning through environmental rewards
questions.explain: Reinforcement learning trains an agent to take actions in an environment to maximize cumulative reward — learning through interaction and feedback. The study guide states RL 'learns through interaction and feedback to maximize rewards and minimize penalties.' This is the exact pattern of game AI learning through reward signals.

questions.q: A global news company uses an LLM to generate article summaries. The model produced a summary of an international summit that stated a specific agreement was reached that never actually occurred. How should the company address this?
opts: Implement stricter safety settings to filter out controversial topics
Use grounding to base model output on the verified source articles
Increase the temperature setting to encourage more diverse and accurate outputs
Fine tune the model on a larger dataset of news articles
questions.explain: Hallucinations occur when LLMs generate confident but factually incorrect content. Grounding connects the model's output to verifiable source articles — the model can only state what is in the source. The study guide defines grounding as 'connecting the AI output to verifiable sources of information.' Temperature increase worsens hallucination. Fine-tuning changes behavior not factual accuracy.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical company processes thousands of research papers, clinical trial reports, and drug interaction databases. These documents exist in various formats with no consistent data schema. What type of data is this?
opts: Unstructured data that lacks a predefined organizational format
Structured data organized in relational database tables
Quality data that is accurate complete and consistent
Semi structured data with partial schema enforcement
questions.explain: Research papers, clinical reports, and varied-format documents are unstructured data — they lack a predefined structure and require sophisticated analysis techniques. The study guide defines unstructured data as 'data that lacks a predefined structure and requires sophisticated analysis techniques.' Structured data is organized in rows and columns like database tables.

questions.q: A foundation model is described as being 'flexible' and 'adaptable.' What do these two characteristics specifically mean according to the Google Cloud study guide?
opts: Flexible means it runs on any hardware and adaptable means it scales automatically
Flexible means applicable to a wide range of use cases
Flexible means it accepts any data format and adaptable means it can be updated in real time
Flexible means low latency and adaptable means it handles high volume requests without degradation
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly states foundation model key features include: 'Flexible to a wide range of use cases' and 'Adaptable to specialized domains through additional, targeted training.' Foundation models are general-purpose (flexible) but can be further trained for specific domains (adaptable through fine-tuning or RAG).

questions.q: A company's AI assistant consistently gives outdated answers about recent regulatory changes because the regulations were updated after the model was trained. Which foundation model limitation does this represent?
opts: Edge case failures on rare scenarios
Data dependency on training data quality
Knowledge cutoff with no awareness of post training events
Bias from imbalanced training data
questions.explain: Knowledge cutoff is a core foundation model limitation — 'AI models are trained up to a specific knowledge cutoff date, meaning they might lack information about events after that point.' The study guide lists this explicitly. RAG with current regulatory databases directly addresses this limitation.

questions.q: A business leader wants to understand what generative AI can do that traditional ML cannot. Which capability is UNIQUE to generative AI?
opts: Creating original product descriptions from a brief set of keywords
Predicting which customers will churn next quarter from historical data
Classifying support tickets into priority categories from training examples
Detecting unusual transactions that differ from normal behavior patterns
questions.explain: Creating original content — product descriptions, images, code, audio — is unique to generative AI. The study guide states GenAI can 'Create: Generate new content.' The other options (churn prediction, classification, anomaly detection) are traditional supervised or unsupervised ML tasks that do not generate new content.

questions.q: According to the Google Cloud study guide, what is the correct nested relationship between AI, ML, deep learning, and generative AI?
opts: GenAI contains ML which contains Deep Learning which contains AI
AI contains ML which contains Deep Learning and GenAI is an application of ML
ML contains AI which contains GenAI which contains Deep Learning
Deep Learning contains ML which contains AI and GenAI is separate from all three
questions.explain: The study guide diagram and definitions show: AI is the broadest field. ML is a subfield of AI. Deep Learning is a subset of ML using neural networks. GenAI is 'an application of ML that focuses on creating new content.' The diagram shows GenAI as the innermost circle within ML within AI.

questions.q: A company is building a gen AI application and the architect describes the 'platform layer' of their architecture. What does this layer provide according to the Google Cloud gen AI landscape?
opts: The core algorithms and neural network weights of the foundation models themselves
The physical GPU and TPU hardware infrastructure for running AI computations
The user facing interface allowing users to interact with and leverage AI capabilities
APIs, data management capabilities, and model deployment tools bridging models and agents
questions.explain: The study guide defines Platform as: 'This layer offers APIs, data management capabilities, and model deployment tools. It bridges the gap between models and agents while simplifying the complexities of infrastructure management.' Infrastructure is the physical hardware. The gen-AI-powered application is the user-facing layer. The model is the algorithm layer.

questions.q: A company's AI generates product descriptions that occasionally include a competitor's name being used for generic product categories (e.g., using a brand name as a category name). This is a responsible AI concern. Which limitation does it represent?
opts: Hallucination generating confident but incorrect content
Bias from training data reflecting how people commonly write
Edge cases where rare trademark scenarios expose model weaknesses
Knowledge cutoff preventing awareness of trademark status
questions.explain: Using brand names as generic terms is a bias issue — the model learned from training data where humans commonly use brand names generically (like 'Google it' for web search). The study guide states: 'Bias: LLMs learn from large datasets which may contain biases. Even subtle biases can be magnified in the model outputs.' This is a subtle bias from common language patterns in training data.

sections.title: Domain 2: Google Cloud GenAI Offerings (35% of exam)
sections.description: Gemini family · Vertex AI · Agent Builder · AI Studio · Workspace · APIs · When to use which

questions.q: An organization wants to quickly experiment with different Gemini models and parameters for content creation without a complex setup or production deployment. Which Google Cloud service should they use for this initial exploration?
opts: Vertex AI Prediction
Vertex AI Agent Builder
Gemini for Google Workspace
Google AI Studio
questions.explain: Google AI Studio is available free of charge and is designed for quick AI prototyping and experimentation — the study guide states 'Google AI Studio is available free of charge and is meant for quick AI prototyping.' Workspace integrates AI into productivity apps. Vertex AI Prediction serves deployed models. Agent Builder creates production AI agents.

questions.q: A company wants to build a production-ready AI agent that searches through thousands of internal documents and answers employee HR questions at scale with enterprise-grade security. Which Google Cloud service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Vertex AI Agent Builder for production AI agent deployment
Gemini for Google Workspace for employee productivity
Google AI Studio for low code agent prototyping
Gemini Notebook for document upload and Q&A
questions.explain: Vertex AI Agent Builder is designed for building and deploying production-ready AI agents at scale — the study guide states 'Agent Studio is for building and deploying production-ready AI applications at scale.' Google AI Studio is for quick prototyping. Gemini Notebook is for personal document Q&A. Workspace integrates AI into Google apps.

questions.q: A large e-commerce company with a massive product catalog wants to improve website search so customers can find products using natural language queries and get relevant results from the catalog. Which Google Cloud solution addresses this?
opts: Google AI Studio to prototype product recommendation chatbots
Gemini Notebook to process and summarize product documentation
Gemini for Google Workspace to enhance product team productivity
Vertex AI Agent Builder with Vertex AI Search to build grounded product search
questions.explain: Vertex AI Search indexes enterprise content and enables natural language search grounded in specific data sources — directly addressing the product catalog search use case. The study guide identifies 'Agent Search: Search and recommendation solutions for your business.' Agent Builder with Search provides the grounded retrieval over the product catalog.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical research department spends significant time manually reviewing new scientific papers to identify drug targets. They need a solution that can answer questions about scientific documents and provide summarized insights without requiring extensive coding. Which Google Cloud service is MOST appropriate?
opts: Vertex AI AutoML to train a drug target classification model
Gemini for Google Workspace to facilitate collaborative document review
Vertex AI Agent Builder to create a document Q&A agent with low code tools
Cloud Vision API to analyze molecular structure images in papers
questions.explain: Vertex AI Agent Builder is designed for creating custom AI agents — including document Q&A and summarization — with low-code capabilities that don't require data science expertise. Vertex AI AutoML trains classification models which is different from answering questions. Gemini Workspace supports collaboration not custom agent building. Vision API analyzes images not text documents.

questions.q: A company wants to integrate Google's generative AI capabilities directly into their Gmail, Google Docs, and Google Slides to help employees write emails, generate presentations, and summarize meeting notes. Which product provides this?
opts: Google AI Studio embedded into Workspace applications
Vertex AI Agent Builder with Workspace connectors
Gemini for Google Workspace integrated across Workspace apps
Gemini Enterprise for custom Workspace API integration
questions.explain: Gemini for Google Workspace integrates gen AI into familiar Workspace apps — the study guide states it 'integrates gen AI into familiar Workspace apps, allowing you to do things like compose emails in Gmail, generate images in Slides, and summarize notes in Meet.' AI Studio is for prototyping. Agent Builder creates custom agents. Gemini Enterprise handles customized search and conversation.

questions.q: A company needs to run a compact AI model directly on mobile devices for offline inference without requiring cloud connectivity. Which Google model is specifically designed for on-device use?
opts: Gemini Flash for high volume low latency applications
Gemma for open source local deployments
Gemini Nano for on device inference on mobile devices
Gemini Pro for maximum accuracy on complex reasoning
questions.explain: Gemini Nano is Google's most efficient and compact AI model specifically designed to run on devices. The study guide states: 'Gemini Nano is Google's most efficient and compact AI model, specifically designed to run on devices.' Gemma is for developer local deployments. Gemini Pro and Flash are cloud-based models for different performance tiers.

questions.q: A company wants to generate high-quality images from detailed text descriptions for their marketing campaigns. Which Google Cloud model handles text-to-image generation?
opts: Imagen for text to image generation producing high quality visuals
Gemini for multimodal content generation across text and images
Gemma for developer friendly customizable image generation
Veo for video content generation from textual descriptions
questions.explain: Imagen is Google's text-to-image diffusion model — the study guide states 'Imagen: It is a text-to-image diffusion model that generates high-quality images from textual descriptions.' Gemini handles multimodal understanding and generation. Gemma is for text-focused local deployments. Veo generates video not static images.

questions.q: A media production company wants to automatically generate short promotional video clips from product description text for their e-commerce platform. Which Google Cloud model should they use?
opts: Gemini for multimodal content generation including video
Veo for generating video content based on text descriptions
Gemma for efficient video generation on local servers
Imagen for generating video frames from text descriptions
questions.explain: Veo is Google's video generation model — the study guide states 'Veo: It generates video content based on text descriptions or still images.' Imagen generates static images. Gemini handles multimodal understanding but Veo is the specialized video generation model. Gemma is an open-source text model for local deployments.

questions.q: A company's call center handles thousands of customer calls daily. They want an AI system that provides real-time assistance to human agents during calls by suggesting responses and surfacing relevant information. Which Google Cloud offering addresses this?
opts: Gemini for Google Workspace for agent productivity
Vertex AI Agent Builder for automated customer responses
Customer Engagement Suite with Agent Assist for live agent support
Gemini Enterprise for customized internal knowledge search
questions.explain: Customer Engagement Suite includes Agent Assist — the study guide states 'Agent Assist: Support your live human contact center agents.' This specifically provides real-time AI assistance to human agents during live calls. Workspace handles productivity. Agent Builder creates automated bots. Gemini Enterprise handles internal knowledge search.

questions.q: A developer needs to convert recorded customer support calls to text for quality review and analysis. Which Google Cloud API provides speech-to-text transcription of audio content?
opts: Natural Language API
Document AI API
Cloud Vision API
Speech to Text API
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly lists the Speech-to-Text API which 'converts speech into text' and 'also transcribes audio and video content.' Natural Language API analyzes text for insights and sentiment. Document AI extracts data from documents. Vision API analyzes images.

questions.q: A company's legal team uses Gemini for Google Workspace. They need to analyze uploaded contract PDFs, get AI-generated summaries of key clauses, and ask follow-up questions while staying grounded in the document content. Which Gemini tool is purpose-built for this?
opts: Gemini for Google Workspace integrated into Google Docs
Gemini Notebook for document upload research assistance
Google AI Studio for rapid prototyping with document inputs
Gemini Advanced for enterprise grade protection and features
questions.explain: Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) allows users to upload documents and acts as a research assistant — the study guide states it 'allows you to upload your files and then acts as a research assistant, summarizing key points, answering questions, and generating ideas, all while staying grounded in your source material.' This is exactly the grounded document Q&A use case.

questions.q: A startup wants to give their software developers AI assistance for writing and debugging code directly within their cloud development workflow. Which Gemini product provides this coding assistance on Google Cloud?
opts: Google AI Studio for prototyping code generation tools
Gemini for Google Cloud for AI coding assistance and
Gemini for Google Workspace for collaborative document development
Gemini Notebook for code documentation research and summarization
questions.explain: Gemini for Google Cloud is the AI assistant specifically for Google Cloud — the study guide states it 'can help you write and debug code, manage and optimize cloud applications, analyze data in BigQuery, and strengthen your security posture.' Workspace handles productivity apps. Gemini Notebook is for research. AI Studio is for prototyping.

sections.title: Domain 3: Techniques to Improve GenAI Output (20% of exam)
sections.description: RAG · Grounding · Prompting techniques · Fine-tuning · Sampling parameters · HITL
