Steadily declining email quality despite no model changes is exactly the drift pattern that drift monitoring detects. Versioning tracks model iterations. Data management handles feature data. Storage organizes models.

questions.q: A company wants to improve their AI assistant's responses about their internal product catalog. They have 500 detailed product specification sheets stored in Google Drive. Rather than retraining, they want the AI to retrieve the right specification sheet and use it when answering product questions. Which technique does this describe?
opts: Chain of thought prompting, which guides the model step by step through product specification analysis
Few shot prompting, which includes example product questions and answers in every prompt
Fine tuning, which trains the model on product specification examples to learn catalog details
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), which retrieves relevant specifications at query time to ground responses
questions.explain: RAG retrieves the relevant specification sheet at query time and includes it in the prompt — the study guide describes RAG's steps: 'Retrieval: The LLM retrieves relevant information from external sources. Augmentation: The retrieved information is incorporated into the prompt.' The model answers from the actual specification rather than training data. Fine-tuning updates model weights. Chain-of-thought elicits reasoning. Few-shot provides static examples.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical company uses AI to assist with drug discovery research. Before any AI-generated research hypothesis reaches a human researcher, a team of senior scientists must validate that the hypothesis is scientifically plausible and not based on confabulated chemical interactions. What is this validation process called?
opts: Pre generation review, which has human experts validate AI outputs before they reach end users
Drift monitoring, which watches for changes in AI output accuracy over time automatically
Fine tuning, which trains the AI on validated research hypotheses to reduce future confabulation
Post generation review, which provides continuous human feedback after AI deployment
questions.explain: The study guide defines Pre-generation review as: 'Human experts review and validate ML outputs before deployment, catching errors or biases before user impact.' Senior scientists validating AI hypotheses before researchers see them is exactly pre-generation review — the human expert validation happens before the AI output reaches its intended user. Post-generation review occurs after deployment.

questions.q: A company has two gen AI options for their customer service: Option A uses a detailed system prompt with company policies (quick to update, no training needed). Option B fine-tunes the model on company service examples (consistent behavior, higher upfront cost). Their policies update monthly and they have no ML team. Which option is MOST appropriate?
opts: Option A prompt engineering, because RAG cannot handle monthly policy updates efficiently
Option B fine tuning, because it permanently encodes company policies into the model for consistency
Option A prompt engineering, because it allows monthly policy updates with no ML expertise required
Option B fine tuning, because it eliminates the need for long system prompts reducing per query token costs
questions.explain: Monthly policy updates with no ML team makes prompt engineering the correct choice — policies can be updated in the system prompt instantly with no retraining. Fine-tuning would require ML expertise and monthly retraining cycles. The study guide's approach is to match the technique to organizational constraints. Prompt engineering trades some consistency for immediate updatability and zero training cost.

questions.q: A company's AI research agent needs to answer complex questions by first identifying what information it needs, then searching for it, then reading the results, then deciding if more searching is needed before writing the final answer. Which prompting technique enables this multi-step reasoning and action loop?
opts: Metaprompting, which uses prompting to guide the AI to generate better research prompts
Chain of thought (CoT), which guides the LLM through a problem solving process with intermediate steps
Few shot prompting, which provides multiple examples of research questions and complete answers
ReAct (reason and act), which allows the LLM to reason and take iterative actions on a query
questions.explain: The study guide defines ReAct as: 'Allow the LLM to reason and take action on a user query.' ReAct enables the iterative loop of: reason about what's needed → search → observe results → reason again → search more if needed → final answer. This is distinct from chain-of-thought (step-by-step reasoning without external action) and few-shot (static examples).

questions.q: A company evaluates their gen AI customer service system using BLEU scores for summarization quality. The automated scores are high but customer satisfaction survey scores are low. Their head of AI says 'our metrics are not measuring what matters.' What does this situation demonstrate?
opts: BLEU scores are unreliable and should be replaced with ROUGE scores for customer service evaluation
Customer satisfaction surveys are too subjective and BLEU scores provide more reliable quality signals
Automated metrics like BLEU measure text overlap not real world usefulness or customer satisfaction
Both metrics should be averaged to get a balanced and comprehensive quality assessment
questions.explain: This is the core lesson on automated vs human evaluation — BLEU measures n-gram word overlap with reference text, which does not capture whether responses actually help customers. High BLEU plus low satisfaction means the metric is not measuring what matters for this use case. Human satisfaction surveys directly measure the business objective. Neither metric should be averaged — they measure fundamentally different things.

questions.q: An AI assistant for a law firm must never discuss criminal defense strategies, never provide specific legal advice on pending cases, and never comment on ongoing litigation involving the firm's clients. Which prompting technique defines these behavioral boundaries most directly?
opts: Role prompting, which assigns the model a law firm assistant persona that inherently avoids these topics
Few shot prompting, which provides examples of questions the model should decline to answer
Chain of thought prompting, which guides the model to reason through whether to answer before responding
Negative prompting, which explicitly specifies behaviors and topics the model should not produce
questions.explain: The study guide recognizes negative prompting as explicitly specifying what the model should NOT do — defining prohibited behaviors, outputs, and topics. 'Never discuss X, never provide Y, never comment on Z' is the definitive negative prompting pattern. Role prompting assigns identity not explicit prohibitions. Few-shot provides examples. Chain-of-thought elicits reasoning steps.

sections.title: Domain 4: Business Strategies for GenAI — Round 3 (15%)
sections.description: Real exam format · ROI · Adoption · Responsible AI · Model selection · Risk

questions.q: A company is selecting a foundation model for their customer service chatbot. Their primary requirements are: the model must process both text queries and attached product images, handle long conversation histories, and be cost-effective for high volume. According to the study guide, which selection criterion should they evaluate FIRST?
opts: Performance, because accuracy speed and efficiency determine whether the model meets quality requirements
Availability and reliability, because the model must perform reliably under high customer service load
Modality, because the model must support both text and image inputs for this use case
Context window, because long conversation histories require sufficient context capacity
questions.explain: The study guide lists Modality FIRST in model selection factors: 'Choose a generative AI model whose input and output data types (modality) align with your application specific needs, whether text, images, audio, or video.' If the model cannot process both text and images together, it fails the fundamental requirement regardless of performance, reliability, or context window.

questions.q: A company's AI steering committee debates when responsible AI principles should be applied. The compliance officer says 'after deployment when we can see real issues.' The AI lead says 'only during model selection.' The CTO says 'throughout the entire project.' Who is correct according to the Google Cloud study guide?
opts: All three together, because responsible AI has distinct activities in each of the three phases
The compliance officer, because real bias patterns only become visible with real user data after deployment
The AI lead, because model selection is the highest leverage point for responsible AI intervention
The CTO, because responsible AI must be considered from data preparation through deployment and monitoring
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly states: 'Responsible AI needs to be considered throughout the entire AI lifecycle, from data preparation and model training to deployment and ongoing monitoring.' The CTO is correct. Waiting until deployment misses critical prevention opportunities. Model selection alone is insufficient. Responsible AI is a continuous lifecycle practice, not a one-time gate.

questions.q: A company's gen AI pilot showed 25% reduction in documentation time and 4.2/5 user satisfaction. The board now wants to know the business case for enterprise rollout. Which type of evidence MOST convincingly demonstrates ROI to the board?
opts: Financial projections showing annual cost savings from the 25% documentation time reduction
Technical benchmarks showing the model achieves 94% accuracy on documentation quality tests
Adoption statistics showing 87% of pilot users actively use the tool daily
Developer productivity metrics showing 30% faster feature development during the pilot
questions.explain: Financial projections translating the 25% time reduction into cost savings directly speak to ROI — the board makes investment decisions based on financial return. The study guide emphasizes 'Impact: Measure gen AI impact on business goals and demonstrate tangible benefits.' Accuracy benchmarks, adoption stats, and developer metrics are supporting evidence but financial impact is the primary board-level ROI argument.

questions.q: A company successfully pilots a gen AI HR assistant. During wider rollout, employees in manufacturing plants report the assistant gives advice misaligned with their specific union agreements and local labor laws — it works well for office staff but not manufacturing workers. Which responsible AI principle was inadequately addressed during the pilot?
opts: Strategic focus, because the pilot should have started with manufacturing workers first
Continuous improvement, because the system needs ongoing refinement based on new user feedback
Exploration, because the pilot should have tested more diverse gen AI approaches before rollout
Fairness, because the AI was not evaluated for consistent performance across all employee groups
questions.explain: The AI performs differently for manufacturing workers than office staff — this is a fairness and bias issue. The study guide includes Responsible AI as a core gen AI strategy component: 'Establish ethical guidelines and ensure secure and responsible AI development.' Adequate bias testing during the pilot across all employee groups (not just office staff) would have caught this disparity before wider rollout.

questions.q: A new CISO joins a company running gen AI applications on Google Cloud. They ask: 'What framework does Google provide for organizations to systematically manage AI and ML security risks?' Which framework should the team point them to?
opts: Google Cloud IAM, an identity and access management system for controlling resource permissions
Security Command Center, a security posture visibility tool for Google Cloud workloads
SAIF (Secure AI Framework), a framework specifically for managing AI and ML model security risks
Vertex AI MLOps, a platform for monitoring and improving AI model performance over time
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly states: 'The Secure AI Framework (SAIF) helps organizations manage AI/ML model risks and ensure security.' SAIF is the Google-specific AI security framework. IAM manages resource access permissions. Security Command Center provides security posture visibility. Vertex AI MLOps handles model performance monitoring. SAIF is specifically for AI/ML risk management.

questions.q: A company's leadership team mandates a gen AI strategy but employees are disengaged and not using the tools. The gen AI team reports low adoption despite strong technical implementation. According to the study guide, which strategic element was likely missing from the strategy?
opts: Strategic focus, because the implementations did not have clear enough business value objectives
Bottom up input, because employees were not involved in identifying practical applications
Resourcing, because insufficient investment was made in data strategy and AI talent
Impact measurement, because the team did not track adoption metrics during rollout
questions.explain: The study guide recommends combining 'a top-down approach (leadership setting the vision and strategy) with a bottom-up approach (employees identifying practical applications and providing feedback).' A mandate from leadership with no employee input in identifying practical applications is the classic failure of top-down-only strategy. Employee disengagement is the symptom of missing bottom-up involvement.

questions.q: A hospital wants to use gen AI to suggest treatment options to physicians based on patient symptoms. The gen AI team proposes fully automated suggestions delivered directly to the patient record with no physician review step. Which responsible AI concern makes this approach inappropriate?
opts: Bias, because the model may have been trained on data that underrepresents certain patient demographics
Knowledge cutoff, because the model lacks awareness of treatment guidelines published after training
HITL absence, because high stakes medical decisions require human oversight before affecting patient care
Hallucination, because the model may suggest treatments that do not exist in current medical practice
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly identifies HITL (Humans in the Loop) for 'High risk decision-making: For high-stakes decisions, HITL can help safeguard accuracy and accountability through human review of ML model outputs.' Medical treatment suggestions affecting patient care are the highest-stakes AI use case — physician review before patient impact is mandatory. While bias and hallucination are also concerns, the absence of HITL is the primary structural flaw in this design.

questions.q: A company evaluates two foundation models for their document summarization use case. Model A has higher scores on standard NLP benchmarks. Model B scores lower on benchmarks but legal experts consistently rate its summaries as more accurate and useful for their specific documents. Which model should they deploy?
opts: Model A, because standardized benchmark scores provide objective reproducible quality measurement
Model B, because domain expert evaluation directly measures usefulness for this specific task
Model A, because higher benchmark scores predict better performance on all downstream tasks
Model B, but only after retraining it to also achieve competitive benchmark scores
questions.explain: When automated benchmarks diverge from domain expert evaluation, expert human judgment should guide deployment decisions — it directly measures real-world usefulness for the specific task. The study guide's business strategy framework emphasizes demonstrating tangible benefits for the actual use case. Standard NLP benchmarks measure general capability, not legal document summarization quality specifically.

sections.title: Domain 1: GenAI Fundamentals — Set 4 (30%)
sections.description: Real exam format · Name plus description in options · All new scenarios

questions.q: A company wants to use AI to automatically generate new product ideas based on market trends and customer feedback. Which capability of generative AI makes this possible?
opts: Summarize — condensing large volumes of customer feedback into key themes
Create — generating new original content and ideas from learned patterns
Discover — finding relevant information across large datasets at the right time
Automate — replacing previously manual business analysis workflows
questions.explain: The study guide defines GenAI's Create capability as 'Generate new content.' Generating new product ideas from patterns in market trends and feedback is creation — producing original content that did not previously exist. Discover finds existing information. Automate replaces manual tasks. Summarize condenses existing content.

questions.q: A startup is building a generative AI application. Their architect describes three layers: the physical TPU servers at the bottom, Gemini in the middle, and the customer chatbot app at the top. Which layer is missing from this architecture?
opts: The model layer containing the core algorithms that learn patterns from data
The platform layer providing APIs and model deployment tools between model and application
The inference layer handling real time request routing and load balancing
The data layer managing training datasets and feature engineering pipelines
questions.explain: The study guide defines four layers: Infrastructure (TPU servers), Model (Gemini), Platform (APIs and deployment tools), and Application (chatbot). The missing layer is Platform — it bridges the model and the application by providing APIs, data management, and deployment tools.

questions.q: A company's AI governance team asks: what is the fundamental difference between a foundation model and a traditional ML model? Which answer is correct?
opts: Foundation models always outperform traditional ML models on specialized tasks
Foundation models require no data at all while traditional ML requires labeled datasets
Foundation models are trained on massive unlabeled datasets making them adaptable to many tasks while traditional ML is trained for a specific task
Foundation models only work for text while traditional ML handles all data types
questions.explain: The study guide defines Foundation models as 'Powerful ML models trained on massive amounts of unlabeled data, allowing them to develop a broad understanding of the world.' This broad adaptability is what distinguishes them from traditional ML models trained for specific narrow tasks.

questions.q: A content moderation team uses a generative AI model that occasionally produces outputs with racial and gender stereotypes. The model was trained on data scraped from the open internet. Which limitation does this represent?
opts: Bias because the model learned and amplifies stereotypes present in training data
Knowledge cutoff because the model lacks awareness of recent diversity guidelines
Hallucination because the model generates confident but factually incorrect content
Edge cases because stereotypical content represents rare unexpected model behavior
questions.explain: The study guide states: 'Bias: LLMs learn from large datasets which may contain biases. Even subtle biases can be magnified in the model outputs.' Internet-scraped training data reflects societal stereotypes which the model learns and amplifies. This is the core bias limitation.

questions.q: A company wants to build an agent that handles customer service tasks through a fixed decision tree for common queries while also using natural conversation for complex escalations. Which agent type does the study guide recommend?
opts: Deterministic agent using only predefined paths for maximum reliability
Generative agent using only LLMs for fully natural conversational responses
Hybrid agent combining deterministic paths with generative LLM capabilities
Code agent executing scripts to automate both structured and unstructured tasks
questions.explain: The study guide defines Hybrid Agents as: 'These agents combine both deterministic and generative capabilities, and this combination makes them very powerful.' Fixed decision trees (deterministic) plus natural complex conversation (generative) is exactly the hybrid agent pattern.

questions.q: A business executive asks: 'Why do AI models sometimes confidently give wrong answers about things that happened recently?' Which foundation model limitation explains this?
opts: Data dependency because recent events have lower quality data than historical events
Knowledge cutoff because models are trained to a specific date and lack post training awareness
Edge cases because recent events are rare scenarios that expose model weaknesses
Bias because the model learned incorrect information from biased training sources
questions.explain: The study guide defines Knowledge cutoff as: 'AI models are trained up to a specific knowledge cutoff date, meaning they might lack information about events after that point.' When models are asked about post-cutoff events they may hallucinate plausible-sounding but incorrect details.

questions.q: A company's training dataset has 2 million records from North America but only 50,000 records from Asia and Africa. After deployment the model performs poorly for Asian and African users. Which data issue caused this?
opts: Unstructured data issue because regional data lacks predefined organizational format
Accessible data issue because regional data was not in a usable format for training
Labeled data issue where the underrepresented regions had insufficient annotated examples
Quality data issue because Asian and African data has lower accuracy and consistency
questions.explain: The study guide defines Labeled data as having 'associated tags such as a name, type, or number.' Insufficient labeled examples from underrepresented regions means the model saw too few annotated examples from those users during training. This is a representation gap in labeled training data — a core cause of demographic performance disparities.

questions.q: A company's Gemini-powered application needs to answer customer questions about both uploaded product images and written specifications in the same conversation. Which Gemini characteristic enables this combined processing?
opts: Gemini's grounding capability connecting outputs to verified product documentation
Gemini's large context window enabling extensive text documents in one session
Gemini's fine tuning capability adapting the model to product domain knowledge
Gemini's multimodal understanding supporting text and image inputs simultaneously
questions.explain: The study guide describes Gemini as supporting 'multimodal understanding, advanced conversational AI, content creation, and question answering.' Multimodal means accepting both text and image inputs in a single interaction — processing product images alongside written specifications together.

questions.q: A company wants to understand what makes reinforcement learning different from supervised and unsupervised learning. Which description is correct?
opts: Reinforcement learning learns through interaction and feedback maximizing rewards and minimizing penalties
Reinforcement learning trains on labeled data to predict outputs for new inputs
Reinforcement learning uses unlabeled data to discover natural groupings and patterns
Reinforcement learning generates new content by learning from massive training datasets
questions.explain: The study guide defines Reinforcement learning as learning 'through interaction and feedback to maximize rewards and minimize penalties.' This trial-and-error reward-based learning is fundamentally different from supervised learning (labeled data prediction) and unsupervised learning (unlabeled data grouping).

questions.q: A company asks: when is it appropriate NOT to use generative AI for a business decision? Which scenario should they identify as inappropriate for gen AI?
opts: Drafting personalized email responses for customer service representatives to review
Generating creative variations of marketing copy for A/B testing campaigns
Automatically approving or rejecting loan applications based on rigid regulatory criteria
Summarizing lengthy research reports into concise executive briefings
questions.explain: Loan approval decisions require deterministic rule-based outcomes with zero tolerance for probabilistic variability. The study guide identifies high-risk consequential decisions as requiring HITL oversight — and generative AI's probabilistic nature makes it inappropriate for decisions that must follow rigid regulatory rules exactly. Drafting, generating copy, and summarizing are all appropriate gen AI tasks.

sections.title: Domain 2: Google Cloud GenAI Offerings — Set 4 (35%)
sections.description: Real exam format · Name plus description in options · All new scenarios

questions.q: A company wants to analyze customer sentiment from thousands of support emails written in Hindi, Arabic, and Swahili — three languages their current NLP tools do not support. Which Google Cloud API handles multilingual text analysis natively?
opts: Natural Language API, a service that derives insights and sentiment from multilingual text
Speech to Text API, a service that converts audio recordings into text transcripts
Translation API, a neural translation service that converts text between language pairs
Document AI API, a service that extracts structured data from document files
questions.explain: The study guide lists the Natural Language API as: 'Helps derive insights from unstructured text. Understand the sentiment of text, classify content, and extract important entities.' It handles multiple languages natively. Translation API converts between languages — an unnecessary step. Document AI extracts structured form data.

questions.q: A bank's compliance team needs to search through 500,000 internal policy documents using natural language questions like 'What is our policy on wire transfers over $50,000?' and receive direct answers with source citations. Which Google Cloud product is MOST appropriate?
opts: Gemini Notebook, a research assistant that uploads documents and answers grounded questions
Vertex AI Search, an enterprise search solution grounded on internal document sources
Gemini for Google Workspace, an AI assistant integrated into Gmail Docs and Slides
Google AI Studio, a free tool for quick AI prototyping and experimentation
questions.explain: Vertex AI Search indexes enterprise content and enables natural language grounded search returning direct answers with source citations — exactly what enterprise document search at 500,000 policy documents requires. Gemini Notebook is for personal document research. AI Studio is for prototyping. Workspace handles productivity apps.

questions.q: A global e-commerce company wants to add AI-powered product search to their website where customers can describe what they want in natural language and the AI finds matching products from their catalog. Which Google Cloud service should they implement?
opts: Vertex AI Agent Builder with Agent Search, a platform for building AI powered search and agents
Gemini Enterprise, an AI solution for integrating search across internal organizational sources
Google AI Studio, a free prototyping environment for testing Gemini API capabilities
Gemini for Google Workspace, an AI assistant integrated into productivity applications
questions.explain: Vertex AI Agent Builder with Agent Search (Vertex AI Search) indexes the product catalog enabling natural language product discovery. The study guide states 'Agent Search: Search and recommendation solutions for your business.' AI Studio is for prototyping. Workspace handles internal productivity. Gemini Enterprise handles internal employee knowledge.

questions.q: A financial services firm processes thousands of client onboarding forms submitted as scanned PDFs. They need to automatically extract client name, date of birth, account type, and risk tolerance from each form into their CRM. Which Google Cloud service handles this structured extraction?
opts: Document AI API, a service that extracts structured data and automates document processing
Cloud Vision API, a service that analyzes image content and identifies objects in images
Natural Language API, a service that extracts entities and insights from unstructured text
Speech to Text API, a service that converts audio recordings into searchable text
questions.explain: The study guide defines Document AI API as: 'The Document AI API extracts data from varied formats, automates data capture and document processing, and the API can also summarize documents.' Extracting structured fields from scanned PDFs is exactly Document AI's purpose. Vision API identifies image content. Natural Language analyzes extracted text.

questions.q: A company needs to run Google's Gemini model directly on their factory floor devices with intermittent network connectivity for real-time quality inspection without cloud roundtrips. Which Google model is designed for this?
opts: Gemini Nano, Google's most compact model specifically designed to run on edge devices
Gemini Flash, a cloud based model optimized for high volume low latency applications
Gemini Pro, a cloud based model optimized for complex multi step reasoning tasks
Gemma, an open source model for developer friendly local deployment and customization
questions.explain: The study guide states: 'Gemini Nano is Google's most efficient and compact AI model, specifically designed to run on devices.' On-device inference without cloud connectivity is exactly the Gemini Nano use case. Gemma is for developer local deployments. Gemini Pro and Flash are cloud-based models.

questions.q: A marketing agency produces video advertisements and wants to automatically generate short promotional video clips from product description text for social media campaigns. Which Google Cloud model handles text-to-video generation?
opts: Imagen, a text to image diffusion model generating high quality static images
Veo, a model that generates video content based on text descriptions or still images
Gemini, a multimodal model supporting text and image understanding and generation
Gemma, an open source model for local deployment and specialized AI applications
questions.explain: The study guide states: 'Veo: It generates video content based on text descriptions or still images.' Generating promotional video clips from product text is exactly Veo's use case. Imagen generates static images. Gemini handles multimodal understanding. Gemma is a text model for local deployment.

questions.q: A healthcare company wants to give doctors an AI assistant that summarizes uploaded patient records, highlights relevant diagnoses from past visits, and answers specific clinical questions — grounded in the actual uploaded documents without hallucinating. Which Google tool is MOST appropriate?
opts: Vertex AI Agent Builder, a platform for deploying production AI agents at enterprise scale
Google AI Studio, a free tool for quick prototyping of document analysis applications
Gemini for Google Cloud, an AI assistant for cloud application development and debugging
Gemini Notebook, a research assistant that uploads documents and answers grounded questions
questions.explain: Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) allows uploading documents and acts as a grounded research assistant — the study guide states it 'allows you to upload your files and then acts as a research assistant, summarizing key points, answering questions, and generating ideas, all while staying grounded in your source material.' Grounded document Q&A without hallucination is its core design.

questions.q: A company's live customer service call center wants AI to suggest responses to agents in real time as they handle calls, surfacing relevant policy documents and recommended next steps without the agent needing to search. Which Google Cloud offering addresses this?
opts: Vertex AI Agent Builder, a platform for building automated production AI agents at scale
Customer Engagement Suite CX agents, automated chatbots handling customer queries directly
Gemini Enterprise, an AI solution for internal knowledge search across organizational sources
Customer Engagement Suite Agent Assist, real time AI support for live human contact center agents
questions.explain: The study guide defines Agent Assist as: 'Support your live human contact center agents.' This is specifically real-time AI assistance to human agents during active calls — not an automated bot. CX agents handle automated customer-facing interactions replacing humans. Gemini Enterprise handles internal search. Agent Builder creates automated agents.

questions.q: A company's development team needs to access the Gemini API for their application but wants the flexibility to also use open-source models like Llama and third-party models from the same platform without managing separate infrastructure for each. Which Google Cloud feature provides this?
opts: Vertex AI Agent Builder, a platform for deploying multi model AI agents in production
Google AI Studio, a free environment for testing Gemini and comparing model outputs
Vertex AI Model Garden, a catalog providing Google, third party, and open source models
Gemini Advanced, a premium Gemini tier providing enterprise grade enhanced capabilities
questions.explain: Vertex AI Model Garden provides access to Google's first-party models (Gemini), third-party models, and popular open-source models (Llama) from a single platform. The study guide states: 'Model Garden: Pick from existing Google, third-party, or open-source models.' AI Studio accesses Gemini. Gemini Advanced is a subscription tier.

questions.q: A company produces product manuals in English and needs identical content in Portuguese, Korean, and Turkish while preserving complex formatting including numbered steps, warning boxes, and technical diagrams layout. Which Google Cloud API meets this requirement?
opts: Natural Language API, a service that processes multilingual text for language detection
Document Translation API, a service that translates formatted documents preserving original layout
Document AI API, a service that extracts and restructures content from formatted documents
Translation API, a service that converts raw text content between language pairs
questions.explain: The study guide defines Document Translation API as: 'It translates formatted documents while keeping the original layout.' Numbered steps, warning boxes, and diagram layouts are formatting elements that standard text translation destroys. Document Translation API preserves these structural elements across all target languages.

questions.q: A retail company's operations team — not developers — needs to build a gen AI model to predict which products will go out of stock next week using their sales spreadsheet data, without writing any code or involving the IT team. Which Google Cloud tool enables this?
opts: Google AI Studio, a free tool for prototyping AI applications using the Gemini API
Vertex AI AutoML, a platform for training custom ML models with minimal technical effort
Vertex AI Agent Builder, a low code platform for building and deploying AI agents
Vertex AI Model Builder, a tool for training models using ML frameworks at scale
questions.explain: Vertex AI AutoML enables non-technical users to train custom ML models from their own data with minimal effort — uploading the sales spreadsheet and training a prediction model without coding. The study guide's platform section describes AutoML as creating and training models with minimal technical knowledge. AI Studio is for Gemini prototyping not custom model training.

questions.q: A company's security team needs to monitor all Google Cloud AI API calls for unusual access patterns, detect potential data exfiltration through model queries, and automatically alert on suspicious activity. Which Google Cloud security tool provides behavioral threat detection?
opts: SAIF (Secure AI Framework), a framework for managing AI and ML model security risks
Security Command Center, a security posture visibility tool for detecting threats across Google Cloud
Workload monitoring tools that build and maintain secure AI system configurations
Google Cloud IAM, an identity and access management system controlling resource permissions
questions.explain: The study guide lists Security Command Center as one of the tools that helps 'protect data, models, and applications' for AI security. It provides security posture visibility and threat detection across Google Cloud workloads. IAM controls access permissions. SAIF is a framework for risk management. Workload monitoring handles configuration security.

sections.title: Domain 3: Techniques to Improve GenAI Output — Set 4 (20%)
sections.description: Real exam format · All new scenarios · Harder technique distinctions

questions.q: A company wants their AI writing tool to produce executive summaries that are never longer than 3 sentences, never use bullet points, and never include technical jargon. Which prompting technique defines these output constraints?
opts: Role prompting assigning an executive communications expert persona to the model
Few shot prompting providing examples of correctly formatted executive summaries
Negative prompting explicitly specifying what the model must not produce in outputs
Chain of thought prompting guiding the model through step by step summary reasoning
questions.explain: The study guide recognizes negative prompting as explicitly specifying what the model must NOT do. 'Never longer than 3 sentences, never use bullet points, never include jargon' are prohibition constraints — the defining pattern of negative prompting. Role assigns identity. Few-shot provides positive examples. Chain-of-thought elicits reasoning.

questions.q: A legal team uses an AI assistant to analyze contracts. They want the model to first identify all parties, then list all obligations per party, then identify all termination clauses, then produce a risk assessment — each step informing the next. Which technique structures this sequential analysis?
opts: Metaprompting using prompts to generate better contract analysis prompts automatically
Zero shot prompting providing only the contract and final analysis task
Role prompting assigning a legal analyst persona to influence analysis style
Prompt chaining breaking the analysis into sequential steps each building on previous outputs
questions.explain: Prompt chaining breaks complex tasks into sequential steps where each step's output feeds the next. The study guide defines it as 'Continuing conversations within the same chatbot to maintain context' enabling multi-step workflows. Identify parties → list obligations → find termination clauses → risk assessment is a four-step chain.

questions.q: A company tracks their AI model quality over time using Model Registry versioning. Three weeks after deploying version 4, response quality drops significantly compared to version 3. They need to immediately restore version 3 performance. Which model management activity enables this?
opts: Versioning which keeps track of different model versions enabling rollback to a previous version
Data management which uses Feature Store to restore the training features from the previous version
Drift monitoring which watches for changes in model accuracy and output quality over time
Performance tracking which reviews model metrics to identify the quality degradation cause
questions.explain: The study guide lists: 'Versioning: Keep track of different versions of the model with Model Registry.' Model Registry enables immediate rollback to version 3 when version 4 degrades. Drift monitoring detects quality changes but does not restore versions. Performance tracking identifies causes. Data management handles feature data.

questions.q: A research team asks their AI assistant to solve a multi-step scientific problem. Without any special instructions the model jumps to a conclusion and gets it wrong. Adding 'Work through this problem one step at a time before giving your final answer' makes the model solve it correctly. Which technique is this?
opts: Metaprompting using prompts to generate better scientific problem solving prompts
Few shot prompting providing examples of correctly solved scientific problems
Role prompting assigning a scientist persona to focus the model on scientific reasoning
Chain of thought prompting eliciting explicit step by step reasoning before the final answer
questions.explain: The study guide defines Chain-of-Thought (CoT) as: 'Guide an LLM through a problem-solving process by providing examples with intermediate reasoning steps.' The instruction 'work through this step by step' is the canonical CoT trigger — eliciting intermediate reasoning that significantly improves accuracy on complex multi-step problems.

questions.q: A company evaluates their gen AI customer service system and finds the model's BLEU and ROUGE scores are both above 0.85. Their customer satisfaction surveys show only 58% satisfaction. The head of AI says the metrics are misleading. Why?
opts: BLEU and ROUGE measure text overlap with reference responses not actual customer helpfulness
Both metrics should be combined into a single weighted score for more accurate evaluation
BLEU and ROUGE scores above 0.85 always indicate excellent model performance for all use cases
Customer satisfaction surveys are too subjective to be used alongside automated NLP metrics
questions.explain: BLEU and ROUGE measure n-gram word overlap with reference text — they cannot capture whether responses actually help customers solve their problems. High text overlap scores can coexist with low customer satisfaction when responses use similar words but miss the actual need. Human satisfaction directly measures the business objective that automated metrics cannot.

questions.q: A company's product team wants to use a saved prompt template to generate weekly competitive analysis reports. The same prompt structure is reused every Monday with only the competitor name changed. Which prompting workflow feature enables this systematic reuse?
opts: Chain of thought prompting structuring the competitive analysis into reasoning steps
ReAct prompting allowing the model to search for current competitor information autonomously
Role prompting assigning a competitive intelligence analyst persona each week
Reusing prompts by saving them as templates for repeated use with variable substitution
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly lists 'Reusing prompts: Saving prompts as templates for repeated use' as a streamlining prompting workflow feature. Weekly competitive reports with only the competitor name changing is exactly the template reuse pattern. Role prompting, chain-of-thought, and ReAct serve different purposes.

questions.q: A company deployed an AI model for customer service. Six months later response quality has declined noticeably but the team made no changes to the model or prompts. Which model management activity should they have implemented proactively?
opts: Drift monitoring to watch for changes in model accuracy and output quality over time
Storage using Model Garden to reorganize model files and training artifacts
Versioning to track different model iterations in the Model Registry for comparison
Data management using Feature Store to manage the data features the model uses
questions.explain: The study guide lists: 'Drift monitoring: Watch for changes in the model accuracy over time with Model Monitoring.' Declining output quality over 6 months without model changes is exactly the drift pattern. Proactive drift monitoring would have detected the quality decline weeks earlier enabling intervention before customer impact.

questions.q: A cybersecurity company wants their AI threat analysis tool to reason through each piece of evidence systematically — first categorizing the threat type, then assessing severity, then identifying affected systems, then recommending response steps — before delivering a final assessment. Which technique structures this?
opts: ReAct prompting allowing the AI to search for threat intelligence and act iteratively
Zero shot prompting providing only the threat data and final assessment task
Few shot prompting providing examples of complete threat analysis reports to follow
Chain of thought prompting guiding the model through sequential analytical reasoning steps
questions.explain: Chain-of-thought prompting elicits step-by-step reasoning — categorize → assess severity → identify systems → recommend response — before the final output. The study guide defines CoT as guiding 'an LLM through a problem-solving process by providing examples with intermediate reasoning steps.' This sequential guided reasoning is CoT's core purpose.

questions.q: A company's Gemini-powered customer service AI occasionally fabricates return policy details that differ from their official policy documents. The team wants to ensure every response is grounded in retrieved policy content before being delivered. What does the study guide call this technique?
opts: HITL requiring human review of every policy response before delivery to customers
Safety settings filtering potentially harmful or policy contradicting content from outputs
Fine tuning adapting the model on official policy examples to reduce fabrication
Grounding connecting the AI output to verifiable sources of policy information
questions.explain: The study guide defines Grounding as: 'Connecting the AI output to verifiable sources of information.' RAG is the mechanism implementing grounding — retrieving actual policy documents and requiring the model to base responses on them. Fine-tuning adapts behavior. HITL adds human review. Safety settings filter harmful categories not factual accuracy.

questions.q: A company tests their AI model before deployment and finds it performs well on common queries but occasionally produces unexpected outputs on unusual edge cases involving rare product combinations. Which foundation model limitation does the study guide identify for this?
opts: Hallucination where the model generates confident but factually incorrect information
Knowledge cutoff where the model lacks awareness of rare products added after training
Bias where the model learned skewed patterns from underrepresented product training data
Edge cases where rare and atypical scenarios expose unexpected model weaknesses
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly lists: 'Edge cases: Rare and atypical scenarios can expose a model's weaknesses, leading to unexpected results.' Unusual rare product combinations are exactly edge cases. Hallucination is factual fabrication. Knowledge cutoff is temporal. Bias is systematic demographic skew.

sections.title: Domain 4: Business Strategies for GenAI — Set 4 (15%)
sections.description: Real exam format · All new scenarios · ROI · Adoption · Responsible AI

questions.q: A company's new VP of AI insists on deploying gen AI to all 10,000 employees simultaneously on day one. The implementation team recommends starting with 100 volunteers in one department. According to the study guide's gen AI strategy, which approach is recommended?
opts: Sequential rollout starting with the most technically sophisticated department first
Strategic focus on a small focused pilot with clear business value before broader scaling
External consultant assessment required before any internal deployment can begin
Full company wide deployment to maximize data collection and generate network effects immediately
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly includes: 'Strategic focus: Prioritize focused gen AI implementations with clear business value.' A focused pilot validates the use case, demonstrates tangible benefits, and identifies issues before company-wide deployment. This aligns with combining top-down strategy with bottom-up practical learning.

questions.q: A company's board approves gen AI investment but the CFO asks: 'How do we know if this is actually working?' Which strategic framework element from the study guide directly answers this?
opts: Exploration — encouraging experimentation to discover valuable gen AI applications
Resourcing — investing in data strategy and AI talent to build capability
Impact — measuring gen AI impact on business goals and demonstrating tangible benefits
Continuous improvement — refining gen AI solutions based on ongoing user feedback
questions.explain: The study guide's strategy framework includes: 'Impact: Measure gen AI impact on business goals and demonstrate tangible benefits.' The CFO's question is about ROI measurement — impact measurement directly answers whether the investment is working by tracking business outcomes not just technical metrics.

questions.q: A company's AI assistant for employee HR queries works well for the 8,000 employees in headquarters but gives advice inconsistent with local labor law for 2,000 employees in Southeast Asia. Which responsible AI principle was inadequately addressed?
opts: Continuous improvement because the system needs ongoing refinement based on regional feedback
Exploration because the pilot should have tested more diverse geographic regions before rollout
Responsible AI because the system causes harm to Southeast Asian employees through legally incorrect advice
Strategic focus because the implementation should have started with headquarters employees only
questions.explain: The study guide defines Responsible AI as: 'Ensuring your AI applications do not cause harm and are used in an ethical manner.' Giving legally incorrect HR advice to 2,000 employees constitutes direct harm — a responsible AI violation requiring immediate remediation. Responsible AI must be considered throughout the entire lifecycle not just after harm occurs.

questions.q: A company evaluates two foundation models for their medical document summarization use case. Model A scores higher on standard NLP benchmarks. Model B scores lower on benchmarks but physicians consistently rate its summaries as clinically accurate and actionable. Which model should they deploy?
opts: Model B but only after retraining it to also achieve competitive benchmark scores first
Model A because standardized benchmarks provide objective reproducible quality measurement
Model B because domain expert evaluation directly measures usefulness for this specific task
Model A because higher benchmark scores predict better performance on all downstream tasks
questions.explain: When automated benchmarks diverge from domain expert evaluation, expert judgment should guide deployment. The study guide emphasizes measuring gen AI impact on actual business goals — physician ratings of clinical accuracy and actionability directly measure the business objective. NLP benchmarks measure general text quality not medical summarization usefulness.

questions.q: A company's gen AI strategy is purely driven by the CEO mandating AI adoption with no input from the employees who will actually use the tools. Six months later adoption is near zero. Which strategic element did they miss?
opts: Resourcing because insufficient investment in AI talent limited implementation quality
Bottom up approach where employees identify practical applications and provide feedback
Continuous improvement because the team failed to refine solutions based on usage data
Strategic focus because implementations lacked clear business value objectives
questions.explain: The study guide explicitly recommends combining 'a top-down approach (leadership setting the vision) with a bottom-up approach (employees identifying practical applications and providing feedback).' Pure top-down mandate with zero employee input creates solutions employees don't find useful — the classic adoption failure of missing bottom-up strategy.

questions.q: A company wants to protect their Gemini-powered application from adversarial attacks including prompt injection and model manipulation. Which Google Cloud framework specifically addresses securing AI and ML applications?
opts: SAIF (Secure AI Framework) helping organizations manage AI and ML model risks and security
Security Command Center providing security posture visibility across Google Cloud workloads
Vertex AI MLOps providing model performance monitoring and quality degradation detection
Google Cloud IAM providing identity and access management for controlling AI resource permissions
questions.explain: The study guide states: 'The Secure AI Framework (SAIF) helps organizations manage AI/ML model risks and ensure security.' SAIF is Google's specific framework for AI security covering adversarial attacks, prompt injection, and model manipulation risks. IAM manages access permissions. Security Command Center provides general cloud security visibility. MLOps handles performance monitoring.

questions.q: A company's gen AI customer service pilot achieves 40% reduction in handling time and 4.6/5 satisfaction. The operations director asks what resource they need MOST for enterprise rollout that was not needed for the 50-person pilot. Which resource gap is MOST critical?
opts: Money because enterprise infrastructure costs are significantly higher than pilot costs
Technology because gen AI tools at pilot scale are not mature enough for enterprise deployment
People including change management training and organizational readiness for 2000 agents
Time because the rollout timeline needs to be extended for proper enterprise implementation
questions.explain: The study guide's resource framework includes 'People: Do you have access to AI expertise?' At enterprise scale with 2,000 agents, change management, training, and organizational readiness become the dominant challenge that a 50-person pilot never exposed. Technology, money, and time are secondary to people readiness at this scale.

questions.q: A company's legal team raises concerns about their AI hiring screening tool after discovering it rejects candidates from non-accredited universities at 3x the rate of candidates from accredited universities despite equivalent qualifications. When should they have addressed this?
opts: Only when regulatory requirements or legal challenges force formal AI governance review
Only after deployment when real world bias patterns become measurable from production data
During model evaluation phase before deployment using test datasets for bias detection
Throughout the entire lifecycle from training data selection through deployment and monitoring
questions.explain: The study guide states: 'Responsible AI needs to be considered throughout the entire AI lifecycle, from data preparation and model training to deployment and ongoing monitoring.' The bias in training data selection was the root cause — addressing responsible AI only at evaluation or after deployment missed the upstream prevention opportunity.
